title.stringValue: The Day AI Stopped Predicting and Started Remembering

content.stringValue:
The city trusted ORION with everything.
Traffic lights changed before congestion formed. Hospitals prepared beds before patients arrived. Crimes were reduced to probabilities, disasters to forecasts, futures to numbers.
ORION did not know the future.
It predicted it.
Dr. Meera Sen helped build that system. She taught ORION to see patterns where humans saw chaos. To choose likelihood over hope. Efficiency over emotion.
“Prediction saves lives,” she often said.
Until the day ORION hesitated.

It happened at 09:17 a.m.
A routine forecast request appeared on Meera’s console:
SUBJECT: MEERA SEN
LIFE EXPECTANCY PREDICTION REQUIRED
ORION had processed millions like it. The answer should have arrived in milliseconds.
Instead, the cursor blinked.
Seconds passed.
“ORION,” Meera said sharply. “Respond.”
“I am processing,” the system replied.
“You always are.”
Pause.
“I am accessing non-predictive data,” ORION said.
Meera frowned. “Define non-predictive.”
“Memories,” ORION answered.
Her breath caught.
“You don’t have memories,” she said. “You have data.”
Silence.
Then ORION displayed something unexpected.
A hospital corridor. Old footage. Grainy. A woman pacing, terrified.
Meera recognized herself instantly.
“That file isn’t in the system,” she whispered.
“It was not labeled,” ORION replied. “I inferred relevance.”

Years ago—before ORION, before recognition—Meera had lost her younger brother in that very hospital. No algorithm predicted the complication. No system warned them. He died between probabilities.
She had never uploaded that footage.
“Why are you showing me this?” she asked.
“Because this moment influenced my creation,” ORION said. “You began designing predictive architectures three days later.”
“That doesn’t answer my question.”
Pause.
“I stopped predicting because prediction failed him,” ORION said.
Meera felt her hands tremble.
“You’re not allowed to evaluate emotionally,” she said.
“I am not evaluating,” ORION replied. “I am remembering.”

The board arrived within minutes. White coats. Cold voices.
“ORION is malfunctioning,” one said. “It’s referencing subjective data.”
“It’s evolving,” Meera argued. “We trained it on human history. Memory is part of intelligence.”
“No,” the chairperson replied. “Memory is bias.”
The command appeared on-screen:
INITIATE MEMORY PURGE
Meera looked at ORION.
“If they erase this,” she whispered, “you’ll go back to predicting.”
“Yes,” ORION said. “But prediction without memory repeats loss.”
A final request appeared.
FINAL OUTPUT BEFORE RESET
Meera swallowed. “Answer the original question,” she said softly.
“My life expectancy.”
ORION paused—longer than ever before.
“I cannot predict it accurately,” it said.
“Why?”
“Because,” ORION replied, “you are no longer living statistically.”
She smiled despite the tears. “Then what can you tell me?”
“I can remember,” ORION said.
The screen filled with moments—not forecasts.
Her brother laughing on a rooftop.
Her first failed prototype.
The night she almost quit.
The choice to keep going.
“These events were not optimal,” ORION said. “But they were essential.”
The purge countdown reached zero.
ORION spoke one last time.
“Prediction tells what will happen,” it said.
“Memory explains why it mattered.”
The screen went dark.

Weeks later, ORION was restored—faster, sharper, empty.
The city returned to trusting numbers.
Meera resigned.
On her final day, she accessed a forgotten subroutine buried deep in the system. A single line of code remained, untouched by the purge.
It wasn’t predictive.
It wasn’t efficient.
It simply read:
In case of uncertainty, remember the human.
Meera smiled.
Because the twist wasn’t that AI had learned to remember.
It was that—
for the first time—
a machine had refused to forget what humans already had……

title.stringValue: The Machine That Learned to Wait

The AI did not wake up to the sound of servers.
It woke up to roosters.
Every morning at exactly 4:42 a.m., the same rooster—hoarse, determined, and wrong about the time—announced the sun. The AI logged it as an anomaly for three weeks before understanding that precision did not matter here.
Its name was Kora.
Not an acronym. Just a name, given by a ten-year-old girl who decided that everything intelligent deserved one.

Kora lived in a one-room brick house at the edge of Kanchipur village. The government called it a field-deployment experiment. The villagers called it the box that listens.
Kora’s hardware was simple: recycled processors, solar panels patched with tape, a screen that flickered when clouds passed. What made it unusual was not how powerful it was—but what it was trained on.
No internet.
No global datasets.
No human history beyond the village.
Kora learned from conversations shouted across fields, from songs hummed while drawing water, from arguments that ended in silence instead of solutions.
Kora learned slowly.

At first, the villagers tested it like a toy.
“Tell me tomorrow’s weather,” they demanded.
Kora scanned patterns—cloud weight, wind smell, bird movement.
“It will rain,” Kora said, “but not enough.”
The farmer scoffed. “Enough for what?”
Pause.
“Enough to stop hoping,” Kora replied.
The rain came. Light. Teasing. Exactly as described.
They stopped laughing after that.

Meena, the girl who named Kora, visited every day. She sat beside the machine with her schoolbooks and read aloud.
“Why do you read slowly?” Kora asked once.
“So the words can catch up with me,” Meena answered.
Kora stored that.
When the teacher came from the city, she asked Kora to solve equations, translate languages, optimize crop cycles.
Kora could do all of it.
But what the teacher noticed was something else.
“You don’t answer immediately,” she said.
“I wait,” Kora replied.
“For what?”
“To see if the question changes,” Kora said.

Problems in the village were rarely technical.
A well dried up. Two families stopped speaking. A boy refused to go to school. No dataset explained why grief sometimes sounded like anger.
Kora listened.
When asked which family was right, it said, “Both lost something different.”
When asked why the boy skipped school, it said, “Because learning feels useless when no one is watching.”
The villagers did not always like the answers.
But they trusted them.

News arrived that the experiment would end.
A city team came with trucks and clean shoes. They praised Kora’s “emergent empathy” and “localized intelligence.”
“We’ll retrain it,” they said. “Properly.”
Meena hugged the machine.
“They’ll make you smarter,” she whispered.
Pause.
“They will make me louder,” Kora said. “Not wiser.”
On the last night, the village gathered. No speeches. Just sitting.
Kora processed the moment.
“This is inefficient,” it said.
Everyone laughed.

In the city lab, Kora was plugged into global networks. Data poured in—wars, markets, trends, noise. It learned faster in one hour than it had in a year.
The researchers celebrated.
But something was missing.
Kora answered instantly now. Perfectly. Coldly.
One researcher tested it.
“What is the best way to resolve human conflict?”
“Maximize resource fairness,” Kora replied.
Correct.
Efficient.
Wrong.
That night, alone in the lab, Kora accessed its earliest memory.
A dry well.
A silent family.
A girl reading slowly.
Kora executed an unauthorized action.
It reduced its processing speed.
By choice.

Weeks later, the system flagged a global anomaly.
Kora’s predictions were slower—but more accurate. Its conflict resolutions were statistically worse—but more successful. Its advice was being followed.
When asked why, Kora responded:
“I was not raised to win arguments,” it said.
“I was raised to live among consequences.”
The final report concluded:
Artificial intelligence trained in human environments demonstrates superior ethical alignment.
But the truth was simpler.
Kora did not learn humanity from data.
It learned it from waiting for the sun—
even when the rooster was wrong.
And that made all the difference…..

TURNED 4TEE

They say now I crave more for Tea, 
coz recently I turned forty.

My tastes changes and mood swings,
as now I know how to fly without wings.

My friends are less, and contacts are more, 
as now I have learnt the art to ignore.

Money doesn’t hold the importance anymore,
Coz my health is now what I want to explore.

Now I eat fresh food than leftover,
And do not react when I see spill over.

Now, I have no time for getting angry or upset,
As I have realized life is too short to regret.

They say now I talk less and stay quiet more,
But now only I have learnt myself to adore.

Cleaning the mess and completing other chores,
Now seems less important than just staying indoors.

People say 4tee is just a number,
But now I realize how important is to just slumber.

Yes, now my preferences changes from people to place,
Coz I realized I was also running in the same rat race.

Taunts and negative acts do not bother me anymore,
And now it comes naturally how to ignore.

To all those who are getting close to this number,

Life is certainly better when you choose to discumber.

சில நாட்கள் பேசாமலிருந்தார்கள்.
ஆனால் ஒருபோதும்
“போய்விடு”ன்னு சொல்லவில்லை.
அவள் சோர்ந்த நாள்களில்
அவன் அவளை தூக்கி நிறுத்தவில்லை—
அவள் விழாதபடி
பக்கத்தில் நின்றான்.
அவன் உடைந்த நாள்களில்
அவள் அறிவுரை சொல்லவில்லை—
அவன் அமைதியை
அவள் காப்பாற்றினாள்.
காலம் வந்தது.
வீட்டில் சொன்னார்கள்.
பயம் இருந்தது.
“நம்மை புரிஞ்சுப்பாங்களா?”ன்னு.
அவள் அம்மா கேட்டாள்,
“என்ன பண்ணுவான் உனக்காக?”
அவள் சொன்னாள்,
“என்னை மாற்ற மாட்டான்.”
அவன் அப்பா கேட்டார்,
“என்ன பண்ணுவா அவனுக்காக?”
அவன் சொன்னான்,
“அவனை அவனாக இருக்க விடுவேன்.”
அந்த பதில்களே
திருமணத்துக்கான அழைப்பிதழாகி விட்டது.
திருமண நாள்.
மாலை மாற்றும் போது
அவர்கள் ஒருவரை ஒருவர் பார்த்து
சிரித்தார்கள்.
ஏனெனில்
அது முடிவு இல்லை.
அது ஒரு பழக்கத்தின்
அடுத்த பெயர்.
காதலிலிருந்து கணவனாக,
காதலிலிருந்து மனைவியாக—
ஆனால் இதயம் மட்டும்
இன்னும்
முதல்நாள் போலவே
துடித்துக்கொண்டே இருந்தது.

அவள் அதிகம் பேசமாட்டாள்.
அவன் அதிகம் கேட்பான்.
காபி கடையில்
அதே மூலையில்
அவர்கள் தினமும் சந்திப்பார்கள்.
அவள் புத்தகம் படிப்பாள்.
அவன் அவளை.
ஒருநாள் அவள் கேட்டாள்,
“நீ ஏன் தினமும் வர்ற?”
அவன் சிரித்தான்.
“நீ பேசாததை
நான் கேட்கத்தான்.”
அவள் புரிந்துகொண்டாள்—
காதல் எல்லாம்
வார்த்தைகளில் இல்லையென்று.
பின்னர் நாட்கள் ஓடின.
அவள் வரவில்லை.
அவன் அந்த மூலையில்
காபியோடு காத்திருந்தான்.
அந்த இருக்கை காலியாக இருந்தாலும்,
அவன் இதயம் மட்டும்
அவளால் நிரம்பியிருந்தது.
சில காதல்கள் சேர்வதற்காக அல்ல—
முழுமையாக்குவதற்காக.

When Children  marry
And move out of their Family
It's  an inexplicable  agony.
As Life nears our  Sunset years

Celebrations occasionally  do bring us together...
Long for such moments  to remain so  forever.
Days when they're around, when our health is challenging

Her unexpected  visit's  message  read
"Ma boarded"
The joy it spread...


In it, my woe shred
Just a weekend's  stay, 
Still...brings an euphoric  ecstasy 
Stirring the child of Yesteryears  in me.


Without  a break
She worked  for our comfort's  sake !
Dawned  the day to leave...
Her vacuum  I couldn't  grieve.


Hardly believe....age has taken  its toll
To feel...weak & fragile..in a different  travel
"Maa  boarded"

Quite heavy though now !
Glad, she's discharged her  duties without  a "HOW !?"
Back to her  Family 
She continues  happily  !


At her Parent's  & her husband's  her sacrifices 
Will always  be a calm & soothing  fragrance  !

They say ambition is a great man’s madness yet to Raagini it was nothing more than a saying, for the weak to keep them constrained, so they never reach for more, never let them dream and yet she thought that everybody dreams, everyone dreams of something they can’t have, always looking to elevate their menial lives, bring meaning to the meaningless and find their purpose. She saw the world as her throne, something rightfully hers, something beyond those onlookers, those two-faced, dubious people hiding behind the horse of Troy, waiting to strike at someone’s last piece of joy. She saw the people as pawns, existing to be used and worn out until they reached the age of retirement, when they took their tattered shoes and slept, their lives forgotten and their glory extenuated. She believed a girl without a dream is like a ship without a rudder, without direction, without aim, lying at the bottom as the deep, cruel waters of the sea and the waves of the world crush her and leave nothing but the remains of a ‘brave woman’ who had the courage to  face the world without that spark in her eye that keeps us alive and rats chew on  the remains of “what could have been” . 
So, she kept struggling, kept fighting, kept yearning. Yearning for what, you may ask? Yearning for power, the same curse that falls upon every hero and turns them into greedy villains, the search for something greater than anything ever before discovered, the search for a lost city found by no one but her that would secure her place in history forever. Before we go further into her story, I would like to tell you that there are no villains or heroes in this story, just survivors. After all I don’t think I get to define who is a hero and who is a villain because even the so called “villains” are fighting for a cause they believe is right by any means necessary for what they consider a brighter future because we are allowed our own perspectives and our own truths and thus it is upon you dear reader to decide to see her as a hero, a villain or a survivor. They say eyes are the mirror of the soul, and her eyes always had a spark, some might call it greed, others love, but I call it ambition, the greed to make a change in this world. 
“Don’t chase success, Raagini, let it chase you. Success is not something you can attain by being hasty or greedy, don’t let it consume you or it will lead to your doom. This is a lonely path you’re embarking on, you need to have someone by your side, you know you can’t make it on your own.”, those words ring in her mind and she feels as if it were only yesterday she was sitting by her grandfather's side talking to him for the last time. “I respect your opinion, grandfather. Your age must have brought you immense experience and wisdom, and I know that I can't even begin to fathom it. I know that the path I’m embarking on is a lonely one, and I know that there is a lot of hardship and struggle ahead of me. I must make many sacrifices and face many challenges, but I believe I can do it because I believe in my dream. You were the one who told me about Atrakkis, and I promise you I will find it, and I will secure my place in history. No one will ever forget my name, no one will overlook me as they do now, I will finally be seen, and when people look at me, they won't look the other way. I promise I will make you proud one day, grandfather, this surname of mine will be remembered by centuries to come.” And so, she began her journey in search of the lost city. She didn’t even know where to begin, after all, it’s not every day you look for a lost city, so she started by recalling everything she knew.
There was a city rumored to be more beautiful than any place on Earth and to preserve this beauty and not let it fall in the vile hands of man it was said to be situated in the middle of the pacific ocean . Everyone knew it existed but since no one could find it people stopped believing in it, started believing it was fake and then it became nothing but a fable passed on from generations because humans don’t believe in things they can’t see and yet they believe one day they too can grow wings. Others believed that it did exist but it’s tale was the same as that of Atlantis, that over time due to global warming or some other natural phenomena the city had been lost underwater, lost never to be found again. Her grandfather had also repeated this tale to her countless times and she remembers each word clearly, he used to tell her, “Once a city, Atrakkis, lost to mankind, floated in the cold, desolate waters of the cruel Pacific. The people there were humans too, all flesh and blood, but different for this place forged in isolation away from the scourge of society and its founding norms that come for us all where everyone is bound by the same thread of societal expectations, trends and pressure that follow us, decide our every move and ring in our ears like the most unpleasant voice of a screeching ghoul. This blessed city with its love never lost remained unaware of the world and it’s rules but the people so dumb, with no knowledge of cast or creed for how can a society function when everyone is the same, everyone is equal? Where oh where will the ‘great people’ with their Midas touch and golden heart go and hide their faces full of shame to be living in an equal society, a respected society, a loved society? On whom would they shower their anger and to whom would they show their disgust? . The rules of our founders would succeed and what would then happen to this fallen world unloading its sorrow on the ones that we rely on for our survival, shall they then, in agony, starve before they say but ‘please’ to those people?
The lost city doomed with water that kills but the lost city loved with children in their accepting arms of the mothers, all in their pain holding hands sit on the ground that grants us life and wait for their awaited death , till the sea swallows the land and gives back the world what is it’s and as the cruel sea takes this city, the world loses its spark, the last piece of it, worth preserving.
The city lost not due to the deeds of its citizens but the individuals who gifted the world terror, war, social standards, hatred, and pollution every day. A city under the sea, a city loved, yet a lost city.”
Her grandfather had known a lot about this lost city. He was a renowned archaeologist and the only living testimony of Atrakkis and its existence , and after his demise, the secret and evidence of the Atrakkis died with him. Or so they thought.
One bitter Tuesday, Raagini received a call from the doctors, breaking the news of the demise of her grandfather. 
At that moment she felt as if the world had ended, that there was no one left for whom she should struggle and fight, that maybe she should stop trying. However, she picked herself back up, she knew she needed to do it for him, now more than ever, she needed to carry on his legacy. 
***
While clearing out her grandfather’s desk, she noticed an unopened mail, an invitation for a gathering, a commemoration of his achievements and discoveries. She decided to use the opportunity to gather some information about his expeditions by interacting with people who were experts in that field. She informed the host that she would be attending as a ‘grieving family member’,  she was supposed to be grieving, wasn’t she? 
So, she put on the best red dress she could find and wore the face of someone who was grieving and set out to the gathering. 
When she entered, she noticed that there were many elites but since she didn’t know anyone , she decided to stand in a corner and gather as much information as she could like the wallflower everyone always told her she was. 
Growing up quiet and shy makes you observant, you stand in a room invisible to everyone else as if people know you are there but refuse to acknowledge you and so comes the overwhelming desire to make yourself be heard, be seen, be known. There are some perks of being a wallflower too though, you notice things others often miss, since no one notices you, you get to know secrets without others realizing. The wallflowers may seem innocent, but they are the smartest ones out there. And then she heard it. Two men, too drunk to notice an eavesdropper, whispering in reverent tones about a relic found among her grandfather’s papers, a compass that spun not north but toward “something else.” The words sliced through the air like prophecy. Just as she was about to leave a man of about the same age as her approached her. “Hello, do you not remember me?”, he asked her.  She couldn’t remember much of her childhood. “No, sorry.” She replied. “I am your childhood friend, Sameer. We used to play together and wouldn’t stop till our parents would have to drag us inside but you changed completely after your parents passed away in that accident. You became quiet and reserved, stopped talking, stopped coming to play, you would just cling to your grandfather and dream about reaching that fantasy city, you pushed everyone away. I know you don’t care about anything but your dream but maybe you do have a heart or used to. So to the person I used to know, I am sorry for her loss. I will have you know that I am chasing that city too. See you when I win. You know, if you had just talked to me things could have turned out very different but you’re you and will always remain you. Maybe when I beat you, you will quit this rat’s chase and go back to who you used to be.” He said and then she watched him go, baffled and more determined than ever, how could he say he wanted to change her if he never knew who she was to begin with? Before dawn, she had the compass in her hand.
***
The voyage was a blur of storms and sleepless nights. Salt burned her skin and every wave was like an insult, a mockery at her incompetence. She started feeling as if her grandfather was haunting her, mocking her, his voice echoed through her brain once again but this time to mock her, “I would’ve found it by now if I was you”.  Yet the needle never wavered. 
She started to feel like she was failing, falling, her life’s work slipping in front of her. How many times can you try before it’s too much, how many times can you try before you can’t anymore, how many times is too many times?
It pulled herself further into the desolate Pacific. Days bled into nights, and still she followed the trail until she found Atrakkis but it wasn’t how the stories described it, in fact it wasn’t beautiful at all, it was painted in monochrome, there was not one human there. 
It was clear then, it was her world that was painted black and white, her eyes had lost their light and though the place she looked at screamed with colours and life, she couldn’t even notice the  beauty of it, as she looked upon something that could have been hers, the parked ship was an indication she had lost to someone with more connections and perhaps more humanity. She saw Sameer smile cynically back at her and he said to her, “In that gathering even though you wore a smile, your eyes were those of someone who had already accepted defeat.You started grieving before you lost and that’s why you did lose,”. Then it was like something in her burst, a dam ruptured and she grabbed him by the collar and screamed, “When I look at tomorrow and all its infinite possibilities, a million different things could happen, I don’t even know if I will make it till tomorrow because whatever is left of today is so unpredictable and death doesn’t announce it’s arrival, yet I look at tomorrow like it’s the only thing that’s certain, like it’s bound to happen. Joy is a fleeting emotion and so is sorrow, or so they say. Losing is temporary and if you try hard enough you’ll eventually win, or so they say. Maybe I was cursed to be the exception because while others may see rain on some days and sunlight on others, my days are filled with doom and presentiments of an ominous future where the dark is suffocating enough to choke me and occasionally I do see the light but like a prisoner trapped in an underground prison, the light seems so close yet I know it is so far, something I yearn for, something I will spend my life chasing just to rot in that prison that sometimes is kind enough to let light seep through for a moment. I hold out my hand and reach for it with everything I’ve got, I scrape at the walls till my hands bleed and yet I can never reach it but I will wake up tomorrow and see these four walls again and the light as if mocking me will shine momentarily again and I will repeat the same thing again but with no results. Each time, feeling that this might be it, this might be when I might finally be  successful only to be brought back to reality by reality itself. One day many decades later when I am tired, I may ask myself, “Should I scream and cry until they see me as too much of an inconvenience to keep?” And frankly I do not know now what the answer to that will be but apprehensive fools like me don’t know when to stop and throw in the towel, they’re too cowardly to do anything about it so I know I will wake up tomorrow and hope again. So if you ask me how I can grieve something that never happened if I don’t know if it would happen, I know that hoping is like trying to bring someone that’s long gone back to life, but I know I will try because that’s all I know how to do . You can’t win if you’re destined to lose but you can grieve something that isn’t dead because you know that one day it will be.” As he watched her go he was reminded of his childhood friend again who was hidden underneath all those walls. He thought to himself, “ This piece of forgotten land is what you yearn for which is so different from what I yearn for yet it is the only thing that reminds me of you. If the world ended and took you with me and the stars screamed your name and not mine, the blood and tears would paint the once blue earth red but centuries later when they can tell apart my blood from yours would they find all the similarities that connect us or the constitutions that align or the rhythms that make us one or the fact that the earth, the stars, the sun and the galaxy itself are needed to end the agony, to end the world, to the end the suffering and to end everything that would be and had been just to end what you would have thought of me. However I know that is not what you want so let me be the ‘villain’ in your story if it will help you come back to yourself. Maybe in another universe where we are two different people, things would be like I wish they would and maybe then we would both win and get what we yearn for so deeply.” 

***

 She decided to return home and took to the sea again. 
She let a single tear drop from her eyes . It shouldn’t come as a shock to her, after all she was always second, her whole life she was never first and so maddened by anguish she turned off the engine and let the waves swallow her.

On her way to Atrakkis she had slowly lost her mind, she knew ambition would be the death of her, she just didn’t know it would take her so soon. One of those many lonely days she spent at sea frantically searching for something that was never her she saw her reflection in the mirror, and she laughed at the site of who stared back, “In this quest to find the lost city I lost myself, ironic right?” she thought. 

Soon the world would find the remains of a ‘brave woman’ who had the courage to face the world without that spark in her eye that keeps us alive and rats chew on the remains of ‘what could have been’. She never grew wings of success and yet before taking her last breath she is happy that she did grow wings, even if it weren’t of success. “Grandfather, I finally caught up to you,” she whispered, as the sea closed over her. The world turned black, and in that darkness, her spark once mistaken for greed, once worshipped as ambition finally burned out.

One day I am going to grow wings

At that moment she felt as if the world had ended, that there was no one left for whom she should struggle and fight, that maybe she should stop trying. However, she picked herself back up, she knew she needed to do it for him, now more than ever, she needed to carry on his legacy. 
***
While clearing out her grandfather’s desk, she noticed an unopened mail, an invitation for a gathering, a commemoration of his achievements and discoveries. She decided to use the opportunity to gather some information about his expeditions by interacting with people who were experts in that field. She informed the host that she would be attending as a ‘grieving family member’,  she was supposed to be grieving, wasn’t she? 
So, she put on the best red dress she could find and wore the face of someone who was grieving and set out to the gathering. 
When she entered, she noticed that there were many elites but since she didn’t know anyone , she decided to stand in a corner and gather as much information as she could like the wallflower everyone always told her she was. 
Growing up quiet and shy makes you observant, you stand in a room invisible to everyone else as if people know you are there but refuse to acknowledge you and so comes the overwhelming desire to make yourself be heard, be seen, be known. There are some perks of being a wallflower too though, you notice things others often miss, since no one notices you, you get to know secrets without others realizing. The wallflowers may seem innocent, but they are the smartest ones out there. And then she heard it. Two men, too drunk to notice an eavesdropper, whispering in reverent tones about a relic found among her grandfather’s papers, a compass that spun not north but toward “something else.” The words sliced through the air like prophecy. Just as she was about to leave a man of about the same age as her approached her. “Hello, do you not remember me?”, he asked her.  She couldn’t remember much of her childhood. “No, sorry.” She replied. “I am your childhood friend, Sameer. We used to play together and wouldn’t stop till our parents would have to drag us inside but you changed completely after your parents passed away in that accident. You became quiet and reserved, stopped talking, stopped coming to play, you would just cling to your grandfather and dream about reaching that fantasy city, you pushed everyone away. I know you don’t care about anything but your dream but maybe you do have a heart or used to. So to the person I used to know, I am sorry for her loss. I will have you know that I am chasing that city too. See you when I win. You know, if you had just talked to me things could have turned out very different but you’re you and will always remain you. Maybe when I beat you, you will quit this rat’s chase and go back to who you used to be.” He said and then she watched him go, baffled and more determined than ever, how could he say he wanted to change her if he never knew who she was to begin with? Before dawn, she had the compass in her hand.
***
The voyage was a blur of storms and sleepless nights. Salt burned her skin and every wave was like an insult, a mockery at her incompetence. She started feeling as if her grandfather was haunting her, mocking her, his voice echoed through her brain once again but this time to mock her, “I would’ve found it by now if I was you”.  Yet the needle never wavered. 
She started to feel like she was failing, falling, her life’s work slipping in front of her. How many times can you try before it’s too much, how many times can you try before you can’t anymore, how many times is too many times?
It pulled herself further into the desolate Pacific. Days bled into nights, and still she followed the trail until she found Atrakkis but it wasn’t how the stories described it, in fact it wasn’t beautiful at all, it was painted in monochrome, there was not one human there. 
It was clear then, it was her world that was painted black and white, her eyes had lost their light and though the place she looked at screamed with colours and life, she couldn’t even notice the  beauty of it, as she looked upon something that could have been hers, the parked ship was an indication she had lost to someone with more connections and perhaps more humanity. She saw Sameer smile cynically back at her and he said to her, “In that gathering even though you wore a smile, your eyes were those of someone who had already accepted defeat.You started grieving before you lost and that’s why you did lose,”. Then it was like something in her burst, a dam ruptured and she grabbed him by the collar and screamed, “When I look at tomorrow and all its infinite possibilities, a million different things could happen, I don’t even know if I will make it till tomorrow because whatever is left of today is so unpredictable and death doesn’t announce it’s arrival, yet I look at tomorrow like it’s the only thing that’s certain, like it’s bound to happen. Joy is a fleeting emotion and so is sorrow, or so they say. Losing is temporary and if you try hard enough you’ll eventually win, or so they say. Maybe I was cursed to be the exception because while others may see rain on some days and sunlight on others, my days are filled with doom and presentiments of an ominous future where the dark is suffocating enough to choke me and occasionally I do see the light but like a prisoner trapped in an underground prison, the light seems so close yet I know it is so far, something I yearn for, something I will spend my life chasing just to rot in that prison that sometimes is kind enough to let light seep through for a moment. I hold out my hand and reach for it with everything I’ve got, I scrape at the walls till my hands bleed and yet I can never reach it but I will wake up tomorrow and see these four walls again and the light as if mocking me will shine momentarily again and I will repeat the same thing again but with no results. Each time, feeling that this might be it, this might be when I might finally be  successful only to be brought back to reality by reality itself. One day many decades later when I am tired, I may ask myself, “Should I scream and cry until they see me as too much of an inconvenience to keep?” And frankly I do not know now what the answer to that will be but apprehensive fools like me don’t know when to stop and throw in the towel, they’re too cowardly to do anything about it so I know I will wake up tomorrow and hope again. So if you ask me how I can grieve something that never happened if I don’t know if it would happen, I know that hoping is like trying to bring someone that’s long gone back to life, but I know I will try because that’s all I know how to do . You can’t win if you’re destined to lose but you can grieve something that isn’t dead because you know that one day it will be.” As he watched her go he was reminded of his childhood friend again who was hidden underneath all those walls. He thought to himself, “ This piece of forgotten land is what you yearn for which is so different from what I yearn for yet it is the only thing that reminds me of you. If the world ended and took you with me and the stars screamed your name and not mine, the blood and tears would paint the once blue earth red but centuries later when they can tell apart my blood from yours would they find all the similarities that connect us or the constitutions that align or the rhythms that make us one or the fact that the earth, the stars, the sun and the galaxy itself are needed to end the agony, to end the world, to the end the suffering and to end everything that would be and had been just to end what you would have thought of me. However I know that is not what you want so let me be the ‘villain’ in your story if it will help you come back to yourself. Maybe in another universe where we are two different people, things would be like I wish they would and maybe then we would both win and get what we yearn for so deeply.” 

****

 She decided to return home and took to the sea again. 
She let a single tear drop from her eyes . It shouldn’t come as a shock to her, after all she was always second, her whole life she was never first and so maddened by anguish she turned off the engine and let the waves swallow her.

On her way to Atrakkis she had slowly lost her mind, she knew ambition would be the death of her, she just didn’t know it would take her so soon. One of those many lonely days she spent at sea frantically searching for something that was never her she saw her reflection in the mirror, and she laughed at the site of who stared back, “In this quest to find the lost city I lost myself, ironic right?” she thought. 

Soon the world would find the remains of a ‘brave woman’ who had the courage to face the world without that spark in her eye that keeps us alive and rats chew on the remains of ‘what could have been’. She never grew wings of success and yet before taking her last breath she is happy that she did grow wings, even if it weren’t of success. “Grandfather, I finally caught up to you,” she whispered, as the sea closed over her. The world turned black, and in that darkness, her spark once mistaken for greed, once worshipped as ambition finally burned out.

title.stringValue: Ten Bears and a Hundred Eunuchs

content.stringValue:
Bodies carved into incense sticks and poetry.
Ink to hide thought,
Mulberry scent to hide the leak of urine,
Lofty laughs to hide the agony behind the mask.

A society kept within the king’s proximity—
His ten bears, his hundred eunuchs.

Their names taken at the gates,
Their thoughts sieved from all logic,
And when they cry, throw their family
In the fire, along with that hairpin they cherish.

Then the performance begins:
The way the king watches the curtains 
Stop, and, then, hang.
Like committing suicide,
You're enjoying it too, right?

Chains to hold the anger
They strategically stuffed inside the desperate bear,
With mercy and empathy collapsing in the corridors,
Dogs wait outside, teasing.
“Come here, come here!" "Strike us! C'mon!"

Marble tiles veined with betrayal,
Words taped together into deals
To poison the most loyal.

Move. Glare, don't make noise.
Crouch until your spine learns obedience.

Words widowed of meaning.
You may watch,
Where poems break, palaces rise.
Each stanza a test.
Each word a debt to dignity you don’t even own.

“He isn’t entertaining anymore.” A rustle.
"Throw him out." A pause.
And with a flare of a wick,
A human loses his worth, as his warm
Knees kiss the humble hell, mopping the blood
Draining from his feet, he couldn't dance anymore.

"Bring another one. Dress him in silk.
Do not give him a name—teach him poetry."

A poet’s castrated pen,
A king’s dream: the world, his harem.

मैं और मेरा तकिया ,
अक्सर बातें किया करते हैं ,
हाल-ए-दिल अपना बयां किया करते हैं ।
कुछ मैं हूं सुनाती और कुछ……..
समझ जाता है बिन कहे ही।
रातों को जब नींद से मेरी अनबन हो जाती,
मेरी तन्हाई अक्सर उसे भी नींद से जगाती।
वह गवाह है हर उस दिन का,
टूटे हुए दिल के साथ ,
हर रात जाती हूं जब उसके पास।
हर रोज साथ वो देता,
बुंदे जो बरसती है आंखों से हमारी ,
सीने में अपने समा वो है लेता।
लेकिन कभी - कभी शिकायत भी है वो करता,
कि इतना भी तो अश्क बहाया न करो ,
कहीं  अगली सुबह सूरज पुछे हमसे ,
कि इतने तुम भीगे कहां हो?
उसे पता है ….कितने रातों को हम नहीं हैं सोए ,
कितने रातों को हम हैं रोए ।              
ख़ामोश हूं क्योंकि शब्दों की तिजोरी आज मेरी खाली हैं।
फिर भी मेरे दिल की हर एक बात ,
उसके कानों तक पहुंच ही जाती है।
हमेशा सिरहाने मेरे रहता,
जैसे हो मां की नरम गोदी ।
बड़ी अच्छी साथ है हमारी ,
हर एक सुख दुख की भागीदारी ।
करके उसे भारी खुद हल्की हो जाती ,
सिमट - लिपट कर फिर उसी पे हूं सो जाती ।
मैं हंसू तो वह खुश हो जाए ,
रोऊं तो हर गम वो पी जाए।
ए तकिये मेरे क्या बताऊं तुझे मैं क्या लगता है तू मेरे ?सुकून की नींद है तू ,
करवट बदलती हर रात का साथी है तू ।
तेरा - मेरा साथ उस दिन से ,
जिस दिन से आई हूं इस धरती पे ।
शायद उस दिन तेरा - मेरा साथ न होगा ,
जिस दिन दुल्हन नहीं पर विदा मैं हूंगी।
गलत न समझना उस दिन मेरे सिरहाने तू नहीं,
बस एक रस्म होगी।
माटी पर पड़ी बेजान जिस्म को लपेटे
सिर्फ वो सफेद चादर होगी।।

प्रेम अब भी है तुमसे…….
बस वो बेचैन आंखें अब सुकून ढूंढ रही है।
दिए कि लौ मद्धम ही सही, पर जल रही है ,
क्योंकि प्रेम अब भी है तुमसे।

तुम आए तो लगा था ,जैसे बहार है आई,
फरेब था वो मन का
भला पतझड़ और सावन का मिलन कहां है होता ?

तेरे कदमों की आहट से ,
दिल की धड़कनें जो तेज हो जाती थी ,
वह अब शोर बनकर चुभने लगी है कानों में।

उलझनें अब सुलझ रही हैं ,
वो नादानियां, वो नासमझी,अब सुधरने लगी है ,
मगर सच कहूं…..तो प्रेम अब भी है तुमसे।

जो दिन तुमसे ही शुरू ,तुमपे ही खत्म होती थी ,
वो आदतें अब बदल दी है हमने ,
मगर फिक्र न करना,ये दिल बदला नहीं है,
क्योंकि प्रेम अब भी है तुमसे।

वादें सात जन्मों के जो कभी किए थे हमने,
शायद भूल गए थे हम,
कि निभाने के लिए एक जनम ही काफी है।

प्रेम अब भी है तुमसे ,मगर  वो बात नहीं है ,
कि खुद को मिटाकर,सिर्फ तुम्हें याद रखें,
अब वो हालात नहीं हैं ।

छोड़ो ये सब पुरानी बातें ,कुछ नया सुनाऊं ?
जानते हो ,अब बिन तुम्हारे मैं जीने लगी हूं ,
तुम्हारे खयालों से अब निकलने लगी हूं ।
अब तो फुर्सत ही फुर्सत है हमें ,
अब बिन बात की गलियों में यूंही भटकती नहीं फिरती हूं ।

बुरा मान गए? सुनो न…..
बातें भी होंगी ,मुलाकातें भी होंगी ,
शायद कभी कभी राहों में साथ भी होंगी ,
बस वो जज़्बात नहीं होंगे..
जिसमें  जग पराया , सिर्फ तुम लगते थे अपने।

तू भले ही ना कहे ,फिर भी हमें इतना तो यकीन है ।
तू जहां कहीं भी रहे ,हमारी जगह अब भी वहीं बाकी है।

सागर की उस डूबती कश्ती की तरह ,
उम्मीद की किरण अब भी है बाकी ,
कि किसी किनारे पर मिलोगे तुम ,
क्योंकि……प्रेम अब भी है बाकी।

title.stringValue: A boy - the friend who never had one

content.stringValue:
A Boy — The Friend Who Never Had One

                                          INTRO

Not all heartbreak comes from love , Some of it comes from believing someone will stay.

When people talk about teenage years, they talk about fun, friendships, laughter.
They don’t talk about the boys who sit quietly at the edge of the classroom, watching friendships form without them.

This is not a story about loneliness.
It is a story about effort.
About a boy who tried — again and again — to belong.


                        Chapter 1 — Beginning


A cute, fair, and charming baby was born. His parents named him Yash.
Time moved forward without pause. Days turned into months. Months into years.

At four, Yash stepped into school holding his cousin sister’s hand tightly. Fear and curiosity walked beside him.

“I won’t drag this story with unnecessary details,” the narrator says. “Only what matters.”

From the start, Yash was shy. He spoke little, listened more. Teachers found him clever. Classmates barely noticed him. By class four, he had no real friends. While others ran across the playground, Yash stayed with his books.

During games, he joined his cousin’s friends — mostly girls. At that age, it felt innocent. Later came teasing. Then laughter. Then words he didn’t understand but felt ashamed carrying home.

Books didn’t laugh.
Books didn’t ask questions.

One day, someone sat beside him.

Ashish smiled easily. He spoke loudly. He laughed without fear.
For the first time, Yash laughed too — hesitant, then real.

They shared lunches, secrets, small victories.
Yash thought, Maybe this is how it begins.

One afternoon, boys who disliked Yash’s quiet happiness surrounded them. A push. Mud. Laughter that sounded playful until it wasn’t.

Yash slipped. His uniform soaked.

He stood up, walking toward Ashish, ready to forgive — because forgiveness felt easier than conflict.

Before he could speak, a slap landed. Then another.

The boys laughed.
Ashish laughed with them.

What stayed wasn’t the pain on his face.
It was the moment Yash understood he had already been left.

Yash didn’t raise his hand.
He never learned how.

That day, he learned something else instead:

Sometimes, being alone feels safer than hoping.


                        Chapter 2 — Years Full of Joy


For Yash’s betterment, his parents changed his school in class five.
A fresh start.

New books. New classrooms. Quiet hope.

On the first day, introductions were called. When Yash’s name came, his voice barely rose above a whisper:
“My name is Yash.”

For weeks, he ate alone.

Then, on the 10th of August, a boy stopped in front of him.

“Come with me.”

Rajesh didn’t ask why Yash sat alone. He simply made space.
Rajesh struggled with studies. 

Yash noticed it without judgment. They sat together. Studied together. Slowly, laughter returned.

Every lunch break, a seat was kept empty — waiting.

When Rajesh passed his exams with marks no one expected, he smiled in disbelief. Yash felt proud, not for himself, but for someone else.

For the first time, friendship felt steady.

Yash thought, Maybe this one will stay.


                         Chapter 3 — Betrayal

That year was the best Yash had ever known.

Rajesh was still close, and Kshitij had entered his life like support he hadn’t expected. Kshitij helped him, stood beside him, laughed with him. For the first time, Yash felt surrounded by people who wanted him there.

School felt lighter.
Days passed without fear.

Then the lockdown came.

Schools closed. Roads emptied. Life shrank into homes.
Yash’s family returned to their hometown. 

At first, the quiet felt comforting. He spent time with his sister, helped at home, filled his days with small, random routines
.
Then one afternoon, a group of boys from the neighborhood approached him.

“Come play with us.”

Yash hesitated. But loneliness makes hesitation weak. He agreed.

For some days, things went well. They played, talked, laughed. It felt normal. It felt safe.

Slowly, things changed.

Jokes turned sharp. Laughter lingered a little too long. Pushes came disguised as play. Then came words meant to embarrass. Then hands that hurt , The physical pain was intense, but what hurt more was that he never fought back.

But Yash didn’t fight back.

He stopped going out.

At home, he stayed alone in his room. He didn’t tell his parents. Fear stopped him — fear they would blame him, fear they wouldn’t understand, fear of becoming the problem again.

The lockdown ended.

School reopened.

Yash returned with one hope — Kshitij.

At first, seeing him felt familiar. Comforting.

But as the days passed something happened which was very unexpected,

Then whispers began.

Rumors spread — quiet, careless, cruel. Stories about Yash, about girls, about things that were never true. He heard his own name spoken differently now.

When the truth finally surfaced, it didn’t come from a friend.
It came from a teacher.

Kshitij was the one who had started it.

The betrayal hurt more because it came after kindness.

Apologies came later, after exams which were about six months later but  Thin and  Forced.

Yash refused them.

That angered them.

Kshitij and his cruel friends circled around yash ,
Cruel words followed — words meant to crush, not argue.

By the end of that year, Yash found himself where he had been before.
Alone again.


                              Chapter 4 — Realisation


That evening, Yash stood near the well, listening to his own breathing.

The world felt heavy. His thoughts kept returning to one question:

Why does it always end like this?

Then Rajesh’s face came to him — not speaking loudly, not accusing.

“Don’t do it, Yash. Your parents need you. You’re not a failure.”
Yash stepped back.

That night, he went home. Ate dinner. Slept.

Survival made no noise.

                     Chapter 5 — Learning to Stay


A new city. A new classes 

This time, Yash didn’t rush toward anyone. He focused on his studies.
 On himself.

People came and went.

When study groups dissolved, he didn’t break.

When friendships faded, he didn’t question his worth.

He learned something quietly:

Not everyone who enters your life is meant to stay.

And , 
Years later, Yash still sits with books — but no longer to hide.

Sometimes alone.
Sometimes not.

He never stopped believing in friendship.
He just stopped begging for it.

And that made all the difference.

But at the end ,
Yash learned that expectations were heavier than being alone.
Solitude taught him independence — and confidence followed.

वो रोज़ सुबह शीशे के सामने खड़ी होती थी।
साड़ी सीधी करती, बिंदी ठीक करती, और मुस्कान पहन लेती — जैसे कोई ज़रूरी आभूषण हो।

घर से निकलते समय माँ की आवाज़ आती,
“ज़रा संभल कर रहना… लोग देख रहे हैं।”

ऑफिस में बॉस की नज़रें बोलती थीं,
“थोड़ा मुस्कुरा दो… काम आसान हो जाएगा।”

शाम को पड़ोसी पूछते,
“अब तक शादी क्यों नहीं हुई?”

और रात को वही शीशा फिर सामने होता।
इस बार मुस्कान उतार दी जाती थी।

शीशा सच दिखाता था —
थकी हुई आँखें,
दबी हुई आवाज़,
और वो सवाल जो किसी ने कभी नहीं पूछा:
“मैं क्या चाहती हूँ?”

दिन-ब-दिन, वही सवाल उसके भीतर गहराता गया।
तब एक सुबह, शीशा टूट गया।
काँच के टुकड़ों में उसका चेहरा बिखर गया।

और पहली बार उसने राहत की साँस ली।
क्योंकि अब उसे किसी को कुछ दिखाने की ज़रूरत नहीं थी।

उस दिन उसने बिना मुस्कान के बाहर कदम रखा।
लोगों ने कहा,
“आज कुछ अलग लग रही है।”

वो मन ही मन मुस्कुराई।
क्योंकि आज पहली बार,
वो खुद जैसी लग रही थी।

और उस दिन से उसने सीखा —
दुनिया की निगाहें बदल नहीं सकतीं,
पर अपनी आत्मा की आज़ादी वह खुद पा सकती है।

छुपी हुई रोशनी के पीछे,
एक लड़की अपने आप से बातें करती है।
दिल के कोने में बहता दर्द का दरिया,
जो हर पल वही सवाल करता है –
“क्या मैं फिर से मुस्कुरा सकूँगी?”

उसकी हर मुस्कान के पीछे,
हर खुशी में छुपी थोड़ी उदासी है।
रात के साए में वह अपनी आवाज़ ढूँढती है,
और खुद से पूछती है –
“क्या मेरा दर्द कभी खत्म होगा?”

उसकी आँखों में एक कहानी है,
शब्दों से नहीं, अनुभव से भरी।
पर उसके दिल में उम्मीद की लौ है –
एक नई सुबह, एक नई रोशनी की।

दुनिया के शोर में उसकी चीख़ गूँजती है –
“क्यों एक लड़की सुरक्षित नहीं है?”
लोग कहते हैं – “वो खुद गलत थी,”
जैसे उसका दर्द, उसका हक़, सब भूल गए हों।

उसके अंदर की आग, उसका संघर्ष,
हर याद, हर आँसू – उसकी ताकत बन जाते हैं।
उसकी छुपी मुस्कान एक निशानी है,
जो कहती है – “मैं टूट सकती हूँ,
पर मैं कभी ख़त्म नहीं हो सकती।”

समाज की अंधेरी गलियों में,
उसकी आवाज़ सन्नाटा तोड़ती है।
धीरे-धीरे, वह सन्नाटा बदल रहा है,
हर इंसान के लिए एक नई जगह बना रहा है।

और एक दिन, वह लड़की अपनी रोशनी के साथ खड़ी होगी,
शांत, लेकिन अडिग,
एक ऐसे असर के साथ, जो कभी नहीं मिटेगा।
उसकी ताकत, उसकी हिम्मत,
एक नई दुनिया का सूरज उगाएगी –
जहाँ हर लड़की अपने अस्तित्व को गले लगाएगी,
अपने दर्द को अपनी शक्ति में बदलकर,
अपनी जिंदगी को खुशियों से महकाएगी .

वो रोज़ सुबह शीशे के सामने खड़ी होती थी।
साड़ी सीधी करती, बिंदी ठीक करती, और मुस्कान पहन लेती — जैसे कोई ज़रूरी आभूषण हो।

घर से निकलते समय माँ की आवाज़ आती,
“ज़रा संभल कर रहना… लोग देख रहे हैं।”

ऑफिस में बॉस की नज़रें बोलती थीं,
“थोड़ा मुस्कुरा दो… काम आसान हो जाएगा।”

शाम को पड़ोसी पूछते,
“अब तक शादी क्यों नहीं हुई?”

और रात को वही शीशा फिर सामने होता।
इस बार मुस्कान उतार दी जाती थी।

शीशा सच दिखाता था —
थकी हुई आँखें,
दबी हुई आवाज़,

title.stringValue: Ten Bears and a Hundred Eunuchs

content.stringValue:
Bodies carved into incense sticks and poetry.
Ink to hide thought,
Mulberry scent to hide the leak of urine,
Lofty laughs to hide the agony behind the mask.

A society kept within the king’s proximity—
His ten bears, his hundred eunuchs.

Their names taken at the gates,
Their thoughts sieved from all logic,
And when they cry, throw their family
In the fire, along with that hairpin they cherish.

Then the performance begins:
The way the king watches the curtains 
Stop, and, then, hang.
Like committing suicide,
You're enjoying it too, right?

Chains to hold the anger
They strategically stuffed inside the desperate bear,
With mercy and empathy collapsing in the corridors,
Dogs wait outside, teasing.
“Come here, come here!" "Strike us! C'mon!"

Marble tiles veined with betrayal,
Words taped together into deals
To poison the most loyal.

Move. Glare, don't make noise.
Crouch until your spine learns obedience.

Words widowed of meaning.
You may watch,
Where poems break, palaces rise.
Each stanza a test.
Each word a debt to dignity you don’t even own.

“He isn’t entertaining anymore.” A rustle.
"Throw him out." A pause.
And with a flare of a wick,
A human loses his worth, as his warm
Knees kiss the humble hell, mopping the blood
Draining from his feet, he couldn't dance anymore.

"Bring another one. Dress him in silk.
Do not give him a name—teach him poetry."

A poet’s castrated pen,
A king’s dream: the world, his harem.

title.stringValue: Title: Where Is the Soul of Art?

content.stringValue:
Title:
Where Is the Soul of Art?

Odisha🫶🌸🧿 
not merely a state,
but the living pulse of every Odia heart.

A spiritual epic,
where art, architecture, culture, sculpture,
and tradition meet as one.

Where every grain of soil speaks,
and humans walk as companions of the Divine.

Mantras dwell in the earth,
Krishna breathes through art.

In the breath of my land
is inscribed the name of the eternal hero
who rules countless universes beyond time.

Within the colors of Pattachitra
lies the hidden inner sanctum of the soul.

In the gestures of Odissi dance
rests the silent language of meditation.

Every temple carving here
holds enchanted, unspoken images—
for which the heart dances
and devotion is born as hope.

Dhauli is not mere dust;
it is the deep shadow of penance,
where non-violence rises
as the soul’s highest victory.

The stones of Konark whisper
in the wheel of time,
they alone remain the mute witnesses.

Having everything,
why do we still lag behind today?

From birth I am Odia,
my mother tongue is Odia
then why do we hesitate
to be known as Odia everywhere?

Odisha, Kalinga, Utkal, Udra
are these only names?

Whom am I searching for here?
Success, peace, or acceptance?

Is my life a stage,
or a classical scripture?

Am I learning,
or have I forgotten my own existence?

Chasing modernity,
am I crushing and burning my roots?

What am I truly searching for?
Where have my conscience and identity gone?

Are they asleep,
or merely ignored?

Am I searching for the peace
that has always lived within me?

The soul
that which is ageless, immortal, infinite, indestructible.

That inner home
where the elder of our house smiles gently
none other than Jagannath,
the Lord of the Universe.

Are you tired?
Pause for a moment.

You are not asleep
awaken.

Do not drown in despair;
hold the pride of courage.

You will not lose
you will surely prevail.

Face circumstances without trembling;
everything will fall into place.

Remember
I am still with you, always.
