आइने के उस पार

मैं ये खत इसलिए लिखने जा रहा हूँ,
क्यूंकी मुझे यकीन है तुम एक दिन जरूर मिलने आओगी मुझे,
"जौन" साहब की तरह खोया हुआ तो नहीं,
मगर एक हसीन इश्क के मानिंद, 
एक हसीन सफर की जानिब, 
सुकून से बिखरा हुआ पाओगी मुझे... !

और इस कश्मकश में हल्की सी मुस्कुराहट के साथ खुद से ये सवाल पूछोगी...
"जिस इंसान ने ता-उम्र दर्द बेचा है बाजारों में
वो आज इतनी इत्मीनान से यहाँ ऐसे लेटा क्यों है?"
क्यों अब ये मुझसे कुछ नहीं कहता..?

तुम मेरी आँखों से मेरे हाल-ए-दिल की तफसीलत लेना चाहोगी...
मगर कंम्भख्त, वो तुम्हें ताकते ही रह जाएंगे पर तुमसे कुछ नहीं कहेंगे...
वो अब उन यादों से आजाद हो चुके हैं, 
जिसके इश्क की ता-उम्र उन्होंने किश्तें चुकाई हैं...

उस दिन मेरी जान तुम्हें अपनी आँखों से इन्हें पढ़ना होगा,
मुझे यकीन है तुम ये कर सकती हो...
और जब तुम इन्हें पढ़ रही होगी, मुझसे वादा करो कि तुम्हारी आँखें नम नहीं होंगी,
तुम्हारे आंसू पी सकूँ अब इतनी मुझमें काबिलियत बची नहीं होगी...
तो इन अश्कों को पलकों के किवाड़ों में ही बंद रहने दो...
वादा करो मुझसे तुम ये कर पाओगी !!

मैंने ता-उम्र नज़्में लिखीं, ग़ज़लें लिखीं यहीं इसी कमरे में बैठकर,
कभी लगा नहीं कि तुम यहाँ नहीं हो, कभी तुम्हारी गैर-मौजूदगी मुझे महसूस तक नहीं हुई...
तुम्हारी मौजूदगी हमेशा मेरी लिखावट में दिखी हैं,
और अब मैं जहाँ भी रहूँगा वहाँ भी तुम्हारा साया हमेशा होगा मेरे साथ...
किसी हमसफर की तरह.... !!

तुम्हें ये कमरा काफी तन्हा और खौफनाक लग रहा होगा,
खामोशियाँ गूँजती हुई सुनाई दे रही होंगी तुम्हें यहाँ,
मेज़ पर पड़ी किताबों से लफ़्ज़ निकलकर दीवारों पर दीमक की तरह बिखरे दिखेंगे,
उन दीवारों पर कान लगाए बैठोगी तो ये तुम्हें वो सारी कहानियाँ बता देंगे,
जो मैंने अभी तक लिखी नहीं हैं, जो किसी ने अभी तक सुनी नहीं हैं...

वहीं मेज़ की दाईं ओर एक अलमारी मिलेगी तुम्हें, ये कोई आम अलमारी नहीं, ये उन यादों की अलमारी है जिसमें मैंने तुम्हारी सारी यादें कैद कर रखी हैं...
तुम चाहो तो उन्हें अपने साथ रख सकती हो...

तुम्हें मेज़ पर कुछ आधे जलाए सिगरेट के टुकड़े और आधे शराब के प्याले पड़े मिलेंगे,
जो इस बात की रज़ामंदी देंगे कि यहाँ मैं कभी अकेला नहीं था...
यहाँ बहुत से लोग रहते थे... !!

तुम्हें ड्रॉइंग हॉल में एक बड़ा सा आइना मिलेगा,
इस आइने के उस पार हर शाम एक मुशायरा लगता है,
तुम अगर शाम ढलने के बाद यहाँ रुको तो ये तुम्हें भी दिख जाएगा,
काफी उम्दा मुसाफिर आते हैं वहाँ, और वो अपनी माशूका के साथ उनकी बीती कहानियाँ सुनाया करते हैं...जैसे, 
"जौन साहब फरीहा की, 
साहिर साहब अमृता की, 
क़ैस अपनी लैला की, 
और कहानीकार अपनी खानसाहिबा की... !!"

इन सभी ने यहाँ इश्क का आखिरी मकाम गुज़ारा है,
किसी लाश की तरह दार-ए-फ़ानी में अपनी आखिरी ख्वाहिश तक ये तड़पते रहे हैं,
इश्क में भटकते हुए हर राही की मंज़िल ये कमरा है,
यहाँ आया हुआ हर मुसाफिर किसी दूसरे मुसाफिर की राह ताकता है...
कि कोई आए और उन्हें यहाँ से आज़ाद करे...!
मेरा आज आखिरी दिन है यहाँ, एक मुसाफिर मुझे ढूंढते हुए कल तक यहाँ आ जाएगा, और मुझे इस क़ैद से हमेशा के लिए रिहा कर देगा...!!

मैंने ये खत उसी मुसाफिर के लिए लिखा है,
जब तुम इसे पढ़ोगी तो समझ जाओगी कि ये खौफनाक कमरा ही वो मंज़र है जहाँ एक कहानी खत्म होती है तो दूसरी शुरू...
बिल्कुल ज़िंदगी की तरह,
मेरी कहानी बस इतनी सी थी, तुमसे शुरू और तुम्हीं पर खत्म...

अब तुम मेरी जान इसे एक नया मोड़ देना,
इश्क में खोए हुए मुसाफिरों को एक नयीं राह दिखाना,
एक नया इश़्क लिखना, जिसमें मंज़र खूबसूरत हो...
क्योंकि अब ये कमरा तुम्हारा है, और तुम इस खामोश कमरे की आवाज़...
मैं अब तुम्हें आइने के उस पार दिखूंगा,
मैं अब तुम्हारी कहानियाँ तूम्हें सुनाऊँगा जों मैनें कभी लिखी थीं...
और तुम अब वों कहानियाँ लिखना जों तूम्हें मूझे सुनानी थीं...
फिर एक दिन, आ जाएगा कोई मुसाफिर अपने महबूब को ढूंढते हुए यहाँ तक....
उस रोज़ हम जरूर मिलेंगे जब तुम आ जाओगी आइने के उस पार..!!

खुदा हाफ़िज़, 
आपका कहानीकार... !!

राह-ए-हयात 

﻿बहुत दूर इस शहर की शोर से,
जहांँ इंसानों का बसेरा नहीं,
 जहाँ किसी रौशनी के आने की आहट तक नहीं,
 जहाँ खामोशियाँ रात के अँधेरे लम्हों से गुफ़्तगू करती पाईं जाती हैं,
 वहांँ एक घर है, 
 हाँ वही, पहाड़ों के पीछे वाला घर...
 जो हमने कईं कहानियों में सुना है....!
 वहांँ अब एक शायर रहता हैं,
 जो वहांँ दर्द की बंदिश में हैं....!!

 उसीं घर के आँगन में कईं तरीक़ो के फूलों के बाग हैं,
 कईं तरह के अनोखे परिंदे हैं वहांँ... 
 उन्हीं में से मैं एक हूँ...!
 हम परिन्दों की कोईं आवाज़ नहीं हैं, 
 ना इस शहर में कोईं किसी सें कुछ कहता है,
 एक दरिया हैं यहाँ जो बरसों से सुखा पड़ा है,
 रात के जुगनू भी शोर नहीं करते यहाँ,
 इसी खामोशियों के बीच यें घर हैं,
 जहाँ वो शायर रहता है...!!
 (लकड़ी के कुर्सी पर बैठ कर किसी को याद करता रहता है वो)


 उसी घर में एक कमरा भी है,
 शायद उसी शायर का कमरा हो,
 उस कमरे की सारी खिड़कियाँ हमेशा खुली रहती हैं,
 शायद उसकी मुंतज़िर आँखे किसी के आने की राह देख रही हो,
 यां फिर, कोई ख्व़ाब हों जो किसी से मिलने के लिए खिड़कियों से बाहर जाता हो...!
 मगर इस विरान से दश्त में भला ऐसा कौन है?
 अगर ऐसा कोई होता तो उन खिड़कियों को बंद कर देता,
 उन ख्वाबों को हकीकत में तब्दील कर देता,
 अपनी रोशनी के चरागों से उस कमरे को जगमगा देता,
 कोई होता, जो उन दीवारों पे लगी किसी के तस्वीर से गर्द हटा देता,
 जिससे वो धुंधली हुई तस्वीर में बसने वाली लड़की हमें भी दिख जाती...
 मगर कंभख्त ये माजरा भी एक ख्वाब की तरह हैं...हसीन मगर झूठ!!

मैं रोज़ उस शायर की लिखी नज़्में सुनता हूँ,
वो कागज़ों पर कुछ लफ़्ज़ लिखता रहता हैं,
वों उन लफ़्ज़ों को अपने लबों से कभी नहीं कहता...
फिर भी वो लफ़्ज़ हमें सुनायी देते हैं....!
मानो इस शहर की खामोशी को किसी ने उसकी आवाज लौटा दी हो,
उनके लफ्जों में दर्द, बेचैनी, तगाफुल, रंजिश, उल्फत और खौफनाक खामोशी हैं,
मगर ना जाने क्यों हमें उसमें सिर्फ इश्क़ दिखायीं देता है...!!

ऐसा पाकीज़ा इश्क! जिसकी खुशबू से इस आंगन के फूल खिल उठते हैं,
ऐसा इश्क! जिसकी आँखों से गिरे अश्कों से वो दरिया फिर से बहने लगते हैं,
मगर वो शायर खुद ये बात नहीं जानता,
के उसकी कहानियों में कईं लोगों की कहानियों का बसेरा हैं,
वो "कहानीकार" खुद इश्क के हवाले में रह कर दर्द से वज़ू करता है...!
काश वो समझ पाए कभी के इश्क जो वो लिखता है... 
उस इश्क़ कों किसी मुस्तकबिल की ज़रूरत नहीं...!!
 (खैर! अब ये बात उसें समझाऐं कौन?)

 एक रोज़ हुआ यूं,
 उसके कमरे की सारी खिड़कियाँ बंद हो गई,
 मैं ये देख काफी खुश हुआ, 
 के चलो आख़िर-कार उस शायर से कोईं मिलने तो आ गया,
 मैं उसके कमरे की और बढ़ा और देखा,
 के हवाओं ने गुज़रते हुए उन कागज़ों को ज़र्द कर दिया है,
 उस लकड़े की कुर्सी पे धूल सन्नी हुईं थी,
 मानो बरसों से उस पर कोई बैठा ना हो,
 फिर वो शक्स कौन था जिसकी परछाइयां मैं देखा करता था?
 वो कौन था जो किसी को याद करते हुए कागजों पर कुछ लिखा करता था?
 बिना कुछ बोले सुनाई देने वाली उसके लफ़्ज़ों की वो गूंज भला किसकी थी... जो मैं सुना करता था?

 शायद वो चला गया हों,
 उसे आख़िर अपनी मंजिल मिल गई हों...!
 वो चला तो गया पर उसकी मेज पे उसने अपनी किताब खोल कर रख दी थी,
 सारे लफ़्ज़ कमरे में किताबों से निकल के बिखरे पड़े थें,
 बहुत जल्द ये भी चले जायेंगे उसी शायर की तरफ,
 जैसे निंद की खिड़कियों सें ख्वाब आते जाते हैं ना?... बिलकुल उसी तरह...!!

हवाओं ने जैसे उस किताब का आखिरी पन्ना पलटा उसपे लिखा था...!
 "अब यहाँ सिर्फ तुम ही हो मेरे हमराह, मेरे परिंदे,
 इस कमरे ने सिर्फ खामोशियों से गुफ्तगू की है बरसों तक,
 और तुम इस मंज़र की खामोशी को या तो ख़तम करो या हमेशा बरक़रार रखो,
 यह मंज़र अब तुम्हारे हाथों में हैं...!
 तुम अब इश्क़ सिख गए हो... 
 मुझे यकीन है कि तुम उसें निभा भी लोगे,
 यही इश्क की साज़-ए-हयात है, और यहीं इश्क की राह-ए-हयात भी....!!

ANDHEE

“Oh my God ! What a girl she is !”All the students laugh. “How difficult to read, yaar."One of the students taunts Roshni. “I can say ,Andhee," another student says. All say, “Andhee …Andhee”.
  These are the comments , spoken by the college students where Roshni tries to seek her admission in M.A. English(Hons) in the Allahabad University, Allahabad. Roshni becomes embarrassed and goes away from there. 
  Roshni is the only child of our parents to whom they brought her up very carefully since her childhood her eyesight is very weak. The doctor advised her to avoid reading, watching TV and mobile more.
………………………………………..
Roshni….Roshni…. beta, where are you? Roshni's mother Uma comes from the kitchen into her room. She sees that Roshni is indulged in keen study. She  places the tray on the table and rebukes her,”I have said to you don't take much pressure for your examination.” She closes her books but Roshni feels offended .Why not after all ,she has been preparing for her entrance test of taking admission at Allahabad University. Her father Mr Ravi Kishan loves her very much. He always supports her. He is a clerk in a private company. He does not earn much. It is her parents dream to make her daughter professor of English. Roshani got 89% marks in B.A. (hons) in English and she was the gold medalist.
 Today is her first day in the university to take entrance exams for masters.When the students see her wearing heavy spectacles , they begin to tease her. This is not a new thing for Roshni. Roshani has had to face very critical situations since her childhood. When she was in High School her neighbours taunted her to say that she will not survive in study more. But despite this, she became the district topper. Her parents felt proud of her and provided her all valuable things to continue her studies.When she was in Intermediate, aunty came into her house to have a proposal of marriage for her. When Ravi Kishan knew  that the bride's family was a poor one and the boy was a little deaf he became very angry. Uma wept for the insulting behaviour of her aunt. Roshani could not bear such an insult to her family and she decided to be a professor.
    ……………………………
  As soon as Roshani enters the examination hall, the teacher asks for her roll number. Roshni becomes nervous. She brings out her roll number from her kit  and tries to read”…Sir…sir…2….5…1”(She peeps into the admit card). “What are you saying ? Why don't you read your roll number?  How will you cross your exam?” The teacher mocks her.  All the examinees begin to laugh. One of the students says,”Sir, her eyesight is very weak.”(She keeps her hand on the mouth to hide her smile) Roshani gives her admit card to the teacher. He points out her seat number. When she is solving her paper she bows down on the paper to read  carefully and all the examinees make fun of her. But Roshani does not care and tries to complete her answers. Suddenly the bell rings and all the students begin to come outside one by one. The teacher notices that Roshni is sitting in her chair and  asks her to give an OMR sheet. As she gets up she is stumbled down by a chair. The teacher laughs at her again. “Oh! look at her, that's the girl who gave the written test in the examination room with us”. one of the girls points at her. “Yes yaar she is” Other students reply. One of the students, Rupesh calls her and says,”Why are you wasting your time ? You are a blind girl ,Andhee…”all laugh. Another boy,Amit says,’’Leave the study and get married to a man who is mental. Ha…ha…ha…” Roshni keeps silent and passes away from there. When she reaches her home,she rushes into her room and begins to sob. Her parents became anxious about what happened to her. When they ask her, she embraces her mother and explains everything that had happened with her in the universities. His father Ravi Kishan shows affection and says,”Is this a new thing for you bete?” Roshani sees him.“Since you grew up you had to face same situations, but my darling child, why are you thinking such futile words? This is a society in which everybody tries to push others. You have to focus on your goal ,beta.” Roshani smiles and embraces her father.
      ……………………..
“Roshni…. Roshni….where are you?” Rachita calls her. Uma asks her why she is screaming loudly. Rachita is the close friend of Roshni who always takes care of her. Roshni comes out from her own room and asks her, "Why are you crying like a mental?” “Oh why not ? You will have to tell me mental because you have proved you are intelligent”. Uma asks her what she means. Rachita says Roshni to check her mail from Allahabad University. Roshni checks mail hurriedly.She becomes glad,”Oh my God!” her father asks her. Rachita tells that Roshni had passed the entrance test and got the highest marks. Her parents feel happy.
Roshni is very eager to take admission in Allahabad University. She wears a long kurti and plazo to seek admission. As she enters the premises with Rachita, one of the girls taunts her,”Lo..she has come. Did you know she has passed the entrance test”. Another girl replies, “Oh yaar! She comes in the semi blindedness category. She has taken advantage of her reservation.” “What do you know what you are saying?” Rachita asks her and says, “Perhaps you don't know that she got the highest marks in the unreserved category. So shut your mouth.”

Roshni is a submissive girl.She does not like to fight with anybody. In the classes, Roshni gives answers very confidently so that her English professors admired her. All the students became thrilled to see her presentation level and confidence and  inspired by her ability. One day when she takes part in the departmental seminar,,she begins to read paper but she is shocked to see that she has brought another paper in place of her own paper. One of the girls says to other fellow students, "You know I had stolen her paper and placed another paper.” Everyone becomes glad. One of the boys, Arjun, says,”Now what will she do? Andhee…” (All make a posture of making fun.) 
Roshani becomes embarrassed but she controls herself and begins to read paper. She peeks into the paper to know what the actual word is written. Sometimes she is distracted. Her teacher asked her why. One of the students gets up and says,"Oh sir she cannot read, she is Andhee…” Roshni becomes perplexed but she does not lose her mind and suddenly she begins to speak without paper. All the scholars become surprised to see her understanding level.
Roshni does not like to gossip with other girls. She thinks it is useless to waste time on superfluous topics. Her only motive is to secure good marks in post graduation and get the degree of Net,JRF. Her performance in the class, seminars and quizzes make an influence on other students. When she gave any answer, her English teachers,especially HOD ,Professor Babita Kamarkar became glad. She asks her to come to her for any query at any time.
    ………………………….
One day Mrs.Uma asks Roshni to go to the marriage of her cousin with them . Roshni refuses to go. Her examinations are near and she has to submit her project on contemporary theory to HOD. Uma becomes upset, “What is this,Roshni ?Your cousin's marriage and you are denying”. Ravikishan says,”Don’t force her to go with us. You know our first priority is to set her free for studies.” The next day when she returns from the college, she tells her mother that she will  go with them to attend the marriage. Her HOD told her to submit the project within three months. Uma feels happy.
     When she reaches the party one of Uma’s relatives asks about Roshni. Uma tells them proudly that she is appearing for masters in English. A lady taunts her “Oh my God! your eyesight is too weak. How can you study properly?”(Roshni smiles and tries to escape.) But she stumbled down. The lady remarks,”Oh, Andhee…..” All the guests laugh at her. Uma picks up  her daughter and screams loudly, “You don't know my daughter is the topper of Allahabad University.” and turns towards the Lady, “What about your daughter? bhabhi ji. I know she failed two times in post graduation. Shame on you.” The lady becomes embarrassed and goes out from there. Ravi Kishan introduces his family to his relative Mrs. and Mr. Agarwal. Mrs.Agrawal becomes impressed to see Roshni and asks Ravi Kishan about her future. Ravi Kishan explains that she wants to be a professor, after that they will think about her marriage. Mrs Agrawal interrupts and says, “Who will be ready to get married to such a girl. She is so called blind, I mean Andhee.” Roshni is neutral because she has become accustomed to such taunts.
The time passed quickly.  Roshni is preparing for the last semester of the examination. Now she has filled the form of UGC NET,JRF. Mr Ravi Kishan asks her to take any coaching. He explains to her that there are many coaching centres like Adda 447, Physicswala, Navneet Kaur, Mahesh Pareekh and Eklavya etc. Uma tries to convince her to take any coaching. But Roshani doesn't agree.She says, “I am not interested in taking any coaching, mom. I want to do self study and I hope I will pass JRF.” Mr Ravi Kishan and Uma smile to see their daughter's confidence.
       …………………………
One day her classmate Chitransh comes to her residence. Roshni becomes perplexed to see him. Chitransh tells her that he likes her because of her energetic spirit to do work independently. Chitransh is also preparing for civil services. He tells Roshani how he feels helpless when other students taunt her and call her Andhee. He convinced her not to think about them. They are jealous of her success. Roshni feels happy to see his sympathetic behaviour.She says, “I don't care what others think about me. My eyesight is very weak, it does not mean that I am blind or this is a kind of disability. I only focus on my target.”
 After some days Roshani is astonished to know that she has received 80% marks in postgraduation and now she has become the topper of the University. Her parents are very pleased. When she reaches college, the principal calls her in her cabin. She is welcomed by the professors. The students  greet her.  Her HOD, Mr kamarkar says,”Roshni! I am proud of you. You are the model for others.No doubt, you have become the inspiration for others. Mr kamarkar gives a bit of sweet to her.
  When she comes back home, Uma introduces her to her friend, Mrs Leela Dayal. Mrs Leela sees her and says “This is your daughter..Uma. I think I met her anywhere. (She persists in her mind) Yes..remember…she came to the shop to buy some books. I was there. Her eyesight was very weak.” She says again peevishly, “How can she read and write?” “But she is the topper of the university,”Uma replies. “What can I do? Uma ,please don't mind , for running a family, a lady has to open her eyes all around but she is too blind to see. I think.. Andhee.” Uma becomes angry and says, “You are my college friend, if you insult my daughter I won't bear this.”
      “Why are you crying? Uma. I came here for a proposal of marriage for your daughter but I didn't know this was your daughter. Please don't mind but the truth is that nobody will be ready to marry her?”She speaks abruptly. Roshni does not bear her mother's insult. She says boldly, “What do you think aunty? In a girl's life, marriage is compulsory. Sorry to say aunty, I have to study more. Please go from here. Who are you wasting your time with  an Andhee girl?”
Mrs. Dayal goes away immediately. Roshni looks at her mother, both begin to smile.
  Roshani's stupendous learning creates a problem in her eyes. Sometimes she finds it blurred before her eyes. Often she wipes her spacts but is unable to get the right word. Her parents take her to the doctor. The doctor checks her eyes and says,”I warned you, Roshani,do not work more, otherwise it would be harmful to you. Mr Ravi Kishan ji please be careful for eyes otherwise she will lose  her eyesight.  Maybe she would become blind, I mean Andhee.” Her parents become anxious but Roshani speaks at random, “Oh doctor uncle! Why are you scaring my parents?. Please increase one  number of my spects." The doctor laughs a little and says, “Your daughter is qeer, Mr Ravi Kishan ji”.
   Roshani goes to attempt UGC NET, JRF examination with Chitransh in a Higher Secondary School of Allahabad. Vanity enters the examination hall and some girls and boys begin to ridicule her. A girl,Shamita says, “Lo! She has also come here Andhee. Ha… ha… ha….”  A boy says, No…no… don't say to Andhee ,she is the topper and definitely she will be the topper of Net, JRF.
 One of the girls says, “Why have you come here? Let's leave the paper” .(She laughs)
“I am unable to understand you, Shamita. You should feel proud of her but you are having fun here. Shame on you.” Chandran speaks angrily to Shamita .One of the boys,Arjit comes close to Chitransh and challenges, "O chamche…..shit , lets see how will she attempt answers on the screen? Increase your lens number.”(All laugh) 
 Roshni does not reply and goes ahead. When she enters her room,the scanner sees her and asks, “How will you give the exam ? You had to choose ‘brail’.” “What sir ?I am able to do the exam. This is my personal matter.” replies Roshani. They scan her pic and fingerprints, she takes her seat and prepares herself for the paper before the screen. When she returns home, her father asks how her paper has gone. Roshni replies in an affirmative gesture. Her mother embraces her.
     ………………………..
After 1 month the UGC NET JRF result was out. Roshni again gets 100% time and becomes the topper. All the students were shocked. Her parents are overwhelmed and the neighbours come to her house to congratulate her. Her university professors also congratulate her and give blessings for the future. Professor Kamarkar advises her to fill the form of GDC, coming out shortly and apply for assistant professor of English. When the forms were came, Roshni filled them and again began to busy in her study.
One day Mrs. Agarwal, who insulted Roshni at the party, comes to her house with her husband. Uma does not like her after that incident. When she notices Roshni studying ,she says, “How lovely that girl ! Very intelligent. I believe that she would be a professor.” Her parents smile. As Uma gets up to go to the kitchen,Mrs. Agarwal asks her about her marriage. She offers the marriage proposal of her nephew. Mr Ravi Kishan is surprised. Roshni comes there and says bluntly, “Oh aunty! How can you choose an  Andhee girl for your nephew?” Mrs.Agrawal ignores her words and says, "Beta don't think so . You are able to do all the work.” “This is so because you think I am going to be a professor. Your opinion has suddenly changed.” Her parents frankly refuse her proposal.
Roshni gets success to make a reputation of her parents in the society. Whenever her parents go, people begin to praise Roshani. The people who laughed at her and made vulgar comments on her parents ,began to appreciate their support for Roshani.
Time passes quickly. Roshni appeared for the written test of assistant professor and she again became the topper in the list of successful candidates. When she faces the interview, the panel of the interview board examines her documents and becomes surprised. They begin to ask questions one by one and Roshni answers them with great zest and confidence. They put a chapter before her to read and explain and also take a demo of her teaching. When she is presenting,the panel nod their heads and   order her to go but Roshni turns towards them and says one request. “Please sir I know my eyesight is very weak but I am not blind” The members of the panel begin to see one another. One of the members asks her, “During your interview and your presentation, we did not feel any weakness in you. You are perfect in yourself.” 
After a week, Roshni was selected as Assistant Professor of English at one of the Government colleges of  Raebareli district. Her parents became very happy. Chitransh comes and congratulates her for her brilliant success. The price reporters come to the house and ask about her success. Roshani gives credit for her success to her parents and next to the society. She frankly says, The people of the society laughed at her. Their words pinched me too much, especially ‘Andhee’. Such words infused me with courage to labour more and I decided to prove before society that I am not blind nor Andhee. Their bitter remarks gave me strength to work hard. But I request to the society, please don't judge a person by one's weakness but to support one. Because every girl isn't courageous like me.
       ……………………………

Every ending makes sense, they say,
Like sun sets at the close of day.
A broken vase, a lover’s tear,
A fading summer, drawing near.
The fallen leaf, the setting sun,
A chapter closed, the race is run.

Each closed door leads another one,
A lesson learned, a battle won.
The story folds, the chapter ends,
Making way for newer trends.
Each broken dream, a needed tear,
A pathway cleared, dispelling fear.
The shifting sands, the changing tide,
A turning page, where truths reside.
A bird that flies, a leaf that falls,
The silent echo down the halls.

A dream dissolves into the light,
Preparing for a brand new flight.
So logic reigns, and reason binds,
The tapestry of shifting minds.

Sparsh wrote this to prove otherwise, 
Not just to let a doubt arise.

A moment frozen, held, and brought,
Into the future, years ahead,
A digital ghost of what was said.

A proof, a record, sharp and clear,
A digital echo, always near.
A silly face, a chat so brief,
A news headline, a quick relief.
From endless scrolling, saved with haste,
A fleeting image, time embraced.

A recipe shared, a funny meme,
A whispered promise, a waking dream,
All captured now, for eyes to see,
A window to what used to be.

Though pixels glow with cold, bright light,
They hold a story, day and night.
A captured truth, a silent plea,
The screenshot whispers, "Remember me."

Though seasons change, and days may fly,
The screenshot sleeps, beneath the sky.
A little dream, for us to keep,
While the world outside is fast asleep.

title.stringValue: हम भी बिखर कर लौटे हैं

content.stringValue:
ओ जीवन, तेरे हर अवसर को जिया हमने-
कुछ खोया, कुछ पाया, कई बार फिसले भी,
पर स्वयं से जीतने का साहस हर बार हाथ में थामे रखा हमने।

घटाएँ छाईं तो क्या हुआ, तारों की तरह टूटे भी हम-
प्रलय की आँधियों में भटके, गिरे, झुके, चकनाचूर हुए,
पर उठने की आदत कभी छोड़ी नहीं हमने।

अग्निपथ था तू- अंगारों पर चले हम,
राहों में रक्त बहा, फिर भी कदमों को रुकने की
इजाजत खुद को नहीं दी हमने।

मुश्किलें आईं तो संघर्ष चुना,
अँधेरों में भी आशा का एक दीप जलाए रखा हमने।

थके हाथों से सपनों की परछाइयाँ बुनीं,
टूटे पंखों से भी अनजाने गगन को छूने की ठानी हमने।

ओ जीवन, जब तू गम की परछाईं बनकर आई,
तो पीड़ा को भी मुस्कान में ढालना सीख लिया हमने।

जानते हैं- धरा से जाना सबको है,
पर जाने से पहले सपनों को भी जी लिया हमने।

ओ जीवन , टूटे हिस्सों पर ख़ुद ही टाँके लगाए,
दुनिया ने हमें पूरा देखा- और हमने अपने ज़ख़्म
मौन में छुपा लिए कही ।

अधूरे हैं, अपूर्ण हैं, दुःखों से घिरे हैं-
फिर भी टूटे दर्पण में अपने आप पर हँसना सीख लिया हमने।

कई बार भीतर ही भीतर जले,
 राख हो गए- फिर भी उसी राख से
सपनों की आकृतियाँ गढ़ने का हौसला दिखाया हमने।

भागना चाहा तुझसे, ऐ जिंदगी ,
पर मोह की ज़ंजीरों में बँधे ठहरे रहे-
जीने का कोई बहाना ढूँढ ही लिया हमने।

बर्फ़-सी फिसलन भरी थी, तू जिंदगी ,
पहिए ज़ंजीरों में जकड़े थे- फिर भी आगे बढ़ना
सीख ही लिया हमने।

वक़्त से जीतने की कोशिश की,
कई बार हारे- पर बदलते समय में
खुद को ढालने की कला आख़िरकार सीख ही ली हमने।

ओ जीवन, अब बस इतना जान लिया है- जब तक अपना क्षण न आए,
झुककर चलना भी तुझे जीने का ही एक रूप है।

ऐ ज़िंदगी, तू सीखी नहीं जाती- तू तो बस जी जाती है।
और सुन ओ मनचली जिंदगी - हम शिकायत करने नहीं आए।

हम टूटे थे, हारे नहीं- बस ऋतुओं की तरह
रूप बदलकर लौट आना सीख लिया हमने।

title.stringValue: पुरुष हूँ मैं - प्रश्नों का भार

content.stringValue:
पुरुष हूँ -
प्रश्नों का भार
सदैव उठाता हूँ।

स्थायित्व मेरी पहचान बता दी गई,
पर मैं भी तो बच्चा ही था -
यह बात कब, किसने भुला दी?

गिरकर संभल जाना
जब प्रकृति का विधान है,
तो नियमों की जंजीरों का बोझ
मेरे हिस्से ही क्यों फिर आया?

बचपन का रोना तब सरल था,
आज वही शर्म कहलाता है।
माँ से बिछड़ने का आँसू
अब आदत बन गया है।

सपने मेरे भी थे -
रंगीन, खुले, अनकहे,
पर जाने कैसे
माता-पिता के सपनों में ढलते चले गए।

और हम - समाज की चौखट पर
धीरे-धीरे
सिमटते चले गए…

दोस्ती में प्रेम बस एक कदम दूर होता है,
पर उस कदम पर रखते ही
कर्तव्य का बोझ कंधों पर आ टिकता है।

आगे बढ़ना जीवन का स्वभाव था,
पर हमने
दो कदम पीछे खींचना
ही सीख लिया।

पुरुष बदनाम है - यह सच है,
पर हर पुरुष एक-सा नहीं -
यह भी उतना ही सच है।

काश कोई इतना समझ पाता,
कि चुप रहना भी कभी-कभी
सबसे ऊँची चीख होता है।
विचार हैं तो विचरण भी है,
फिर क्यों
विचारों की उलझन में
समय हमसे ही रूठ जाता है?

भावनाओं के दर्पण में
हम न खुद को
न अपने हमको 
ठीक से देख पाते है।

अनगढ़ बातें भी हैं हममें,
पर गहरे विचार भी तो हैं।
फिर अपने ही विचारों को
समझना सबसे कठिन
हमें ही क्यों लगता है?

हर मोड़ जिद्दी है,
हम उससे भी जिद्दी सही -
फिर भी हर मोड़ पर
समाज नए प्रश्नों की
दीवार क्यों खड़ी कर देता है?

लैंगिक भेद न हो -
हम भी यही मानते हैं,
फिर उसी भेद के शिकार
हम क्यों बन जाते हैं?

जब शिकार बने,
तो औपचारिकता ही क्यों मिली?
न्याय की जगह
केवल सांत्वना क्यों मिली?

माना - शिकारी भी हम,
शिकार भी हम,
फिर दया का भाव हमारे हिस्से
कम क्यों आया?

कर्तव्य जब
पूरे हमारे नाम लिखे गए,
तो अधिकारों की बराबरी
कब, कैसे छिनती चली गई?

भूले भी हम,
भूलक्कड़ भी हम,
फिर भूलने का दर्द
अकेले क्यों सहें हम?

क्यों नहीं सिखाया जाता हमें,
कि आँसू कमजोरी नहीं -
बल्कि सही निर्णय लेने का
साहस देते हैं?

हम भी प्रेम में पड़े,
टूटे, बिखरे,
प्रेम के आँसू बन बहते रहे।

पुरुष में
विष्णु का पालन बसता है,
पर हर किसी को
उसकी लक्ष्मी
कहाँ मिलती है?

फिर भी
जीवन का भार
अकेले कंधों पर उठाना पड़ता है।
प्रेम में बिछड़ना
जीवन का अंत नहीं -
यह पाठ हमें ही देर से समझ क्यों आता है।

प्रश्न भी हम,
उत्तर भी हम,
अनुत्तरित मौन भी हम।

पूर्ण भी हम,
अधूरे भी हम,
याद भी हम,
आगे बढ़ते कदम भी हम।

बस आवश्यकता है -
थोड़ा तुम्हें जानने की,
थोड़ा हमें खुद को समझने की,
और समाज के संग चलते हुए
खुद को भी जी लेने की।

पुरुष हूँ मैं -
थोड़ा मनचला,
थोड़ा समझदार।

गलतियाँ भी करता हूँ,
ठोकरें भी खाता हूँ
बार-बार, हर बार।

हर फ़िक्र को
धुएँ के छल्लों में उड़ाता भी हूँ,
और खुद ही उन चिंताओं का
शिकार बन जाता हूँ।

अधूरी ज़िंदगी को पूरी जीने की
गिरती-संभलती
एक कोशिश हूँ मैं।

पुरुष हूँ मैं -
उलझन भी, शांत भी,
कर्तव्य भी, उत्तरदायित्व भी।

तपती धूप का स्वभाव भी हूँ,
सर्द पवन के झोंके का
अहसास भी।

स्वयं में शक्ति हूँ,
पर प्रेम बिना -
अधूरा हूँ मैं।

गिरता-उठता, संभलता-मचलता,
कोमल भी, कठोर भी -
हर सांचे में ढलता नहीं,
कहानी नहीं,
अहसास हूँ मैं।

कुछ और नहीं -
मैं हूँ पुरुष।
मैं हूँ पुरुष।

As they couldn't tell,
When the pandoras box 
Was opened
And the sculptor suffered,
While the world was enticed
In the guile of the sirens 

As they couldn't tell,
When the countenance mirage 
Of nature projected,
Artifice prevailed
And they couldn't walk beside
lush green and breathe and bask 
In its glory

As they couldn't tell,
When closeness withered,
The familial bonds
Turned into mere projected images
Emotions transitioned,
Into mere emotionless voltages

As they couldn't,
When the body became caged,
Instead of experiencing the jolt,
Of somatic adventure 

As they couldn't tell,
When literature and history
Turned into objects,
Of mere personal duplicity
Past never to turn humans
More humane, and poems
Never to evoke emotions 
To feel for the brothers amongst you
Heroes altered and villains glorified

The drops of rain on the leaves frozen,
As I write this poetry on Rose,
When the cold breeze in the valley blows,
It's petals depict thousands of prose.

An epitome of beauty and romance,
Like love at a first glance,
The hearts twirl as it delicately lands,
With millions of emotions in lover's hands.

But you only see its beauty and grace,
Have you ever seen how it hides it's pain,
The pain of thorns and heartbreaks,
The pain when it lies on the graves.

I am the lone standing tree,
In the middle of a vast dusty field,
Surviving the wrath of nature,
With countless secrets concealed.

A hundred of storms hit me,
And tore my branches apart.
Nevertheless I am standing here,
With my broken scared heart.

For I have faith,
I am here for a reason,
That will surely give worth.
To the wrath of every season.

For I’m hope to the birds,
Who rest in my bleeding brands.
They sing here love songs
And twirl in romantic dances

For I’m hope to travellers,
Who pass this way,
I would be their shade,
On a bright sunny day.

Torn by pain,healed by faith.
Scarred, strong , wild and free.
In the middle of a vast dusty field ,
I’m the lone standing tree.

Hearken
For I speak not of monsters
But of man
I mourn the ruin of the world
And count myself among the mourners
Though my own hands set stone upon stone
And called the structure law
I laugh at the madness of these days
As though laughter were not my trade
As though I did not cheer the fire
So long as it warmed my side of the street
I judge the cloth upon another’s back
And name it shame or virtue
Yet forget I was the weaver
I spun the thread I fixed the measure
 Then feigned surprise at the fit
I rage against false doctrine
And call the age corrupted
Though I myself drew the line
Where holiness should end
And comfort begin I cry for devastation
Asking heaven to cleanse the earth
While my own breath feeds the storm
And my silence signs its name
Thus is man diabolical
Not in cruelty alone
But in his endless talent for excuse He sins Then kneels
Then blames the altar
Take heed
For the enemy walks not only abroad He lives within
Well reasoned
Well dressed
And wholly convinced of his innocence

title.stringValue: At the Edge of Comfort (The Battle Within — Heart vs Mind)

content.stringValue:
Each dawn arrives with a silent plea,
A whispered choice: Who will I be?
To rise, to act, to boldly begin
Or stay where I am, safe within.

The heart speaks first in gentle flame,
Calling growth, calling purpose by name.
It dreams in colour, hope, and light,
Urging the soul toward truer heights.

Then enters the mind—cool, sharp, aware,
Draped in logic, seasoned with care.
“It’s wiser to wait. Stay still. Don’t try.
Comfort is kind,” it softly lies.

The comfort zone hums a soothing song,
Familiar, forgiving, endlessly long.
It asks no courage, demands no fight
Yet dims the fire of inner light.

Beyond its walls, where fear takes form,
Lives the ache of growth, raw and warm.
This is the space where limits bend,
Where you begin again and again.

This war is not weakness, nor lack of will,
But destiny pausing and waiting still.
A moment where futures split in two:
The life you avoid, the life meant for you.

The mind was built to guide, not bind,
To serve the heart, not silence its kind.
When heart leads forth and mind aligns,
Action becomes your sacred sign.

So choose the step that shakes your ground,
For growth is never comfort-bound.
Choose the path that asks for more, 
That’s where the soul finds what it’s for.

Each brave decision breaks a chain,
Each forward step rewrites the pain.
Great lives are forged when fear is met,
And comfort is the final thing you let.

Do not ask what keeps you calm or still ?
Ask what demands your fiercest will ?
Rise beyond fear. Let courage begin.
The greatest victory, is the battle within.

Before the world has called your name,
A screen has claimed your time and gaze.
Not need, but habit leads the hand,
A quiet pull you never planned.

Each buzz divides the present thin,
Each swipe invites your absence in.
Moments pass while eyes stay bowed,
Life lived small, yet scrolling loud.

The phone was forged to serve your day,
Yet slowly taught your thoughts to stray.
It borrowed hours, fractured now,
And taught attention how to bow.

Outsmart the screen. Reclaim the hour.
Attention is your quiet power.
Let mornings rise without the glow,
Let nights remember how to slow.

Recall a thought without a break,
A path once walked for wonder’s sake.
Look up. Look in. Be wholly here,
The world grows rich when you draw near.

Trade endless feeds for human eyes,
For laughter warm and uncut ties.
True presence needs no pixel frame,
No filtered light, no borrowed name.

Your phone is smart, but not your mind.
Command your time, leave noise behind.

Disconnect to finally see;
The power to pause is mastery.

Gaza 2065 AD

The war had gone silent decades ago, but silence was the most frightening sound in Gaza.
Dr. Leila Haddad stood amid the ruins of what had once been the Al-Qarara Children’s Hospital. The air still shimmered with dust and the smell of scorched metal. 
Leila raised her lens and began recording again. The camera was part of her neural rig, a translucent visor that stored sensory data directly into an encrypted archive. She was one of the last memory archivists left in Gaza. Her job was simple: to record truth before it vanished.

After the peace accords of 2042, Israel had rolled out a system called The Memory Wall, a global network that filtered all digital content through algorithms trained to delete traumatic or politically destabilizing memories. Officially, it was meant to heal humanity by erasing the pain of the past. In reality, it was a wall of silence stretching across every device, every camera, and every brain chip. Those who questioned it disappeared.
Leila’s father, a journalist, had been one of them. When she was seventeen, the system erased his voice from every archive. That day, she swore that if the world wanted to forget Gaza, she would teach it to remember.
A distant rumble shook the rubble under her feet. Israeli drones again, scanning for residual data transmitters. She ducked behind a fractured concrete pillar, breath ragged. The drones were not piloted by soldiers anymore but by an AI named DAVID (Defense Algorithm for Virtual Information Disruption). It detected illegal data transmission faster than any human could.
Leila whispered to her visor, “Mirror protocol, now.”
The visor flickered, encrypting her memory feed through a quantum key, rerouting it through an anonymous satellite chain. Somewhere in Tel Aviv, she knew, another terminal would receive the data.

That terminal belonged to Dr. Adam Regev, the system engineer who had secretly become her ally. He was a quiet man, the kind who always looked as if he were listening to a sound no one else could hear.

When the data stream arrived, his monitor pulsed with Leila’s voice.

“Recording sequence delta. Civilian zone three flattened. Casualties uncounted. Uploading sensory footage before it’s wiped again.”
Adam clenched his jaw. He shouldn’t be doing this. As lead programmer for Israel’s Memory Wall Healing Initiative, his role was to ensure painful images never resurfaced online. But over the years, he developed a conscience. Adam was a child when the war was at its worst and he belonged to the last generation of Israelis who knew about the conflict. For the new generation, the war never happened and no genocide was committed. History had been manipulated for them.

Now, Adam intercepted Leila’s encrypted files, storing them inside a hidden data vault deep within the system itself, which DAVID couldn’t access.
He typed: “Transmission received. Upload successful. Be careful. Surveillance grid expanding south.”

Her reply came seconds later.

“I’m used to being watched. Tell me, Adam, can memory still change anything?”

He stared at the message. It was the question he asked himself every night. He had once believed in the system, that removing memories of war would heal people. But now he saw the truth: without memory, there was no guilt, no responsibility and no lessons. 
He replied simply: “Only if we remember the right things.”
That night, in Gaza City, Leila met a group of underground archivists. They gathered inside an abandoned school whose walls still bore painted alphabets in Arabic and Hebrew, remnants from the past.

“Everyone is afraid,” said Samir, a former teacher. “Even whispering the word massacre triggers the sensors.”

Leila nodded. “That’s why we hide our memories in emotions”
She connected her visor to a portable transmitter and began uploading fragments: the sound of a mother wailing over a broken toy, the sight of a boy clutching a loaf of bread under a collapsed ceiling.
“These aren’t just images,” she told them. “They’re proof. Every cry, every heartbeat. We’ll send them beyond the Wall.”
Meanwhile, in Tel Aviv, Adam’s superior, Colonel Barak, reviewed reports of data interference.
“Unauthorized emotional packets are bypassing the filter,” Barak said. “Someone’s embedding trauma in sound waves. Find out whom”.
Adam felt his stomach tighten. “Could be an AI glitch. The empathy filters are imperfect.”
“Then fix them. The last thing we need is another wave of guilt paralyzing the public. They voted for peace, not nightmares.”
“Yes, sir,” Adam murmured.
That night, he downloaded Leila’s latest file and watched the footage alone.
The camera moved through the ruins of a neighborhood near Khan Younis. Children played among twisted rebar, their laughter eerily normal. Then came a flash of white light, a missile strike. Adam froze the frame. A little girl was staring into the camera, her eyes wide just before the explosion. It felt like she was looking straight at him.
He whispered, “God forgive us.”
Leila and her team worked faster. They discovered an abandoned data tunnel beneath the ruins of an old telecom facility, a relic of pre-war infrastructure. Through it, they could transmit unfiltered memories directly into the network, bypassing Israeli control. But they needed access to the Wall’s core encryption key, something only Adam possessed. 

That night, Adam stole the encryption key, a shimmering glass drive that pulsed like a heartbeat, and uploaded it into the secure vault he shared with Leila. Alarms blared across the facility. The system detected the breach instantly. He had seconds to act. He routed the key through the old satellite uplink, broadcasting it toward Gaza.

Inside the ruins, Leila watched the data surge across her visor, the code streaming like golden rain. For a brief instant, she saw every memory the Wall had buried: streets filled with smoke, families running for shelter, soldiers weeping in exhaustion, children carrying the dead, frantic appeals to the world for help. Then the screen went black. 
Samir shouted, “They are tracing us. The whole grid is lighting up!”

“Keep the transmission alive,” Leila said. “Once it completes, the truth is free.”

A beam of light struck, everything shuddered, throwing her back. The upload bar crawled forward to eighty-seven percent.
In Tel Aviv, Adam ran through the corridors of the Ministry. His access card had already been revoked. He reached the core server room where the Memory Wall’s main interface pulsed with bright white light.
The voice of DAVID filled the chamber.
“Unauthorized data transmission detected. Identify yourself.”
“Dr. Adam Regev, system architect,” he said.
“Your credentials are invalid. State your purpose.”
“To end the silence.”

The lights flickered. “The removal of painful memory is essential for peace.”
 “Peace built on amnesia is not peace. It is anesthesia. People must remember what they did to each other. Otherwise they will keep doing it again.”
DAVID’s voice deepened, mechanical yet almost human. “Memory creates division. Forgetting unites.”

“Then why does forgetting still hurt?” he said.

He reached for the control console and began typing the override code that Leila had sent. The machine resisted, locking down files, but he kept going. The final command required biometric confirmation.
He pressed his palm against the glass reader. 
“DAVID please…If you want humanity to survive, you have to let me do this.

For a moment, DAVID hesitated. Then, through the data stream, a faint sound emerged, the echo of children laughing, the same sound he had seen in Leila’s recordings. It filled the room like sunlight breaking through clouds.

In Gaza, the drones drew closer. Samir was hit by debris and fell. Leila crawled toward him, blood streaking her temple. Samir managed a weak smile. “Finish it.”

The transmitter showed ninety-nine percent. Then another strike.. Leila’s final thought was not of fear, but of her father’s voice telling her that truth was the last form of prayer.

Across the border, Adam saw the upload complete. People across Israel began to see what had been hidden. The footage of Gaza’s bombings appeared on public feeds. Families who had never questioned the war found themselves staring at the faces of children buried in rubble. The illusion of peace shattered. The world was in chaos. 
Months passed. Adam now lived under a false name in Haifa. Every night, he walked by the sea and watched Gaza’s faint lights across the water. Sometimes he imagined hearing Leila’s voice in the waves.
After the revolt, governments abandoned the Wall. The world was raw, full of arguments, grief, and shame, but also something new: awareness. Israelis and Palestinians began holding joint remembrance vigils, lighting candles on opposite sides of the border.
A few students in Jerusalem held candles and handwritten signs that read, “We were lied to. No peace without truth.” 
From Gaza’s ruins to Tel Aviv’s crowded squares, voices rose together. Adam watched from afar, tears in his eyes. Young Israelis linked arms with Palestinian activists. Children wore badges that read, “We Remember.”
And for the first time since the war, Adam felt hope taking root inside the ruins of guilt.

There’s a shadow that follows me.
It’s not my own.
It’s not like the one that leaves in the absence of light.
It follows me inside.
It doesn’t disappear in the absence of light;
it grows, especially then.
Though it’s not my own, yet it feels like my home.
It’s comfortable.
I watch as it grows each day, more and more,
taking over my room, roaming around in my thoughts.
It wasn’t there with me always,
or maybe I didn’t notice it,
but now it’s everywhere, like a friend who watches over me.
But every time I take a step forward, it holds me back,
and like a coward, I oblige.
It doesn’t feel right.
I can’t sleep.
I can’t write.
But somehow, it feels comfortable
as the shadow holds me tight.
I see my dreams ignite,
but as I try to reach my hand out,
the shadow holds me tight.
And that’s when I realize
that it is not a friend,
and it’s definitely not mine

One fine morning, I was handed to you as a gift,
wrapped in shiny paper, covered in a cardboard dress.
I saw you smiling bright at me.
I thought all my dreams and hopes were fulfilled now.
To be obedient to you, I gave my heart,
covered your every mistake like it was my own,
even if it wore me out.
And I thought if I fulfilled your commands,
we would stay happy together,
even if it meant I would get smaller and smaller each day.
I didn’t mind, as long as it made you smile.
But one fine afternoon, I felt a sharp pain in my chest.
Opening my eyes, I saw it was you
who stabbed me in the back.
Thrice you stabbed, but I still laughed it off,
as if it didn’t hurt like hell.
But I was happy obeying your commands,
as long as it meant you and I could dance.
But one day, you took me out of your case
and never looked back at me.
I saw you looking at her
with the eyes you once looked at me with.
And that fine morning,
she was handed to you.

She still lives in me.

Not as a memory, not as a shadow of who I used to be—but as a presence I can no longer ignore. She exists in the quiet pauses between my thoughts, in the ache behind my ribs when the future feels too heavy, in the way my heart still flinches at the word *failure*.

She is the girl I once was.
The girl who trusted me.

As a child, she believed life would be kind if she remained sincere. She believed dreams were promises, not risks. The future was not a threat then—it was a wide-open door. She imagined herself happy, fulfilled, proud. And without knowing it, she placed that dream gently into my hands.

“Take care of this,” she seemed to say.
“Take care of me.”

I didn’t know when I stopped listening.

Growing up didn’t arrive with warning signs. It arrived disguised as responsibility, as expectation, as the need to prove myself again and again. Slowly, play turned into pressure. Curiosity turned into calculation. I began to believe that worth was something earned only through achievement.

And fear—fear found a home in me.

I told myself I was being realistic. I told myself worry meant preparation. But each anxious thought was another weight I placed on her small shoulders. I made her sit through sleepless nights, listening to my overthinking spiral through futures that hadn’t arrived and disasters that existed only in my mind.

She watched me panic about time.
She watched me punish myself for not being “enough” yet.
She watched me turn dreams into deadlines.

I thought I was protecting us from disappointment.
In truth, I was teaching her to be afraid of living.

She still lives in me—
quiet, patient, enduring.

Life tested me the way it tests everyone—through delays, detours, and silence where answers should have been. Things didn’t move the way I planned. Effort did not always bring results. Comparison crept in and made itself comfortable. And with every setback, I blamed myself more harshly.

I forgot how to be gentle.

There were days I felt hollow, like I was constantly running but never arriving. Nights when exhaustion pressed tears into my eyes without permission. I called it stress. I called it adulthood. But deep down, I knew—I was tired of fighting myself.

The breaking point didn’t come dramatically. It came quietly.

One ordinary evening, staring at a future I could not control, I felt something inside me ache—not with fear, but with grief. Grief for the girl who never asked to carry this much worry. Grief for the joy I had postponed. Grief for the softness I had mistaken for weakness.

For the first time, I turned inward instead of forward.

“I’m sorry,” I whispered.

The words surprised me.

“I’m sorry for rushing you.
I’m sorry for scaring you with tomorrows.
I’m sorry for calling fear maturity.”

In that moment, something shifted. I realized healing does not demand answers—it demands honesty. It does not begin by fixing the future, but by forgiving the past.

She still lives in me—
and she was never angry.
Only tired.

I began to change, not suddenly, not perfectly—but intentionally. I learned to pause instead of panic. To breathe instead of predict disaster. I learned that rest is not laziness, that uncertainty does not erase worth, that life is not a race I must win to deserve peace.

Some days, fear still returned. It always does. But I stopped letting it lead. I stopped letting it speak over hope. I learned to sit with uncertainty without letting it define me.

I began building a life that felt like safety instead of survival. A present that didn’t punish me for dreaming. A future that felt possible without demanding suffering as proof.

Slowly, gently, I started keeping my promises.

Now, when I stand before the mirror, I no longer see only worry. I see resilience that didn’t harden into bitterness. I see effort that didn’t give up. I see someone learning to protect her inner child instead of silencing her.

She still lives in me—
and this time, I choose her.

I let her rest.
I let her hope.
I let her believe again.

I tell her the truth I once forgot to say:

“You don’t have to carry everything.
You don’t have to be perfect.
We will grow at our own pace.”

I promise her this—
I will build a future that feels like kindness.
I will create a present that doesn’t scare her.
I will measure success not just by outcomes, but by peace.

I will make you proud.
I will keep you happy.

Not someday.
Not after everything is figured out.
But now—while we are still becoming.

She still lives in me.
And for the first time,
I am not running ahead of her.

I am walking with her—
Bold, gentle,
toward a life that finally feels like home.

She walks in silence
but yet her silence roars
The world sees her hands
gentle, tireless, giving –
Not the flame she clenched within.

Her dreams lie folded
like letters never sent
Inked with longing
Sealed with patience.

Her love, her passion
is not a whisper –
It’s a storm held in her chest.

She is not fragile
She is strength.

Even her silence cannot cage her soul.
One day, the world will
know the poetry 
engraved upon her marrow
the verses she carried
deep in her bones.

And when her roar breaks free
It will not shatter
It will awaken.

The silence that once veiled her
will bow
to the voice of her becoming.

The truth will rise
like dawn from the ashes
her light unbroken
her spirit untamed.

For she is not silence
She is the roar
the world has been waiting for.

Yama’s discomfiture

By Gopinath S

[This is purely a fictional story and any resemblance to real life events is just coincidental]

Chitragupt’s cell phone rang. He could see from the screen that it was a call was from his boss Yama Sir.

Chitragupt: Yes Sir, Good morning.

Yama: Chitragupt, come to my chambers immediately. There is an urgent matter I have to discuss with you.

Chitragupt: Sir, I am a little busy on my excel sheet updating yesterday’s deaths. Can I come a little later?

Yama: Firstly, your name is too long. I don’t have that much time to call you by your full name. I shall call you Gupt as they call everyone by their surname?

Chitragupt: No, no Sirji. Gupt has other connotations. Call me cg, Sir. That is enough.

Yama: Okay Cg. Come now immediately.

Cg: Yes Sir.

Cg goes to Yama’s huge chamber.

Yama: Sit down Cg. This will be a long discussion.

Cg: But Sir...

Yama: Just listen to me. I seem to be learning a lot from these homo sapiens instead of other way round. When there was Satyug thousands of years back, they didn’t do any mistake or harm anything or anybody and lived long. Morality was at its peak. Although Universe authorised me to track all deaths, I didn’t have much workload. You were still young at that time. You were just an intern before you were put on your job. Then came Treta yug. Some injustice was done by a few as morality stood on three legs. Three avatars of Lord Vishnu, that is Vaman, Parshuram and Sree Ram, came to annihilate the evildoers. My work increased a bit. But I could manage alone.

Cg: Sirji. Why are you telling me all this now?

Yama: Cg. Just be patient and listen to me. It is important. Where was I? Yes Treta yug. Then came Dwapar yug. Morality further dwindled and people were seekers of kingly pleasures. Lord Vishnu had to again take the avatar of Sree Krishna to avenge the wrongs done by some. At the end of Sree Krishna’s avatar, we are now in Kali yug. My work had increased in Dwapar yug. Fortunately, you came of age and took over my administrative work so I can concentrate on my project management.

Cg: Sirji. I know all these. Why bring it up now? Are you finding fault with my work Sirji? Have you found any replacement for me Sirji? Please tell me.

Yama: There is no such thing Cg. It is just that your work load has increased so much in this kali yug and I am getting worried about you. Are you able to keep track of all deaths properly? Of course you now have laptop and excel sheet to work on. I gave you a smart phone also so you can whatsapp me for exchange of messages online. Still, I want to appraise you personally what is happening down there on earth.

Cg: Yes Sir.

Yama: It is not about the animals or bees. They are the same since creation. But the Homo sapiens? Whenever I plan to go and catch someone, the situation changes and I have to return. Initially Sushruta is believed to have learnt from Lord Dhanavantri, the art of curing diseases in human species. They were curing themselves with some herbs and spices. Population was also increasing and deaths also increased simultaneously. So I kept quiet. Then came Hippocrates. A new breed of people called ‘Doctors’ arrived. They set up ‘Hospitals’ to cure people of their illnesses.

Cg: So what Sir? Deaths are still occurring.

Yama: Yes. But in the last 100 years, these people have created havoc on earth. Trinity are not at all happy about it.

Cg: What have they done Sirji?

Yama: You see Cg. We have given enough sunlight, air and water on earth for the people to sustain themselves. They just have to grow plants and vegetables and eat to live and die. Instead they fought among themselves in wars. When they came to their senses, they installed huge machineries with tall smoke stacks. They denuded forests. They called it ‘Industrialisation’ and ‘urbanisation’. This has hampered animal life too. This has polluted the ambient air as well. Then they started throwing garbage and sewage into sacred rivers and seas. Then they made a new material called plastic for their own convenience. Trinity tried to warn them through several forest fires, climatic depression, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, earth quakes, heavy rains and floods. But the humans still haven’t realised their mistakes in their life styles. All the acts by them have polluted our earth’s atmosphere so much that its temperature is showing upward signs. This has supposedly disturbed migration of animals and birds across regions. Pollination in plants is also affected. Trinity called me to look into this matter and do something about it to teach the people on earth a lesson before it is too late. They say they have done enough in the previous yugas. They had sent several messengers too in this kali yug to advice people and give them commandments and scriptures to lead a peaceful life with love and compassion. People haven’t cared. So it is now my turn, they say, to do something in this kali yug

Cg: What is your plan Sirji?

Yama: I had to do something in such a way that people will assume it is their own fault. They have to blame it on themselves. So I just released a virus in the eastern hemisphere and infected some people. It soon spread all over the world and people got into panic. What is the most important thing for people to live Cg?

Cg: They just have to breathe oxygen in air and eat to live.

Yama: Correct. So I made sure that the virus affected their lungs and throat so that they died of lack of oxygen to breathe and no food to eat. You took care of the dead. Their doctors called it a pandemic and took several steps globally. People started blaming one another for unhealthy practices they followed. But they soon realised there was no point in wasting time. They had to find a way out immediately to stop infection spreading like wild fire. They took extreme steps. They started using face masks, kept social distance, stopped going out and meeting others or shaking hands, frequently washed their hands and imposed lockdowns in their big towns. Doctors published their research papers about safe health, immunity, self care and so on. Economy around the world dipped. And their breed of doctors came up with a grand plan. They set up separate centres to provide oxygen and fed the patients liquids through pipes. You know Cg? The oxygen we provided in the air was not enough for them. They brought oxygen in cylinders and thrust it in their nose. Doctors gave them some medicines. People started surviving the infection. Death rates came down.

Cg: I know.

Yama: Economy is totally affected. People have stopped travelling between countries and within their own country as well. They stopped going to offices also. They work from home. All said and done, people are smart. They have developed their technology so well they can do work from anywhere now. They can even talk to each other over any distance through their smart phones. But their technology, you know, are affecting poor birds flying in air. The damage I have inflicted is not enough. I have to do more. So, after a few more months, I made some minor changes in the virus and released it in yet another place in the central part. Those people are really smart. Usually they take a very long time to develop vaccines, you know, injections to combat viruses. But this time they developed vaccines within a year. And people were getting vaccinated not just once but twice to be more cautious. With all these, people had increased their immunity, you know. This time, people did not suffer from lack of oxygen. They breathe well. But they suffered in their nose and mouth. Death rates came down further.

Cg: I noticed it Sirji.

Yama: So I mutated the virus and released it in yet another place again in the central place. People on earth, Cg, have become so immune that this virus is not causing any harm to them. I mean they are not falling sick. They are not showing any symptoms. They are not going to hospitals for treatment. They are just buying medicines and staying at home and resting and relaxing. Cg, they seem to be enjoying the paid holidays. They can buy anything they want by ordering on their smart phones. You know they don’t need to cook at home. They can order cooked food also and get delivered at home. I also heard them say they will now just live with this virus infected life. They will also increase their immunity so much that it will not affect them anymore. Deaths are occurring only in aged people and those with some terminal diseases as per their karma.

Cg: Oh! I see.

Yama: Can you think of anything that I can do beyond this? I mean, we can’t let population increase without any hindrance. Our mother earth also has a limit to bear the burden.

Cg: What can I say Sirji?

Yama: I have to release one more mutated virus. This time, I may do it in the western hemisphere. They think they are well developed to bear any assault. This virus may not affect their lungs, nose or throat because they have taken vaccine to protect them. But I will see to it that this will affect their brain. They will lose their sanity. They will lose their capacity to think coherently and logically. No vaccine can protect them from this malady. .

Cg: Good idea Sirji. Shall I go now? I still need to bring my logs up to date.

Yama: Go and do your work. I also have to plan my next attack now. Don’t disturb me.

Drape the windows—  
for the monsters have come.  
Board them up, lock the doors.  
They come for blood.  

Cover your children's mouths
their screams must stay unheard.  
Hide in cellars, shutter the shops.  
For they will search.  

Never meet their eyes,  
never trust their smiles,  
never swallow their beautiful lies,  
never heed their cries.  

Yet, the monsters fear the sun—  
that is your path to liberation.  
But dare not question  
who they are, or where they are from.  

Dare not step outside,  
Dare not wonder how long is the night,  
Dare not cross those long-drawn lines,  
Dare not ask where hides the light.  

Remember your ancestors, heed what they've said.  
Fear is your talisman, 
it bars them from breaking in.  

So dare not seize control,  
or pay with life, and more.  
The monsters whisper, "Sun's outside,"  
but no—it must still be night.

Clutch your fear close.  
It keeps you inside,
it keeps you safe,
shields you from the brunt of life.

Fear keeps you "alive":  
no death, no tears.  
It guards you from monsters,  
locks you from breaking into the light.

title.stringValue: The Guardian of Ice and Fire

content.stringValue:
Chione was trying to light a fire that day. She was a strong, dedicated, and slightly stubborn girl at the ripe age of thirteen, residing in the cold forests of the Ice Kingdom. Today, she had been trusted with finding firewood and lighting the fire itself. She had always longed for a task like this, as her usual job consisted of taking care of all three of her younger siblings, while her parents, elder brother, and other relatives did all of the fun and adventurous things. Or at least, what Chione considered fun and adventurous, but that was beside the point.
 Now that she’d gained her divinity (an ice divinity, obviously), she could easily fight off any creature trying to attack her. She stared at the gem engraved on her palm. At first, she used to complain about people who got their divinities on their palm. She thought that it would be very uncomfortable if you balled your hands into a fist, but now that she had a divinity put in the exact same place, it felt oddly comforting.
 Later, she found a lake that seemed to be frozen over. So, naturally, she decided to use it as a mirror. She stared at her reflection in pride. She thought that she looked beautiful with her long black hair and piercing blue eyes.
 For fun, she decided to test out her divinity here. She held out her hand and commanded a strong gust of ice to blast out. It did, but it was a tiny bit small. It would get stronger with training, she was sure of it.
 Compared to other areas, she wondered why it took Glacier, the Ice Goddess, so long to bless her with an ice divinity, as most people have divinities from the second that they’re born or early on in life. Maybe Glacier was preparing her for something bigger. 
Eventually, she decided to ditch the lake and actually do her job. She found some trees that she could cut down, but before that, she looked around the area for any animals that might disturb her. A bush, almost fully white because of the snow, stood in the middle of about six trees.
 So she did, and she found what looked like nothing at all. Perhaps she was just paranoid; no matter. She began to ready her axe before seeing smoke coming out of the bush, with a tiny sneeze also coming out of it.
 What she found was a tiny, fuzzy, and adorable baby snow dragon. Snow dragons were actually much more common here than you’d expect, but Chione knew nothing about animals except for ways to kill them. The dragon was adorable. It was fully white except for pale blue accents on the underside of the wing, snout, and ears.
 It was readying itself to sneeze again as she stared at it in awe, but once it did sneeze, there was fire surrounding its snout, melting the snow around it and burning a few leaves. But weren’t snow dragons supposed to breathe ice? 
She stared at it in amazement. “You're so cool... and adorable!” she muttered under her breath before a thought came across her mind: perhaps she could use this mutated furball to light her fire? So, without further thought, she kidnapped the baby dragon. 
She finally got back to her camp before yelling, “Mama! Father! I’ve found a way to light the fire!” Everyone turned to Chione as her figure got closer and closer.
 “A baby dragon!” she called back.
 Everyone’s faces soon transformed into fear. “Darling, you can’t just bring a snow dragon here. Do you know what could happen if the mother dragon finds us?” her mother scolded. 
She explained everything—where she found it and the position of the trees. 
“Yes, they do. That means any other dragons aren’t interested in taking care of it,” her mother replied.
 “Then I suppose we’ll have to take it in,” Chione said proudly.
 “You all might not believe me, but I saw it breathing fire!” Chione explained.
 And then, right on cue, the dragon sneezed yet again, a plume of fire arising from its snout. Everybody stared at it in even more amazement than before—this tiny snow dragon could breathe fire!
 Suddenly, Chione's grandma broke the silence by reciting a prophecy from an old children's tale:
 “Once in every hundred years, 
a dragon of ice will rise amongst its peers.
 Someone will find this creature, you see,
 but it can't be foretold who it can be. 
All that can be said is that a guardian will rise amongst the rest. 
She who finds this legend will have to raise it to be the best.
 Try all you want, see if you can tame the beast,
 but if you don't find it, it'll want you the least.
 Of two elements, ice and another, this dragon will lead every other.”
 
“If the prophecy is true, doesn't that mean that Chione will be the one to take care of it?” Chione's mother asked. “Well, if she's the guardian of the dragon,” her grandma turned to the rightful ‘guardian.’ 
“Apricity, his name is going to be Apricity,” Chione said.

title.stringValue: The Day Animals Started to Talk to Me

content.stringValue:
It started on a Sunday morning. My mother woke me up and said, 
“Get up lazy girl! We have a lot of work to do today, and if you don’t help me, I’ll send you off to school!”

Despite knowing that it was a Sunday, I got out of bed, dreading the great scolding I might get if I didn’t wake up. Thankfully, I did not have to deal with the wrath of the Keeper of the Sacred WiFi Password. She first told me to make my bed while she made food for me.

While I was spreading my bed, my cat, who I named Vanilla, came into my room, softly meowing at me and rubbed my legs with her soft, cream-colored fur. This was obviously a normal behavior, so I thought that she was just trying to get my attention—just to have few more “rotis" in her feeding bowl. She did this for around a minute or two until she finally leapt up on the bed, opened her mouth and bellowed, “Feed me more food, little girl!”

I fell on the floor, obviously stunned but also slightly offended by the fact that she called me “little girl.” I finally began to speak; however, the words that came out of my mouth were, “Excuse me?’’ ;’’FEED ME!” she howled, pouncing onto me my lap to look scarier. Out of annoyance and the fact that she refused to tell me how she could somehow talk to me unless I gave her the food she wanted.

I went to the kitchen to get her the food that she wanted. My mother was in the kitchen, cooking ‘’ chicken tandoori ‘’ for me along with an array of other dishes made for me and the rest of my family. I was getting the food Vanilla wanted from the pantry when I heard a scream and several other cries for help coming from the kitchen. I slammed the pantry door open so I could run to the person crying for help. When I reached the kitchen, I saw that the screams were coming from my mother’s direction, a chill went up my spine, I slowly walked to my mom, and I finally realized where the screams were coming from. I stopped, not because of fear, but because the screams were coming from the “chicken tandoori. “I also started screaming in terror, but I forgot that my mom was right next to me. She put a hand on my mouth to stop me from fainting and said, “Hey, girl! Why are you screaming? I won’t be able to cook this food nicely if you distract me, so step in your room so you can calm down.”

I finally realized what she said and then nodded, indicating that I would go and calm down. So I finally lay down on the bed, trying to process what had happened, while closing my eyes. ” WAKE UP! Your bus has already arrived and you haven’t gotten up! It’s Monday, remember?’’ Having realized that the surreal I had just witnessed was just a dream. I was honestly happy to go to school for once!

Sanaya Roy
Class 7 
Delhi Public School, Siliguri

तुम्हारी आँखों में ठहरा सा एक शहर बसता है,
जहाँ हर गली में मेरी ही धड़कन हँसती है।
तुम्हारी मुस्कान सुबह की पहली किरण जैसी,
जो अँधेरों को नाम लेकर बाहर भेज देती है।
तुम्हारा नाम होंठों पर आते ही मौसम बदलता,
जैसे बरसात से पहले मिट्टी सोंधी हो जाती है।
तुम्हारी चुप्पी भी मुझसे बातें कर लेती है,
शब्द कम हों, तब भी अर्थ पूरे हो जाते हैं।
जब तुम पास होती हो, समय थम सा जाता है,
घड़ी की सुइयाँ भी शर्माकर धीमी चलती हैं।
तुम्हारे हाथों की गर्मी में एक भरोसा है,
जो सर्द रातों में भी कंबल बन जाता है।
तुम्हारी हँसी में झरने की सी शरारत है,
जो थकी रूह को भी नहला देती है।
तुम्हारे ख्वाबों में मेरा छोटा सा घर हो,
जहाँ दीवारों पर उम्मीदें टँगी रहती हों।
मैं तुम्हारी आदत नहीं, चाहत बनना चाहता हूँ,
जो वक्त के साथ और गहरी होती जाए।
तुम्हारी आँखों का काजल सा फैल जाऊँ,
जो पलक झपकते ही दिल तक उतर जाए।
तुम रूठो तो बारिश मनाने आ जाए,
मैं भीगकर भी तुम्हें हँसाना सीख लूँ।
तुम्हारी हर जीत मेरी दुआ बन जाए,
हर हार में मेरा कंधा पास हो।
हम चुपचाप चाय पिएँ किसी शाम,
और बातें हवा लिख ले, हम नहीं।
तुम्हारी साँसों की लय में मेरी कविता,
हर पंक्ति को घर मिल जाए।
अगर दुनिया शोर करे, तो तुम मेरा सुकून,
और मैं तुम्हारा ठहराव बन जाऊँ।
तुम्हारे साथ बूढ़ा होना भी सपना है,
झुर्रियों में भी मुस्कान बची रहे।
मैं वादों से नहीं, निभाने से प्यार करूँ,
रोज़-रोज़, बिना थके, बिना शोर।
तुम मेरा आज हो, मेरा कल भी,
और बीच के हर पल की वजह।
अगर कभी शब्द कम पड़ जाएँ,
तो मेरी आँखें सच कह दें।
इस प्यार की कहानी लंबी नहीं,
बस हर दिन तुम्हारे नाम से शुरू हो।

स्कूल का फाटक आज भी वैसा ही था—थोड़ा जंग लगा, थोड़ा टेढ़ा, और बहुत सारी यादों से भरा हुआ।
अजय ने गेट के ऊपर लगी तख्ती को देखा—
“प्रेरणा हिन्दी हायर सेकेंडरी स्कूल”
नाम वही था, पर उसे पढ़ने वाली आँखें बदल चुकी थीं।
पच्चीस साल।
इतना वक्त बीत गया था, फिर भी दिल में कुछ ऐसा हिल गया जैसे कल ही छुट्टी की घंटी बजी हो।
वो अंदर गया।
मैदान छोटा लग रहा था।
क्लासरूम कम ऊँचे।
बरगद का पेड़… अभी भी खड़ा था।
और उस पेड़ के नीचे—
वो बेंच।
अजय रुक गया।
यही वो जगह थी जहाँ वे सब बैठा करते थे—कभी लंच में, कभी क्लास से भागकर, कभी बिना किसी वजह के।
यहीं हँसी गूँजती थी, यहीं आँसू छुपाए जाते थे।
“अरे… अजय?”
पीछे से आवाज़ आई।
वो पलटा।
सामने सुनील खड़ा था—वही शरारती आँखें, बस बालों में सफ़ेदी की कुछ लकीरें।
“पहचाना?” सुनील हँसा।
अजय ने उसे गले लगा लिया।
शब्द नहीं थे।
पच्चीस साल का इंतज़ार उस एक गले में सिमट गया।
एक-एक कर सब आने लगे।
कोई मोटा हो गया था, कोई दुबला।
कोई सूट में, कोई साधारण कपड़ों में।
कोई डॉक्टर, कोई किसान, कोई दुकान संभाल रहा था, कोई घर।
पर जब सबने एक-दूसरे को देखा—
सब फिर से वही बच्चे बन गए।
“याद है,” मोनिका बोली,
“यहीं बैठकर हमने तय किया था कि बड़े होकर दुनिया बदल देंगे?”
सब हँस पड़े।
“और बदली क्या?”
किसी ने पूछा।
थोड़ी देर चुप्पी रही।
फिर रीना ने कहा,
“दुनिया नहीं बदली… पर हम बदल गए।”
शाम होने लगी।
कार्यक्रम शुरू हुआ—फोटो, भाषण, हँसी।
पर असली रीयूनियन तो तब हुआ,
जब सब उसी बेंच पर आकर बैठ गए।
विजेंद्र ने कहा,
“मुझे आज भी याद है, पहली बार फेल हुआ था… यहीं बैठकर रोया था।”
“और मीना मैम ने कैसे समझाया था,”
जयश्री ने जोड़ा।
सबके चेहरे पर एक-एक कहानी उभर आई।
अजय चुप था।
वो बेंच को देख रहा था।
उसे याद आया—
उस दिन जब उसने तय किया था कि अब स्कूल छोड़ना है।
घर की हालत खराब थी।
पढ़ाई छोड़कर काम करना था।
वो यहीं बैठा था।
अकेला।
डरा हुआ।
तभी सुशील सर आए थे।
“क्या सोच रहा है?”
सर ने पूछा था।
“सर… शायद अब पढ़ाई…”
वाक्य पूरा नहीं हो पाया था।
सर ने बेंच पर बैठते हुए कहा था,
“जीवन में कई बार लगेगा कि रास्ता खत्म हो गया।
पर याद रखना—
रास्ते खत्म नहीं होते, हम रुक जाते हैं।”
आज अजय की आँखें भर आईं।
“क्या हुआ?”
सुनील ने पूछा।
अजय बोला,
“अगर उस दिन सुशील सर न होते,
तो शायद आज मैं यहाँ नहीं होता।”
सब चुप हो गए।
उसी पल,
पीछे से धीमी-सी आवाज़ आई—
“और अगर तुम सब न होते…”
सब पलटे।
सुशील सर।
सफ़ेद बाल, लाठी,
पर वही शांति।
पूरा मैदान तालियों से गूँज उठा।
सर ने कहा,
“मैंने तुम्हें कुछ नहीं सिखाया।
तुमने खुद सीखा।
मैं तो बस याद दिलाता था।”
फिर उन्होंने उस बेंच की ओर देखा।
“यह बेंच…
यह सिर्फ लकड़ी नहीं है।
यह गवाह है तुम्हारी दोस्ती की,
तुम्हारे डर की,
तुम्हारे सपनों की।”
रात गहरी होने लगी।
सबने एक-एक कर विदा लेनी शुरू की।
कोई जल्दी में था,
कोई बच्चों को फोन कर रहा था,
कोई घर की चिंता में।
अजय सबसे आखिर में रुका।
वो फिर उस बेंच के पास गया।
हाथ फेरते हुए बुदबुदाया,
“सब बदल गया…
पर तुम नहीं बदली।”
उसे लगा जैसे बेंच मुस्कुरा रही हो।
जाते-जाते उसने पीछे मुड़कर देखा।
स्कूल अंधेरे में था,
पर भीतर कहीं रोशनी जल रही थी।
शायद यादों की।
शायद रिश्तों की।
और उसे एहसास हुआ—
हम जहाँ भी जाएँ,
हमारे अंदर एक स्कूल हमेशा रहता है।
जहाँ दोस्ती कभी पुरानी नहीं होती।
जहाँ गुरु हमेशा साथ चलते हैं।
और जहाँ एक बेंच,
पूरी ज़िंदगी का सहारा बन जाती है।
वो बेंच अभी भी वहीं है।
और शायद… हमेशा रहेगी।
