THE NIGHT MY FAITH WAS TESTED IN SILENCE

content.stringValue:
Title
The Night My Faith Was Tested in Silence
Subtitle
A true story of belief, fear, and an unanswered mystery that strengthened my faith
The Night My Faith Was Tested in Silence
My name is Saurabh Gautam, and this is a true story from my life—one that I have never shared with anyone, not even my family. I am sharing it now because the theme is “Real Story”, and this incident is as real as my breath, as real as my fear that night, and as real as my faith today.
I belong to a Hindu family. I was born into Hindu traditions, festivals, prayers, and customs. My family respects all religions, and from childhood, I was taught that God is one, though people call Him by different names. As I grew older, my understanding of faith changed. I did not abandon my roots, nor did I disrespect them. Instead, my faith expanded.
Over time, I found myself deeply connected to Jesus Christ. I chose Jesus as my Guru, my guide, my protector—not because someone forced me, not because I was influenced, but because my heart found peace there. For me, Jesus is not limited to a religion; He is a presence, a comfort, a strength that holds me together when my mind is heavy and my heart is restless.
In my hometown, I regularly visit a church. I go quietly, respectfully, and with humility. I do not go to convert anyone or to prove anything. I go there to pray, to sit in silence, and to feel protected. Whenever I am stressed, anxious, or mentally disturbed, I find relief in prayer.
The pastor of that church is a man I deeply respect. I will not disclose his name, not because I fear anything, but because he deserves privacy and dignity. He is intelligent, honest, calm, and deeply committed to helping others. What I admire most about him is that he never asks for money. Whenever someone comes to him in pain—mental, emotional, or spiritual—he helps without expecting anything in return.
Many times, when I go to church, I notice people who seem… different. Some cry uncontrollably. Some scream. Some collapse. Some speak in strange voices. The pastor and his team pray for them patiently. Over time, those people calm down. I do not fully understand these things, and I never try to judge them. I just observe silently.
Whenever I feel stressed, I simply request the pastor to pray for me. He always does. He never asks why, never questions my belief, never judges my background. That itself is a blessing.
I am a normal person with normal habits. I like reading, learning new things, and watching movies. I especially enjoy Hollywood movies, mostly because of their storytelling and visuals. What happened one particular night changed the way I look at silence, fear, and faith forever.
That Night
It was a normal day. I had gone to church, prayed, and returned home. There was nothing unusual about the day. No arguments, no stress, no bad news. After dinner, I decided to watch a movie on my laptop.
I honestly do not remember the movie’s name. I only remember that it was a Hollywood movie, and it was late. I started watching it around 11:00 PM. My room door was locked from inside, as it usually is. My laptop was plugged into the main switch. Everything was normal.
Sometime between 11:00 PM and 1:00 AM, I fell asleep while watching the movie. This was not unusual for me. Many times, I fall asleep with the laptop on my bed. I clearly remember the movie still playing when my eyes closed.
The next thing I remember is waking up suddenly around 4:00 AM.
What I saw froze my body.
My laptop was closed.
The charging wire was unplugged from the main switch.
And most terrifying of all—
My room door was open.
For a few seconds, I did not move. I did not breathe properly. My heart was beating so fast that I could hear it in my ears. My mind started racing.
I was alone in my room.
I had locked the door.
I had not woken up in between.
No one had entered my room.
No one had a key.
Then how?
Who closed my laptop?
Who unplugged the charger?
Who opened the door?
There were no signs of theft. Nothing was missing. No noise had woken me up. The house was silent.
Fear slowly wrapped around me like a cold blanket.
The Fear I Could Not Explain
I am not an easily frightened person. I believe in logic. I believe in science. But that morning, logic had no answers.
I checked the latch. It was fine.
I checked the switchboard. It was intact.
I checked my phone—no calls, no messages.
I tried to convince myself that maybe I did it unknowingly. But deep inside, I knew that was not true. I am a light sleeper. I always remember waking up, even briefly. That night, there was no memory at all.
I sat on my bed for a long time, unable to think clearly. I did not scream. I did not run. I did not call anyone. I just sat there, silent and afraid.
For the first time in my life, I felt a kind of fear that had no shape, no sound, no explanation.
Why I Told No One
I did not tell my family.
I did not tell my friends.
I did not even tell the pastor.
Why?
Because some experiences are too personal, too fragile to be spoken aloud. I feared that people would laugh. I feared they would dismiss it as imagination. I feared that if I spoke about it, the fear would grow stronger.
Instead, I chose silence.
I prayed.
I did not ask God to explain it.
I did not ask Jesus for answers.
I only asked for protection.
And slowly, the fear faded.
Faith Without Answers
That incident remains a mystery to this day. I still do not know what happened that night. I do not try to interpret it as a miracle or as something evil. I do not claim it was supernatural. I also do not deny that it could have been something beyond my understanding.
What I do know is this:
That night taught me that faith does not always come with explanations.
Sometimes, faith means trusting even when you do not understand. Sometimes, protection is silent. Sometimes, God does not speak—He simply watches.
After that night, my belief in Jesus did not weaken. It became calmer, deeper, more mature. I stopped asking for signs. I stopped seeking proofs. I started valuing peace.
I still go to church.
I still pray.
I still respect my Hindu roots.
I still believe God is one.
And I still remember that night—not with fear, but with humility.

What This Story Means to Me
I am not sharing this story to scare anyone. I am not sharing it to prove anything. I am sharing it because real life is full of moments that do not fit into logic, religion, or science neatly.
Some experiences exist only to remind us that we are not in complete control.
That night did not give me answers.
It gave me faith without conditions.
And sometimes, that is enough.
Conclusion
If you ask me today whether I am afraid of that incident, my answer is no. I am grateful that nothing harmful happened. I am grateful that I was protected. I am grateful that my faith was tested—and survived.
Some stories remain mysteries forever.
Some prayers are answered silently.
Some doors open for reasons we may never know.
This was one such night in my life.
And this is my real story.

✍️লিপিকা দাস

"ছেহঃ গাড়ীখন এতিয়াহে বেয়া হ'ব পাইছিল নে..!!"-- মুখতে ভোৰভোৰাই তাই গাড়ীৰ পৰা নামিল । বাহিৰত তেতিয়া দোপালপিটা বৰষুণ জাকে গোটেই অঞ্চলটো ধুই নি আছিল । ঘোপ মৰা অন্ধকাৰত চকুৰে একোৱে মণিব নোৱাৰা অৱস্থা । মবাইলৰ ফ্লেছ লাইট জ্বলাই তাই গাড়ীৰ চকাটোলৈ পোহৰ মাৰি পঠালে । 
"Oh Shit!!"-- গাড়ীৰ আগৰ সোঁফালৰ চকাটো ফুটি থাকিল । অফিচ ট্যুৰৰ পৰা ওভতাৰ পথত মাজনিশা এইদৰে ফচি যাবলগীয়া হ'ব বুলি তাই ভাবিব পৰা নাছিল । কি কৰা যায় বাৰু এতিয়া..!! ক'ত কটাব তাই এই বর্ষাসিক্ত অন্ধকাৰ নিশাটো..!! ইফালে-সিফালে চাই পঠিয়ালে তাই । ফ্লেছ লাইটৰ পোহৰত জিলিকি উঠিল বেনাৰ এখন । "Hotel Dark Fantasy- Fooding and Lodging" ।
"উফ ৰক্ষা । ৰাতিটো ইয়াতেই মূৰ গুজিব লাগিব কোনোমতে । এতিয়া আৰু পলম কৰি লাভ নাই ।"-- ভেনিটি বেগটো মূৰৰ ওপৰত ধৰি তাই হোটেলৰ ফালে দৌৰিবলৈ ধৰিলে । দুপৰ নিশা ও হোটেলৰ মূল দুৱাৰখন খোলা থকা কথাটো তাইৰ তেতিয়া মন কৰিব পৰা কৈ শক্তি নাছিল । বৰষুণত তিতি জুৰুলি-জুপুৰি হোৱা তাই  নিশাটোৰ বাবে ৰুম এটা বিচাৰি হোটেল মেনেজাৰৰ ওচৰ চাপিল । প্ৰতিকূল বতৰৰ বাবেই কাৰেণ্টৰ দেখাদেখি নাই বুলি মেনেজাৰে তাইক জনাইছিল যদিও এন্ধাৰৰ বাবেই মেনেজাৰৰ মুখখন স্পষ্টকৈ দেখা তাইৰ নহ'ল। 
"তিমিৰ, এইফালে আহ । বাইদেউক তেওঁৰ ৰূমটো দেখাই দে গৈ ।"-- ম'ম এডাল হাতত লৈ কৃষ্ণকায় ল'ৰা এজন আগুৱাই আহিল । 
"আহক বাইদেউ ।"-- তাইক বাট দেখুৱাই ল'ৰাজন আগুৱাই গৈ থাকিল । বৰষুণৰ বাবে বতৰটো ঠাণ্ডা, তাতে আকৌ বৰষুণত তিতা বাবেই তাইৰ বেছ ঠাণ্ডা লাগিছে । বাহু দুখন হাতেৰে পিহি পিহি তাই তাক অনুসৰণ কৰি থাকিল ।
"এইটো আপোনাৰ ৰুম বাইদেউ । আলমিৰাত কাপোৰ আছে কেইযোৰ মান । আপুনি পিন্ধিব পাৰিব । আপুনি চেঞ্জ কৰি লওঁক, মই আপোনাৰ বাবে গৰম চাহ একাপ লৈ আহি আছোঁ । আপোনাৰ ভাল লাগিব ।"-- ৰূমটোৰ একোণত থকা আলমিৰাটোৰ ফালে ল'ৰাজনে আঙুলিয়াই কথা কেইটা কৈ গ'ল ।
"থেঙ্ক ইউ । অলপ জলদি দিবা দেই । আৰু শুনানা, ভোক লাগিছে খুব । চুপ জাতীয় কিবা থাকিলেও দিবা চোন । তুমি অনালৈ মই চেঞ্জ কৰি লওঁ বাৰু ।"
"হ'ব বাইদেউ, মই আনি আছোঁ ।"--- এখোজ দুখোজকৈ সি আঁতৰি গ'ল । বাথৰুমত সোমাই ফ্ৰেছ হৈ আলমিৰাটোৰ পৰা কাপোৰ এযোৰ উলিয়াই পিন্ধি ল'লে তাই  । কি কৰো, কি নকৰো বুলি ভাবি তাই ইউটিউবত হিচক'কৰ "Psycho" খনকে চাবলৈ ধৰিলে । Horror থ্ৰিলাৰ বোৰে তাইক বৰকৈ আকৃষ্ট কৰে ।
এনেতে..... টক-টক-টক....
"কোন?"
"বাইদেউ মই । চাহ আৰু চুপ আনিছোঁ ।"
"ৰ'বা গৈছোঁ ।"-- ততাতৈয়াকৈ গৈ তাই দুৱাৰখন খুলি দিলে । ভোকত আতুৰ হৈ পৰা তাইৰ অপেক্ষা কৰাৰ শক্তি যেন নাইকীয়া হৈ গৈছিল ।
"এয়া লওঁক বাইদেউ ।"-- ট্রেখন আগবঢ়াই দি সি কৈ থকাৰ মাজতে কিবা এটা যেন মজিয়াত সুলকি পৰিল । 
"Sorry বাইদেউ । কেনেকৈ যে সুলকি গ'ল..!! আপোনাক ভয় খুওৱাৰ অলপো মতলব নাছিল ।"-- মজিয়ালৈকে দীঘল হৈ যোৱা হাত দুখনে সুলকি পৰা মূৰটো বুটলি থাকোতেই মূৰটোৱে কথা কেইটা কৈ উঠিল ।
তাৰ পিছৰখিনি............
ফোন স্ক্ৰীণত তেতিয়াও চলি থাকিল হিচক'কৰ "Psycho"

title.stringValue: When hope walked with me and made me walk again

content.stringValue:
“When Hope Walked With Me and Made Me Walk Again"

It was a normal day in 2012.
I was working peacefully in my hometown when I noticed a troubling infection near my ankle...something that refused to heal.
With a congenital defect shadowing me since birth, I was no stranger to medical worries. Yet this time, it felt different… heavier.
An initial surgery and debridement were done, but the infection stubbornly stayed. Concerned, my uncle consulted specialists once again.
Their verdict came like a hammer blow ... “Below-knee amputation would be the best and most permanent solution.”
I couldn’t believe it.
Soon, I was taken to a specialty hospital in Coimbatore, with my brother and uncle by my side. Even there, the experts repeated the same advice.
At first, I refused.
“What if I can’t walk again?”
“What if life never feels normal again?”
That night, lying awake in the hospital bed, my mind was a whirlwind of fears.
I thought of my aging parents, alone in my hometown, silently depending on me.
I thought of my own solitary life, now shadowed by an uncertain future.
“How will I take care of them?”
“How will I take care of myself?”
But the doctors counselled me patiently, explaining the greater danger of untreated infection and the shrinking chances of survival without intervention.
Broken inside, I agreed.
Sometimes, acceptance is the hardest battle.
The Operation and Aftermath
A few days later, the operation took place.
The bitter truth had to be swallowed . my leg was amputated below the knee.
I spent almost a month in the hospital, facing some of my darkest days. My uncle and brother .. their quiet support became my pillars. My younger sister and brother-in-law also came, wrapping me with moral courage I didn’t know I still had.
I tried to be brave, but the ache inside me went deeper than the missing limb. When my little four-year-old niece saw me, her innocent sadness pierced my heart. Even my aged parents, struggling with travel, came to be with me. Their presence made my heart heavy and light at the same time.
Above all,  my sister-in-law  became a blessing. Her care, her delicious dishes filling the home with warmth .... all these became the medicine no doctor could prescribe.
The New Beginning:
Days turned into weeks.
Wounds began to heal.
Pain faded into acceptance.
And then came the day I stood again .. a prosthetic leg supporting me, trembling but determined.
Exactly three months after the surgery, just as the doctors had promised, I took my first steps. They were small, slow, unsure ... but they were my steps. My victory.
A wave of humility flooded me. I bowed my head silently, grateful to God for blessing me with a loving family ...
a thousand prayers of my mum and dad that always stood like rock solid support,
an uncle who has been with me through every thick and thin since childhood,
a brother who stood as my shadow,
a sister-in-law who fed my heart with care,
a sister and brother-in-law who were there for me,
and the brilliant doctors, nurses, and prosthetists who stitched not just my body, but my spirit back together.
I also felt an ocean of gratitude for the advancements in prosthetic technology, which gifted me the simple yet priceless miracle ...
the ability to walk again.
To live again.
To dream again.
I was still me.
A little changed outside, but stronger, humbler, and infinitely richer inside.

Months passed after my operation, and the quiet struggle I endured slowly turned into an unspoken strength. My body, though still recovering, had found its rhythm again. I began to move forward, one careful step at a time, with my prosthetic leg firmly on the ground. Life, though altered, felt steady once more.
In the end, my journey taught me one simple truth… if we firmly believe in His plan and surrender to His will, even the harshest hardships can turn into stepping stones. Trusting Him doesn’t take away the pain, but it fills us with the strength to endure it. And in that faith, life gently reveals better solutions than we could ever imagine …. reminding us that His ways, though mysterious, always lead us toward healing, hope, and a brighter tomorrow.
Today, as I look back after thirteen years since that unexpected chapter, I realise how profoundly it shaped the person I have become. Frankly speaking, that episode gave me far more strength than I ever imagined. It taught me to learn, to accept, and to face whatever life offers — placing deeper trust in His plans, even when they feel unclear.


SUNIL KUMAR MAGATAPALLI

Over-ambition gives nothing but stress and restlessness. Even becoming powerful often fails to bring satisfaction. At first, we chase power for fame, but later we realise that fame itself is hollow. It is a temporary pleasure. Real recognition comes from hard work, sacrifice, and selfless service. If life demands effort and sacrifice anyway, then why run blindly after fame? Instead, live consciously. Enjoy healthy pleasures. Listen to your heart and allow yourself to breathe.
Learning is one of the purest joys of life. Every human, nature itself, and even God teaches us something. When we remain respectful, the world responds with kindness. Awareness empowers us, while ignorance weakens us. Question things, research deeply, and never silence your curiosity. Curiosity is not rebellion; it is intelligence.
Revenge is often mistaken for strength, but in truth it exposes fragility. Real revenge is becoming so strong, so wise, and so fulfilled that negativity loses its power over you. Forgiveness is not weakness—it is compassion. Anger is natural; bitterness is optional. If emotions explode within us, both we and God are aware of the damage they cause.
Let us make this era meaningful. Time itself is neither good nor bad; it is our karma that defines it. No one is born good or evil—character is shaped by thoughts and actions. Knowledge purifies the mind. Sacred texts teach values, discipline, and awareness. Accept your flaws, because no one is perfect. Ego blocks learning; humility opens the door to growth.
Do not harm others. No one is your property, and you are not anyone’s master. Jealousy only blinds us. Someone else’s success does not diminish your worth. Comparisons are poisonous. Harmony reflects strength, while unnecessary conflict exposes inner chaos. Respect is earned by self-control.
Anger exists in everyone—it is human. What matters is how we respond to it. Develop emotional strength so that others’ anger does not wound you. A calm response is more powerful than loud retaliation. As Dharmaraj Yudhishthir said, “The real bath is the one that purifies the heart.” True purification comes from replacing bad habits with good ones.
Make a firm decision to improve yourself. The past is over; do not waste your future repeating old mistakes. Self-control must come first. The mind behaves like a restless monkey—it jumps endlessly. Observe it, discipline it, and remind it who is in charge. Strive to become the best version of yourself, not to dominate others but to master yourself.
Work sincerely, but rest wisely. Clear your path through effort and discipline. Leave harmful habits, no matter how tempting they appear—health is non-negotiable. Remember God consistently, not for demands but for guidance.
There are many forms of God—Ganesh, Hanuman, Shiva, Vishnu—but every individual connects deeply with one chosen deity, the Isht. Identify the form that resonates with your struggles and fears. Worship with discipline and sincerity. Effort must come first; divine grace follows. As my teacher once said, “The thirsty one goes to the well, not the other way around.”
Avoid alcohol and recklessness—it destroys families, fuels crime, and clouds judgement. Drive responsibly. Ego on the road turns people into dangers, not kings. Mental well-being is crucial. Abandon desires that demand great effort but give little value. Excitement fades quickly; regret lasts longer. True wisdom lies in patience, research, and mindful choices.
Money is valuable because it represents hard work. Use it wisely—for comfort, growth, service, and compassion. Excess without purpose leads to carelessness. A balanced life with sufficient resources is richer than endless accumulation.
Clean your mind, purify your actions, and the world—and God—will witness your greatness.

Why do I feel so jittery?

Arrows fly and the battlefield roars. Yet it is not enemies; it's myself. My hands tremble, not from the sword I bear, but from the burden of decisions. Which duty is truly mine, and which to let go? Which path is righteousness, and which is merely attachment disguised as purpose?

Do I shape my destiny, or does it shape me?

I have spent my life chasing my desires, holding on to what I am rewarded and fearing losses. But am I truly this person, or only the reflection of who I believe I should be? The body will fade, the name will vanish, the world will forget you, but your soul will endure. The soul, the spark within that notices, feels and understands, lasts beyond everything.

Lord Krishna said, 'Do your duty without clinging to results,' but I ponder, how can I truly act if I don't care for consequences?Slowly, I realize I can't truly cling to the result because it isn't mine to control. Winning or losing doesn't define strength; it's about showing up, being present and acting with integrity. 

Yes, I am afraid—but who among us is not? Fear may cloud our vision, but it doesn't have to stay that way. I must face my true self, without pride, masks or illusions. Then I will act without seeking reward, recognition or comfort. I will act simply because it is the right thing to do. Because it must be done. Because it is the path meant for me. 

The greatest battlefield is not around me—it is within. The real war is fought in thoughts, desires, and emotions. If I can master myself, understand things as they truly are and act honestly and firmly, then maybe I will feel I have fulfilled my responsibility.

I need you to listen.

I don't ask for approval to claim beside you,
I arrive with clarity and certainty. 
Quiet, undeniable
Controlled and anchored 
Unquestionable  

I notice what others ignore.
The shimmer in their eyes that trembles 
The version of reality they choose
When resilience speaks without words.
I make no intrusion. 
I hold my judgement.
I trust the power of my silence.

You carry weight without wavering. 
Every choice you make is precise.
And when you select me, everything shifts.

I avoid lingering when absence feels heavy.
I remain where boundaries blur, where warmth is mistaken for entry. 
Safeguarding is silent; it anchors within and stays watchful.

Call it dominance, if you wish. 
I will call it clarity and architecture, every line drawn with care. 
I don't choose for you.
I choose you.
Because you trust my steadiness, my way of framing the edge, grounded, silent, and exact.

I never threaten. 
Silence carries me.
The pause that hangs before my words,
the intensity that hardens in my stare, that carries the warning.
A clear boundary is sensed and respected.
They're honored.
People adjust.

You are not claimed. 
You are chosen.
Met with intention.
Visible, never hidden.

My words stay gentle. 
My presence stands on its own. 
My gifts need no consent.
You ease into me, your sharpness going quiet.

If my love feels heavy, it's only because it stays.
If it hits hard,
It's because I don't dilute my current.
And if others flinch at the current, what they're really feeling is the current I carry, full force.

Whatever comes close, 
meets understanding first.
And understanding is a gate that few stumble through twice.

With a sky full of stars, silent as the sky itself,
wearing the solitary beauty and diamond glow of constellations,
sit beside me.
Lonely, wordless, two minds side by side—
the fountain of heartbeat, the rasp of lungs,
and no other sound between us.
Beyond me, emerging from me,
my soul, my being, my existence
will become your sky and cradle you—
even then that silence will surround us like clouds.
If you come, if you love—
then love like death,
in that silence where all paths of return have dissolved.
The word that exists in wordlessness, 
I know you understand.
Shallow navel, shallow mind, 
the clamour of expression—
they could never bind me,
not even after seven lifetimes.

In some corner of this city’s lined footpaths,
under the shy shelter of tarpaulin and banners,
I first met her.
Disheveled hair,
the heartbeat clear through her ribcage,
a swollen belly from malnutrition,
absorbed in slate and pencil.
The bells of buses, trams, rickshaws,
the irritated curses of office goers—
all rendered meaningless by her busyness,
which outdid even the city’s busiest artery.
I stood stunned, gazing at her.
When Merry, sitting on the mat of fallen Bur flowers by the railing like her—wild-grown—
looked up with a smiling face,
I first lifted poetry into my arms
from the dust-laden royal road of the city.
I have found her many times since,
and she finds me in her own way.
On cyclone nights in the mad waves of Ganges,
In rainy or sunny afternoons amid the city’s dust-scent on highways,
in the golden molten moonlight of bliss full winter nights
in the lotus pond by distant hill, 
with solitary kingfishers sipping date-palm sap,
in the long myna-like eyes of tribal girls—
she has come searching.
She has come searching for me
to the cremation ghat.
Taking my hand, leading me home,
Seating by me on the stained chair,
in the conversation between dust-covered table and fountain pen—
she whispered to my tired ear:
on all the days of heartache,
bring poetry with your pen every day.
She explained:
poetry has mind, poetry has body,
poetry is a treasure of utmost care—
we owe poetry so much.

मैं रुकूँगी नहीं…
चाहे राहों में
कितने ही ताने क्यूँ न पड़े हों,
चाहे सपनों को देखकर
लोगों के चेहरे क्यूँ न मुड़े हों।
मेरे हौसले दर्पण नहीं
जो समाज के अनुसार झुक जाएँ,
मैं वो ज्योति हूँ
जो अँधेरों में भी अपना मार्ग बना जाएँ।

मैंने सहा है वो दर्द भी
जिसकी कोई आवाज़ नहीं होती,
और झेला है वो संदेह भी
जिसे कोई ज़ुबान नहीं देती।
पर मेरे भीतर की नारी
कभी हार मानना जानती नहीं—
ये वही शक्ति है
जो राख से भी अग्नि जन्म देती है।


कोई कहता है—
“तेरे सपने बहुत बड़े हैं,”
तो मैं मुस्कुराकर कहती हूँ—
“मेरे हौसले उससे भी बड़े हैं।”
मैं चूल्हे की राख नहीं,
वेदों की अग्नि हूँ,
मैं केवल देह नहीं,
संघर्षों से बनी शक्ति हूँ।

थकान चाहे मेरे कदमों को रोक दे,
पर ये आत्मविश्वास मुझे
पंख बनाकर उड़ने को कहता है।
जहाँ लोग हार मान बैठते हैं,
मैं वहीं अपने साहस का दीपक जलाती हूँ—
क्योंकि मैं जानती हूँ
जिस दिन मैं ठहर गई,
उस दिन मेरे सपने भी रुक जाएँगे।

आज मैं संघर्ष कर रही हूँ,
कल इतिहास लिखूँगी,
मैं गिरूँगी हाँ,
पर हर बार गिरकर
पहाड़ की तरह उठूँगी।
ना मुझे किसी के आशीर्वाद की भीख चाहिए,
ना मान्यता का प्रमाण पत्र—
मेरी पहचान मेरी मेहनत है,
और यही मेरा अभिमान है।

मैं रुकूँगी नहीं,
क्योंकि मैं 'औरत' हूँ —
और मुझमें वो शक्ति है
जो सृष्टि को जन्म देती है,
जो राख में भी से
नया सूरज गढ़ देती है।

मैं रुकूँगी नहीं…
क्योंकि मेरा सफ़र
किसी मंज़िल पर खत्म नहीं,
बल्कि नई पीढ़ियों के लिए
एक प्रेरणा बनकर शुरू होगा।

वो चूल्हे की आँच से
आसमान की उड़ान तक आई है,
हर दौर में खुद को
नए सांचे में ढाल लाई है।


कभी बेटी बन सपनों को
पायल में बाँध दिया,
कभी माँ बन अपने हिस्से की
नींद तक दान कर दिया।


उसने सहना सीखा,
पर चुप रहना नहीं,
अब झुकी हुई नज़र भी 
सीधा सवाल करती हैं ।


वो अब इजाज़त नहीं माँगती
अपने फैसलों के लिए,
अपने हक़ की लड़ाई
खुद लड़ती है हौसलों के सहारे।


उसके हाथों में
सिर्फ़ मेहंदी नहीं हैं ,
कलम है, कुदरत है,
और बदलाव की कहानी है।


स्त्री कमजोर नहीं,
ये सोच ही कमजोर थी,
आज जब वो खड़ी हुई है
तो दुनिया भी आगे गई हैं।


सशक्त स्त्री कोई और नहीं,
ये एक जागती हुई पहचान है,
जहाँ स्त्री आगे बढ़ती है
वहाँ दिल से उसे सलाम है।

These nights Of joy and of lights 
Of merriment and of union 
Of purity and of light

Still drowning in the deep ocean 
Beginning to swim 
Yet nowhere close to cruising their waters 
This human heart of mine lies shattered In a pool, of joy, oozing from the peices 
Broken pole star in a dark night 
Watching over a once lost traveler 
Watching over her in the annual eclipse 
Overflowing with melancholy 
Yet looks at her with a heavy happiness 
For the once lost traveler is 
Lost no more 
Now surrounded by allies 
With all else that was missing 
Healed of old wounds 
As beautiful as the little bear 
So much older,so much wiser 
Yet still a fresh new butterfly 
Whose wings betray what she is now 
This broken pole star shall return to sleep 
Looking forward to the next eclipse 
Looking forward to seeing her new wings 
Looking forward to seeing once again 
The lost traveler, effortlessly navigating
The path that is life, with a new guiding light
Fly high little butterfly
Fly high

It all began on a typical Saturday morning at the local tennis club, where I had been taking lessons for months. As I awaited my instructor, I noticed a girl practising her serves on the adjacent court. Though she was consistently messing up, her determination and focus caught my attention as I found myself drawn to her grit. That's when I met Sophia, exchanging pleasantries between serves. We hit it off immediately, bonding over our shared love of tennis and introvert tendencies. Little did I know that our lives would soon become intertwined in ways I never could have imagined. A few weeks after that first meeting, and by total coincidence, I transferred mid-year into Sophia's college because my dad had gotten transferred as well. This marked a significant transition; while the campus was unfamiliar, seeing Sophia's familiar face in the crowd made the adjustment a little easier.
As we spent more time together on and off the court, Sophia and I gradually began forming a tighter bond. We discovered that we shared more than just a love for tennis - we shared the same passion for life, the same desire to learn, and the longing for genuine connection. Our conversations flowed effortlessly, jumping from superficial topics like our favourite books and movies, or even professors we hated, to deeper ones like childhood memories and future dreams. Slowly but surely, Sophia's vulnerability and trust drew me in, and I found myself opening up to her, showing her layers of me I never knew existed. I shared with her my own struggles, my fears, and my insecurities. And to my surprise, she listened with empathy and understanding, offering those rare words of encouragement mixed with support and acceptance. As we bonded over shared experiences and emotions like these, our connection deepened, and we became each other's constant, each other's safe haven. We laughed together, cried together, and navigated our lives together, our friendship growing stronger with each passing day.
In Sophia, I found a kindred spirit, someone who understood me without judgment, someone who accepted me for all I was. And I knew that she felt the same way about me. Our bond was built on mutual vulnerability, trust, and empathy. We didn't try to change anything, just simply accepted each other, flaws and all, and in doing so, we created a sanctuary, a space where we could be ourselves, without fear of misunderstanding or criticism. As we navigated the ups and downs of college life, Sophia and I found comfort in each other's presence. We'd spend hours on end talking about our hopes and dreams, our fears and anxieties. We'd share our deepest secrets, our darkest thoughts, and our most cherished desires. And through it all, we'd find solace in each other's company, a sense of peace that eluded us in our daily lives.
But it was in those fleeting moments, those unguarded seconds, that I saw the truth. A flash of fear in her eyes, the split second of hesitation in her voice, a subtle withdrawal from the world. It was as if the mask she wore for the world to see had slipped, revealing the pain and trauma that lay beneath. My heart skipped a beat as I recognised the signs, the same signs that I had seen in myself. Echoes.Echoes of a traumatic past, those of lingering scars. In that moment, somewhere deep down, I knew that Sophia's story was similar to mine, that she had seen the same pain, the same suffering I had. I knew that her wounds were still raw, that she was still afraid to trust completely. I didn't want to risk reopening old wounds or triggering painful memories. So, I kept my knowledge to myself, using it instead to pad my actions,
to guide my words, and to deepen our connection. In doing so, I created a safe space for Sophia, a space where she could be herself, without the fear of judgment or desertion.
I knew that hell. It had more than enough potential to destroy emotions, leaving a person feeling empty. Feeling purposeless. My own traumatic past still lingered, a constant reminder of the struggles I had faced. I always been ostracised by the people around me. At first, they only refused to acknowledge my existence, but as time passed, it only got worse, morphing into active hostility. I was always wiping away quiet tears that wouldn’t stop falling, screaming silently to be seen, just wishing someone would look at me and see a boy, not a guinea pig for cruel entertainment. My initial years were spent getting excluded from social events, alienated by my classmates and much worse. Every inch of me would be criticised and laughed at. My clothes, my interests, my choices, my hobbies, my body, me. I’d be pushed around, called all sorts of names, and made to feel worthless. I had no one to talk to, no one to confide in. My parents were always busy, my teachers didn't care, my friends were nonexistent, and my classmates were the ones tormenting me. My only support was myself. Every day was a struggle, new gashes appearing in my flesh before I could heal past ones. The cuts that did heal left everlasting scars that began to tingle with that same familiar pain when I saw beyond her mask.
I stood in silence, recounting my past, as i decide to respect Sophia's boundaries, to let her tell me when she chooses to, to keep her secret. I was reminded of my own past. I knew the weight of lingering scars, of wounds that still ached. I knew what it was like to feel vulnerable and exposed, to fear being judged or rejected. Determined to save Sophia from that same hell, I slowly became her support and made it my mission to be the rock she could lean on, her escape from daily life, where she could find solace. We bonded slowly, as I shared her joys, offered comfort in her sorrows, and stood by her side through every up and down. Never did I give out a clue that I knew of her. This was a secret I kept locked away, hidden behind my own mask of calm compassion.
And in that knowledge, the bond grew stronger, our connection deeper. I felt a sense of empathy and understanding that was beyond words, a sense of solidarity that only came from shared experiences. But despite this profound understanding, I never revealed that I knew so deeply about her. I didn't want to pry or intrude on her pain. Not yet. I chose not to make her feel the sense of vulnerability that preceded betrayal. Instead, I chose to keep this within me, to respect her decision, and to let her know that I was there for her, without a shadow of condition or expectation. This silence was not of ignorance or indifference, but of empathy and love.
My motivation went beyond mere kindness or altruism. I wanted to be that one person to Sophia that I never had when I needed it most. I wanted to be the friend who stood by her side, unwavering and unshakeable. I wanted to be her haven where she could find peace, the comforting presence that would keep her demons at bay. I knew what it was like to be alone, to be adrift in that sea of uncertainty, and I was determined to be the anchor that held Sophia fast. I would be the one to hold her hand through the darkness, to guide her towards the light, and to help her heal from the wounds of her past.
My love for Sophia wasn't a desire for romance, but a profound recognition of a truly beautiful soul. I didn't want to possess her; I simply yearned to witness her journey and ensure she never had to navigate the shadows alone. Loving her meant finding a rare, quiet sanctuary in our shared silence, a place where the jagged edges of our pasts didn't need to be hidden or explained. It was fierce loyalty born of the relief of finally being understood without misunderstanding. I loved her for the safety we built together, a
bond far more sacred than fleeting attraction, and I was committed to being the shield that guarded her peace at any cost.
But our growing friendship didn't go unnoticed. Rumours began to spread like wildfire through the college corridors. Students whispered that Sophia and I were dating. The rumours were false, but they stuck, and soon Sophia was being bullied by our peers. They made fun of her for being "irresponsible," avoided her even more, and treated her like total garbage. Behind her back, she was constantly judged and badmouthed for hanging out with the “creepy recluse”. Gradually, people began seeing Sophia as the weird, eerily quiet kid in her class. She was oblivious to the fact that we were the freshest tea in a one-mile radius as talk spread even to the juniors, but still did feel that something was off and would talk to me about it frequently.
Soon after, Sophia introduced me to Rachel, one of her casual friends, whom I later grew closer to and came to become a part of our tight-knit circle. Her gentle soul and bright smile made her a joy to be around. I knew that Rachel's home life was tough - her parents were separated, and she lived with her mom, who struggled to make ends meet. Despite the challenges, Rachel's innocent soul remained kind and unshakeable. She had a way of looking at the world that was both refreshing and heartbreaking - a sense of wonder and trust that I feared would one day be lost. As I got to know Rachel better, I was struck by her resilience and adaptability. She never complained about her situation; instead chose to focus on the positive aspects of her life. Her optimism was contagious, and being around her made me realise how much I took for granted. While Sophia remained my closest confidante, Rachel's presence in our lives brought a sense of warmth and comfort, and I felt grateful to have her as a part of our newfound trio.
As the three of us spent more time together, our bond grew stronger. We often hung out, exploring the community and trying new things. We had weekly excursions, whether it was hiking through nearby trails, trying out new restaurants, or visiting local museums. But it wasn't just the big adventures that brought us closer together. Sometimes, we'd just sit together, talking about life, playing board games, or reading books. These quiet moments were just as precious as our more ambitious outings. We'd spend hours lounging around, sharing stories, and supporting each other. Rachel would often bring over homemade treats, and the three of us would indulge in snacks while discussing everything from our favourite books to our deepest fears. We all believed that friendship isn't just about grand adventures but also about the small everyday moments, the laughter, and the memories that make life worth living. As we sat together, surrounded by the comforts of home, I felt grateful for the bond that we shared. We were more than just friends; we were a support system, a haven, and a constant source of encouragement.
As time passed, I began to notice a shift in Rachel's behaviour around me. She’d always been affectionate and playful, but now her actions seemed laced with a newfound intensity. I couldn't quite put my finger on it, but I sensed a shift in how she saw me, now in a deep-seated longing for connection and love. It dawned on me that Rachel's behaviour might be a cry for affection, a desperate attempt to fill the void left by her turbulent home life. Her parents' separation had left emotional crevasses, and I assumed she was seeking solace in our friendship. At first, Rachel's flirting was subtle. She'd touch elbows while laughing, or find excuses to sit close to me. But as the days blurred into weeks, her advances became more blatant. She'd make suggestive comments, her eyes sparkling with that mischievous glint. The tension between us came to a head on Halloween night. We had met up with a couple of friends, but as the evening wore on, Rachel
suggested we take a walk alone. The crisp autumn air was accompanied by the occasional icy gust of wind as we strolled side by side. As we walked, Rachel reached out and tried to take my hand. I hesitated, unsure of how to react. To me, Rachel had always been a friend, nothing more, nothing less. I valued our friendship, but had never seen her in a romantic light. That's why, when she tried to take my hand, it didn't feel like a friendly gesture but something beyond that. Something I wasn't comfortable with. I pulled away, trying to brush it off as a casual gesture. The aftermath was awkward. I, of course, walked her home, being the gentleman, But We didn't talk to each other for a fortnight, the silence between us thick with unspoken emotions. After the longest time without any action on her part, I decided to confront her. On giving her an ultimatum, something I’m still deeply ashamed of, she confessed to everything. How she kept trying to slip me hints, how she interpreted my compassion as something beyond, how she loved the attention I gave her, how my presence made her “whole”, how she’d fallen head over heels for me. After taking a minute to gather myself back up, I told her what I truly felt. I did blame myself for not reciprocating her feelings, but I couldn't lie to myself, to forcefully produce something that wasn't there, to fake my emotions and misuse her trust, when I'd seen her as only a friend. Rachel, with tears pouring down her cheeks, was hurt and confused, trying to process my unexpected rejection.
Instead of accepting my rejection and moving on with the understanding that I'd never see her as anything more, Rachel let her obsession with me consume her, blinding her to the devastating consequences of her soon-to-come actions. She was convinced that Sophia was the only obstacle standing between us, and with ruthless determination, she set out to sabotage our friendship. Rachel's words cut deep, deeper than any blade, as she deceitfully told Sophia that my kindness and compassion were hiding ulterior motives, that I liked her romantically, rather than the genuine value I placed on her as a person. This poisonous lie seeped into Sophia's fragile psyche, reawakening her deepest fears and traumatic past. The wounds Sophia had carefully stitched up over the years now burst open, releasing an endless, gushing torrent of pain and insecurity, accompanied by the shards of shattered trust. Rachel's desire for me had become an all-consuming force, destroying everything in its wake. She was willing to annihilate a friendship that had brought us all so much joy, simply to satiate her own hunger. The Rachel I thought I knew – kind, compassionate, and genuine- was no more, now replaced by a ruthless, cunning, and cold stranger. Her actions served as a stark reminder that even the most seemingly innocent among us can be transformed by the corrosive power of desire.
Sophia, once open and trusting, now stood behind an impenetrable wall, her eyes cold and distant. She had blocked all pathways of communication, cutting me out of her life swiftly and mercilessly. The distance between us grew, a chasm that seemed impossible to bridge, a huge ocean that echoed with past memories. Rachel's manipulation was devastatingly effective. She had played on Sophia's deepest fears, using her own jealousy and insecurity to drive a wedge between us. Sophia, already insecure and fragile, had been unable to resist the insidious whispers that had eroded her trust. Sophia must have felt like she was losing her grip on reality. Rachel's lies had been expertly crafted to exploit Sophia's insecurities, making her question everything she thought she knew about our friendship. The doubts had crept in like a thief in the dead of night, snatching away Sophia's confidence and replacing it with crippling uncertainty and loss of trust. Rachel's manipulation was a masterpiece of psychological warfare, leaving Sophia feeling battered, bruised, and bleeding. Rachel's actions were selfish, cold and calculated, driven by her own desire to keep Sophia away. She couldn't bear the thought of Sophia being happy with me, of our bond growing stronger. So, she set out to destroy it. She didn't think twice and instantly threw away years of friendship and betrayed Sophia, pitting her against me. And now, Sophia was gone, lost to me forever. The pain of losing her was crushing, but the knowledge
that Rachel, who seemed like an innocent, sweet lamb, had manipulated her, pitting her own vulnerabilities against her, felt like a terrible twisted lie. I was confused, desperate. I tried to set things right, but the damage was done. I spiralled through the five stages of grief. Denial: "This can't be happening." Anger: "Why did Rachel interfere?" Bargaining: "What could I have done differently?" Depression: "I've lost her forever." And finally, Acceptance: "She's better off and happier without me around."
Later on, my name became synonymous with the bullying, a constant reminder to Sophia of the pain and humiliation she'd endured. She believed that I was the reason people bullied her, that my presence in her life had somehow triggered the cruelty of our peers. The rumours and lies had been relentless, painting me as a villain, a mastermind of manipulation. She wanted nothing to do with me. In her eyes, I was a reminder of the darkness she'd faced, a symbol of the suffering she'd endured. It was then that she began hating me.
The real me, her rock, her supporting pillar were all erased, replaced by a new narrative, one casting me as a monster. A new version of me was being instilled in her, one that was so warped and distorted, completely glazing over what I actually was. The memories of our laughter, our conversations, and our quiet moments together were all tainted by this new reality. I was no longer the person she had once trusted, but a caricature of evil, a shadow of her own fear and pain. The weight of her anger, her resentment, was crushing, but I knew I had to bear it. I had to let her hate me, because it was easier on her to hate me than to face the truth that we'd both been victims of jealousy, pawns in a convoluted game of cruelty and deception.
As time passed, I wanted to reach out to Sophia, try to clear the air and repair our friendship. But I knew that approaching her would only make things worse. The rumours and bullying would start all over again, and Sophia would be forced to relive the pain and humiliation. I couldn't do that to her. I had to prioritise her well-being, even if it meant sacrificing my own desire to reconnect with her. Moreover, I didn't want to disrupt her life, cause her more stress, or make her feel uncomfortable. I also didn't want to give Rachel the satisfaction of knowing that she had successfully driven us apart. Most importantly, I didn't want Sophia to feel obligated to respond or reconcile with me, only to appease her own guilt or sense of duty. I wanted her to be free of all that, to live her life without the weight of our complicated past.
With a leaden heart, I stepped back, the weight of my sacrifice crushing me like nothing else, suffocating me beneath its oppressive grief. Not because I didn't care about her, but because I cared too much. The thought of causing her more pain, more humiliation, was unbearable, a torment that ripped my soul to shreds and left me gasping for air. Regret and self-loathing haunted me for months, their dark shadows lingering in every corner of my mind, taunting me with what could never be. But as time took its course, I came to realise that loving someone isn't about possession or control; it's about liberation. The freedom to love without expectation. Love means letting go, even when it shatters your own heart into a million pieces, leaving you shattered, lost, and forever changed. It means prioritising the other's happiness, even if it means sacrificing your own.
To this day, a glimmer of hope remains, a flicker of light in the darkness that has consumed me. Perhaps one day Sophia would return, her eyes finally open to the truth, that my actions were driven by a soul-deep love for her, a love that had compelled me to sacrifice my own heart for her freedom. Maybe she’d see the tears I'd cried, the sleepless nights I'd endured, and the endless longing that had haunted me since she'd
gone. Maybe she’d understand the anguish that had ravaged my soul, the desperation that had driven me to let her go, and the desolate emptiness that had remained. And maybe, just maybe, she would forgive me, and we could start anew, our love reborn from the ashes of heartbreak and regret.
-Beetroot

title.stringValue: Chalo na baba purani reet badalte hain

content.stringValue:
Meine kaha tumse chalna sikhao,
Tumne chalna hi nahi sahi rah chunna bhi sikhaya,
Meine kaha tumse bolna sikhao,
Tumne bolna hi nahi uske sahi arth bhi bataye.
Meine kaha tumse frock dilao,
Tumne frock, skirt, dilayee saath meri hud aur maryada bhi bataye.
Jab padhne ki baat ayee to sabne kaha ladki hai jaana to sasural hai kya karegi karke padhai,
Sabki baaton ko nazar andaz kar mujhe badi degree dilayi.
Fir jab byah ki baat aayi to kyon meri ungli kisi anjaan hathon mein thamayi,
Apni jhuthi hansi ke peeche apne gham ko chipaya,fulon se saji doli mein mujhko bithaya aur kaha,
Ashirwad hai mera, sada khush rehna,
Tujhe mere hisse ki bhi Khushi mile, kabhi gham na sehna.
Chalo na baba purani reet hum badalte hain,zindagi bhar saath rehne ka wada hum kartein hain,
Na byah karungi mein ,
Na karna tum meri bidayi , 
Sabse kehna tum baba betiyan nahi hoti hai parayi.
Apna angan suna kar auron ka angan kaise roshan kar paoge,
Budhape mein akele kaise reh paoge.
Jitni khushiyan di hai tumne uska mol chukana hai,
Baba teri ladon hu mein mujhe paraya nahi kehelana hai.
Chalo na baba purani reet badalte hain, basate hain koi aisa jahan,
Jahan maa baap aur betiyan saath mein rehte hain,.
Chalo na baba hum purani reet badalte hain.

Kal Naina ka birthday hai,wo aaj office se jaldi ghar aa gayee hai, kal ka din uske liye bahut important hai,wo Amit ko propose karne wali hai, flowers le liye hain, gifts le liye hain aur ring bhi le li hai, bas ab ek letter likhna baki hai, naina letter likhne baith jaati hai, bahut sari pyari batein likhti hai letter mein achanak khidki se barish ki boondein uske chehre par padti hai aur wo apne khayalon ki duniyan se bahar aa jati hai. Naina ko barish bahut pasand hai, wo khidki ke bilkul paas chali jati hai, achanak uski nazar samne wale coffee shop par khadi ek ladki par padti hai, Jane kyon Naina ko aisa laga jaise us ladki se Naina ka koi connection hai. Naina bade gaur se us ladki ki harkaton ko dekhti hai uske ek haath mein guldasta hai aur doosre mein kuch bags.Wo time dekhti hai aur age badh jaati hai, shayad use road cross karna tha, andhera ho chala tha barish bahut tez nahi thi magar fir bhi street light mein thik se kuch dikh nahi Raha tha.us ladki ko bheeg jane ka dar tha, wo thoda hadbada jati hai, naina dhyan se use dekhne ki koshish mein thi ki achanak zor se chillane ki awaz ati hai, are ye kya us ladki ka accident ho gaya. Naina wahan Jane ko hoti hai ki tabhi darwaze ke khulne ki awaz aati hai, Amit aur Sagar ghar mein dakhil hote hain, Sagar ki hathon mein jo bag tha Naina ka dhaan apni our kheenchte hai magar naina kitchen mein chali jaati hai, wo glass hathon mein leti hai Pani bharne ke liye ki tabhi Amit ki kahi hui baatein Naina ko pareshan kar deti hai, wo Amit ke paas akar bade pyar se uske sir pe haath ferti hai aur poochti hai ki kya pareshani hai, aur Amit ne Sagar se ye kyon kaha ki humare khushiyon ke pal itne kam kyo the. Magar Amit Naina ki baaton par dhyaan nahi deta aur Sagar ke haatho se bag le kar saaman dekhne lagta hai, bag se ek box niklata hai jisme ring thi, Naina chaunk jaati hai, ye to bilkul waisi hi ring hai jo usne Amit ke liye li thi, wo thoda aur pareshan jati hai, fir wo guldasta nikalta hai, fir wo dress ab Naina se raha nahi jaata aur wo Amit se poochti hai ki ye sab kiska hai, itne mein Naina ka dhyan apne dress ki taraf jaata hai jo usne peheni hui thi. Ab Naina ko samajhne mein jyada waqt nahi lagta hai hai ki, Amit aur Sagar uski baat sun kyon nahi rahe the, wo sara saman kahan se aya tha, kuch der pehle jis ladki ko Naina ne coffee shop pe dekha tha uske saath Naina ko connection sa kyon mehsoos ho raha tha. Naina ko samajh aa gaya tha ki wo ab dhundh ho chuki hai, uski saanse aur uska astitwa ab khatma ho chuka hai. Wo ladki naina thi, wo saara saman Naina ka tha, wo accident bhi Naina ka hua tha. Wo bade pyaar se Amit se apne pyaar ka izhaar karti hai, aur khidki ki taraf chali jaati hai, apne adhure likhe khat ko padhti hai jisme bas I love you likhna baki tha, uski aankho se ansuon ki do boond chalak jaati hai, aur barish ko dekhte hue wo khud barish mein kahin ghum ho jaati hai,

Yet you are not here
Everything feing to be same
But something is still missing 
I am missing 
You are missing 
Then I sit and wonder
What all these samness feels so unfamiliar 
I am not the same 
Now without your talks this house echoes differently 
The laughter we shared ; stays still at family gatherings 
The food we shared is same but tastes soo different without you
Our siblings whispers has lost its warmth
 Festivals come but they don't stay 
Beacuse you are not around
Everything night I go to bed with wishing ; to see you in the morning
And when I wake up 
You are still not around
I need that warm hug 
I need our banters to echo in this house
Ohh I am soo helpless 
Beacuse I know you are not around 
At nights I break your name
Rising with tears in my eyes
And I know now you are not a phone call away
You are beyond my reach ; somewhere you are pain free
But I still hope to see a glimpse of my little silly brother 
I wish you were still here 
Not somewhere written in the beautiful sky
I want our silly banters back 
I want you to call my name and tease me again
Where everything can be the same
Now people ask me "why have you so changed?"
I simply simle and say 
For me everything has changed 
The day you left

You loved me 
In the quiet winter nights
When noone was watching, 
Just you and I sitting under the moonlight and the stars
It was when life was easy; but not when it got tougher 
When you staying with me meant a sacrifice for you
Then I realised "ohh it's a halfway love"

I spent an enternitiy to convince myself that " maybe this halfway love is enough for me"

Now I have realised 
 This halfway love of yours ; gave me a reason to stay with you
But never made me feel secure
 I want you to love on only in long winter nights but in broad daylight as well
I want you love me when life feels like a nightmare; I want you to hold my hands and tell me everything is going to be okay
I don't need this halfway love of yours

Halfway love is not enough

ज़िन्दगी नदामतों से लबरेज़ थी, तुम्हारे आने तक

हमें करीब लाने को रची है साजिशें ये हवाएं तक
हम आह भी करें तो खबर पहुँच जाती है तुम तक

सारे अल्फ़ाज़ थम से गए थे मेरी वफ़ा के अफ़साने में, तुम्हारे आने तक

नज़रें मयस्सर न थीं किसी के इंतज़ार को, तुम्हारे आने तक,
तुम्हारा जाना अब गवारा नहीं, ठहर जाती हैं नज़रें तुम्हारे ओझल होने तक

मैं वफ़ा की तलाश में था इस दौर-ए-बेवफ़ाई में, तुम्हारे आने तक
तुम्हारी हद-ए-वफ़ा देख कर लगा, मैं भी बेवफ़ा ही रहा अब तक

आग़ाज़ किया है, एक दिन पहुँच ही जाऊँगा अंजाम तक
कारवाँ-ए-मोहब्बत चलता रहेगा गर्दिश के हर इम्तिहान तक

मैं नहीं जानता तुम्हारी तलब मुझ में रहेगी कब तक
मगर ये सुकून भरी ख़ालिस मोहब्बत ज़िंदा रहेगी रूह जाने तक

मैं वो चाँद नहीं जो सिर्फ रातों को चाँदनी बिखेरे ज़मीं तक
मैं वो आसमां हूं, ठहर जाऊंगा तुम्हारा हमसफर बनकर उम्र भर तक

ये महफ़िल, ये सामेईन, ये नाज़रीन— याद रखेंगे तुम्हारी दास्तां ए मोहब्बत को सदियाँ तक

content.stringValue:
ਬਹੁਤ ਸੋਹਣੀ ਸੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਚਲਦੀ 
ਪਤਾ ਨ੍ਹੀ ਕਿਸਦੀ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਲੱਗ ਗਈ
ਖੁਸ਼ੀਆ ਚ ਹਸਦੇ ਦਰਦ ਨੇ ਘੇਰੇ ਪਾਲੇ
ਇੰਝ ਲਗੇ ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਹੀ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਠੱਗ ਗਈ
ਤੇਰਾ ਪਿਆਰ ਸੀ ਮੇਰੇ ਲਈ ਰੱਬ ਦਾ ਹੋਣਾ
ਪਰ ਕਿਉ ਇਹ ਪਿਆਰ ਰੱਬ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜੂਰ ਨਾ ਹੋਇਆ
ਸ਼ਕਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਪਾਬਦੀਆ ਚ ਪਾਈ ਰੱਖਿਆ
ਜਦੋਂ ਤਕ ਮੇਰਾ ਦਿਲ ਟੁੱਟ ਕੇ ਚੂਰ ਨਾ ਹੋਇਆ
ਤੇਰੀਆ ਦਿੱਤੀਆ ਬਹੁਤ ਖੁਸ਼ੀਆ ਨੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ
ਦੁੱਖ ਤਾਂ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਚਲਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੋਂ ਮਿਲੇ
ਇਹ ਨਾ ਸੋਚੀ ਤੂੰ ਮੇਰੇ ਲਈ ਕੁਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ
ਨਾ ਹੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਸ਼ਿਕਵੇ ਨਾ ਗਿਲੇ
ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੌਣ ਦੀ ਜਿੱਦ ਮੇਰੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਵੀ ਸੀ
ਪਰ ਮਾਂ ਪਿਓ ਦੇ ਬੋਲਾਂ ਮੂਹਰੇ 
ਮੈ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹਾਰ ਗਈ
ਆਖਰੀ ਵਾਰ ਦਾ ਰਹੇਗਾ ਪਿਆਰ ਮੇਰਾ ਤੂੰ
ਤੇਰੇ ਉਤੋਂ ਮੈ ਆਪਣਾ ਆਪ ਵਾਰ ਗਈ 
ਚਲਦੇ ਹਲ਼ਾਤਾ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਏਨਾਂ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਤੋੜ 
ਕੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਤੇਰੀ ਵਫ਼ਾ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਲ ਨਾ ਹੋਇਆ ਮੋੜ
ਮਰਜ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਸਾਹ ਵੀ ਨਾ ਲਿਆ ਜਾਵੇ
ਮੇਰੀ ਕੱਲੀ ਕਲੀ ਪਸੰਦ ਦੀ ਚੀਜ਼ ਤੇ ਵੀ ਰੋਕ ਲਾਈ ਗਈ ਏ
ਭਰਾ ਵੀ ਕਹੇ ਇਹਨੇ ਇੱਜਤ ਰੋਲ ਕੇ ਭਜ ਜਾਣਾ 
ਕਿਉਕਿ ਓਹਦੇ ਵੀ ਮੇਰੀ ਕੱਲੀ ਕਲੀ ਗੱਲ ਕੰਨੀ ਪਾਈ ਗਈ ਏ
ਸਮਾ ਤਾਂ ਭਾਵੇਂ ਠੀਕ ਹੋਜੇ ਪਰ ਮੈ ਏਨੀ ਟੁੱਟ ਚੁੱਕੀ ਆ 
ਕਿ ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਚਾਅ ਕੇ ਵੀ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਨੀ ਜਾਣਾ
ਤੂੰ ਕਵੇ ਤੇ ਤੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਏ ਮੇਰੇ ਪਰ 
ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਹੁਣ ਪਿਆਰ ਦੇ ਰਾਹੀ ਮੁੜਿਆ ਨੀ ਜਾਣਾ
ਪੁਰਜਾ ਪੁਰਜਾ ਖਿੱਲਰ ਚੁੱਕਿਆ 
ਜਿਹੜਾ ਤੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਵੀ ਲੱਭਿਆ ਨੀ ਜਾਣਾ
ਰਹਿ ਲਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਬਿਨਾ ਹੁਣ ਤੂੰ
ਤੇਰਾ ਦਿਲ ਮੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਦੁਬਾਰਾ ਠੱਗਿਆ ਨੀ ਜਾਣਾ
ਤੇਰੇ ਵਾਂਗ ਇੱਕ ਆਸ ਮੈ ਹਾਲੇ ਵੀ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦੀ ਆ
ਪਰ ਡਰ ਲਗਦੈ ਜੋ ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੋ ਰਹੀ ਉਹ ਤੇਰੇ ਤਕ ਨਾ ਆ ਜੇ
ਮੇਰੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਲਗੇ ਇਲਜਾਮ ਮੈ ਜਰ ਲਾ ਗੀ 
ਪਰ ਮੇਰੇ ਰਾਹਾਂ ਦੀਆ ਮੁਸੀਬਤਾਂ ਤੇਰੇ ਉਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਦਾਗ ਨਾ ਲਾ ਜੇ
ਭੁੱਲੀ ਮੈ ਕੁਝ  ਨਹੀਂ ਯਾਦ ਸਾਰਾ ਕੁਝ ਏ ਮੈਨੂੰ
ਬਸ ਖੁਦਗਰਜ਼ ਬਣ ਰਹੀ ਆ ਤੇਰੇ ਲਈ
ਕਿ ਤੇਰੀ ਜਾਨ ਤਾਂ ਬਖਸ਼ੀ ਜਾਵੇ ਤੈਨੂੰ
ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ ਤਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਹਿ ਸਕਦੀ ਪਰ
ਇਹ ਮੰਨ ਲਈ ਕੇ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਵੀ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਵੀ ਹੋਵਾਂਗੀ ਠੀਕ ਹੀ ਹੋਵਾਂਗੀ
ਜੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਮੈ ਖੋ ਲਈ ਆ 
ਤਾਂ ਤੇਰੇ ਤੋ ਤੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਖੋਨ ਦੇਵਾਂਗੀ 

ਮੇਰੀ ਮਰਜ਼ੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਮੋਹ ਖਤਮ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ 
ਪਰ ਇਹ ਸਮੇ ਨੇ ਮੇਰੀ ਰੂਹ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਰਵਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਏ
ਦੁਆ ਕਰਦੀ ਆ ਤੂੰ ਖੁਸ਼ ਤੇ ਸਹੀ ਸਲਾਮਤ ਰਹੇ ..ਕਿਉਕਿ
ਤੇਰੇ ਕੋਲੋ ਦੂਰ ਹੋਕੇ  ਤੇ ਇਹ ਸਮੇਂ ਚ ਮੈ ਆਪਣਾ ਆਪ ਈ ਗਵਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਏ ....।

FOREWORD
by Sweta Samota

Some stories do not arrive to entertain.
They arrive to liberate.
The Resilient Woman Within is one such story.
In my years of working closely with women from diverse backgrounds, cultures, and life stages, I have learned one undeniable truth: many women do not lack strength. They lack permission. Permission to speak. Permission to leave. Permission to choose peace over endurance.
Ashira’s story gives that permission.
This book does not begin with drama; it begins with stillness - a mother watching her children laugh freely. That image alone tells us everything. Because freedom, once tasted, never leaves you. And safety, once experienced, becomes non-negotiable.
What follows is not an easy story to read - but it is a necessary one.
Through Ashira’s journey, we witness how emotional manipulation hides behind the language of care, how fear quietly replaces love, and how a woman’s spirit can be eroded without a single visible bruise. These are the stories society struggles to name - and therefore often ignores. This book names them with courage and honesty.
But this is not a book about suffering.
It is a book about rising.
The Resilient Woman Within is a mirror for many women who are still doubting themselves behind closed doors. It tells them gently but firmly:
Leaving is not failure.
Choosing peace is not selfish.
Rebuilding is not starting late - it is starting right.
This book deserves to be read slowly, felt deeply, and shared bravely.  Not just by women who have lived this story - but by families, friends, and communities who must learn to listen better and stand stronger.
May this book reach every woman who needs to hear this truth today:
You are not broken. You are becoming. And resilience already lives within you.

Prologue

Ashira sat beside the window, one late afternoon when the sunlight peeked gently across her bedroom like a warm embrace. Her daughter, Misha, 10 years old, sat on the floor, lost in her drawing - her fingers smudged with colour, eyes shining with quiet imagination. Her son, Azlaan, 6 years old, was playing with his favourite bright-red car across the tiles, making soft engine sounds only he understood.
Their laughter echoed softly, filling the room with a peace Ashira once believed she would never experience again.
She exhaled, a slow, grateful breath.
 This is happiness, she told herself. Not the loud, dramatic kind the world often glorifies - but the soft, steady, healing kind that grows after storms.
She watched them play, her heart full.
And then -
A single shift in the wind, a distant sound and a familiar smell - something stirred, and like a tidal wave crashing into a quiet shore, a memory pulled her backwards.
Her vision blurred.
The room faded.
And suddenly… she was no longer sitting by a window in her safe home.
She was back in the life she had fought so hard to escape.
Her mind drifted to her childhood days - those simple, unfiltered moments when life felt like an endless summer. She remembered running barefoot on warm floors, her mother’s voice calling her for meals, and the innocent dreams she carried in her little hands.
Back then, she believed the world was kind.
Back then, she believed she would grow up to build a life full of love, respect, and quiet stability.
She had no idea how dramatically life would reshape those dreams.
But those childhood days also held strength - strength she would one day draw upon, the strength that would save her.
And as the memories unfolded, gently and painfully, her story took shape.

But she knew one thing, with absolute certainty -

Ashira worked harder than anyone expected from a young girl, learning how to balance logic with creativity, and learned how to grow without forgetting her roots. She mastered tools and techniques, navigated deadlines, built friendships, and became more confident.
Yet, within her lived another fire - one that had never gone out.

And that was her greatest reward.
It was during this period that Ashira’s parents began searching for marriage proposals. They even justified their growing demands for money by insisting that they had “invested” so much in raising a doctor son. Ashira’s parents, simple and trusting, believed every word.
