There once lived a woman named Aanya, who believed that life was simple and predictable. She had dreams, ambitions, and a heart full of hope. She imagined that if she worked hard and stayed true to herself, life would reward her with a steady path and familiar joys. But, as life often does, it proved far more unpredictable. Challenges came not as gentle nudges but as storms that tested her resolve at every turn.
The first of these storms appeared quietly, almost unnoticed. An opportunity she had been preparing for slipped through her fingers. The disappointment stung, not because she had failed others, but because she had failed herself. She had believed in her abilities and had hoped that the world would recognize her efforts. But it did not. For the first time, Aanya felt the heavy weight of frustration pressing down on her spirit.
Yet, she did not give up. She took a deep breath and reminded herself that even the smallest step forward is progress. She began each morning with intention, telling herself that today she would do something meaningful, however small. Some days, it was simply completing a task she had postponed; other days, it was speaking kindly to someone she encountered, or reading a few pages of a book that inspired her. Slowly, she realized that life’s victories often come disguised as ordinary moments.
The journey was not easy. Aanya stumbled repeatedly. She faced rejection from those she trusted, projects she had poured her energy into failed to yield results, and the people around her sometimes offered criticism that felt harsh and discouraging. At first, these setbacks shook her confidence. She questioned herself endlessly, asking whether her efforts were in vain. Sleepless nights became familiar companions, and more than once, she found herself staring at the ceiling, imagining a life where the storms never came.
But it was during these quiet nights, in the silence of her thoughts, that she discovered a deeper strength within herself. She realized that setbacks were not signs of weakness but invitations to grow. They were teachers in disguise, challenging her to learn patience, humility, and resilience. She began to see failure not as an end but as feedback—a way for life to guide her toward better understanding of herself and her purpose.
Aanya also learned the importance of perspective. She noticed small joys she had previously overlooked: the laughter of a child playing nearby, the kindness of a stranger, the soft glow of sunrise painting the sky. These moments reminded her that the world was not entirely harsh and unyielding. Even when life seemed unrelenting, beauty persisted in subtle forms, waiting to be noticed. She learned to savor these fragments of light, using them to fuel her spirit on days that felt heavy with darkness.
Her growth was gradual. She began experimenting with new skills, exploring interests she had neglected in the past, and taking calculated risks. Each success, however minor, felt monumental. A completed project, a thoughtful conversation, a personal breakthrough—each of these small triumphs built a foundation upon which she could stand taller, think clearer, and act bolder. Aanya discovered that resilience is not instantaneous; it is cultivated day by day, moment by moment, choice by choice.
Along the way, she also discovered the power of helping others. She found joy in listening to someone else’s struggles and offering encouragement, even when she felt unsure of herself. She realized that by guiding others, she was also guiding herself, learning empathy, patience, and the satisfaction of contributing positively to the world. Each act of kindness, each shared insight, became a brick in the foundation of her own strength.
Aanya’s journey was not without loneliness. At times, the weight of her challenges felt too heavy to bear alone. She longed for someone to share her victories and setbacks with, someone who understood her journey fully. Yet, she found companionship in unexpected places: the mentor who offered guidance without judgment, the friend who listened without offering unsolicited advice, and even in strangers whose small acts of consideration reminded her that humanity is generous and kind. These connections, though fleeting at times, reminded her that she was never truly alone.
Over the years, Aanya’s persistence began to bear fruit. Her work, once overlooked, started receiving recognition. People began noticing her dedication and insights. She was invited to speak in forums, workshops, and gatherings, sharing her story of perseverance. With each opportunity, she felt a deeper sense of purpose. She realized that her struggles, rather than defining her limitations, were shaping her ability to inspire others. Her journey became a beacon for those navigating their own storms, a living testament to the power of endurance and hope.
Through it all, Aanya carried with her important lessons: that life’s hardships are not punishments but guides; that courage is not the absence of fear but the ability to act despite it; and that the greatest victories are often born from the smallest steps taken consistently over time. She internalized the wisdom of those who had faced adversity before her. Maya Angelou’s words resonated deeply: “YOU MAY ENCOUNTER MANY DEFEATS, BUT YOU MUST NOT BE DEFEATED.” Each time she faltered, she reminded herself of this truth, letting it guide her toward action rather than resignation.
The transformation was not sudden. It did not happen overnight. Rather, it was the culmination of years of steady growth, patience, reflection, and effort. Aanya became someone who could navigate life’s challenges with grace, inspire others through her words and actions, and embrace each day with a sense of purpose and gratitude. She learned to celebrate not just her victories but her resilience, her courage, and the unwavering belief that she could face whatever life presented.
Her story, though filled with ordinary moments, became extraordinary because of the lens through which she lived it. She learned that heroism is not reserved for the famous or the powerful—it is found in the quiet, consistent acts of courage, kindness, and determination that define our daily lives. She understood that the essence of a fulfilled life is not the absence of struggle but the mastery of perseverance.
Eventually, Aanya’s journey culminated in a life rich with meaning. She was recognized not only for her achievements but also for her ability to inspire, guide, and uplift others. Her story reminded those who heard it that adversity is not a dead end but a beginning, that failure is not the opposite of success but part of the journey toward it, and that resilience is a choice accessible to anyone willing to embrace it.
And in the quiet moments of reflection, Aanya understood the ultimate truth of her journey: that the unbroken spirit is not born from comfort or ease but forged in the fires of challenge, shaped by perseverance, and illuminated by hope. Her life, though imperfect and often tested, was a testament to the transformative power of persistence, courage, and unwavering faith in oneself.
The moral of Aanya’s story is simple yet profound: Life will test you. It will challenge your patience, your belief, and sometimes even your hope. But if you continue, step by step, with courage in your heart, you can rise from any fall. Every struggle is an opportunity, every failure a teacher, and every dawn a chance to start anew. The unbroken spirit is the one that truly wins, for it carries within itself the power to turn hardship into triumph, fear into courage, and dreams into reality.

Nila was thirty-five when life seemed to snatch everything she held dear. A painful divorce left her alone with two young sons - one eight years old, the other barely one and a half. The comforting presence of her father was gone, his gentle words replaced by an echoing emptiness. Her career as an assistant professor had been abruptly paused, and her ambitions were shelved. Her mother was bedridden, relying on Nila for every meal, every movement, every breath. Financial struggles pressed down like a mountain. Health challenges whispered doubts into her mind. Nights were the hardest. She’d tuck her sons into bed and quietly cry, wondering if she had the strength to face another sunrise. The world felt like an unending storm, and she feared she might drown in it.
Yet, amid the darkness, a tiny spark refused to die. Nila remembered the girl she once was the dreamer who believed in possibilities beyond despair. She whispered to herself: “THE ONLY WAY TO DO GREAT WORK IS TO LOVE WHAT YOU DO,” words of Steve Jobs that fueled her determination. She decided she would rise not just for herself, but for her sons, for her mother, for the life she had always imagined.
Starting from zero was terrifying. Every day demanded courage: juggling her sons’ needs, tending to her mother, paying bills, and reviving her stalled career. Rejection after rejection tested her resolve. Sleepless nights blurred into weary mornings. Some days, she questioned herself bitterly. Yet she persisted. With each small victory, Nila grew stronger and more confident. Slowly, she refined her skills as an academic writer. She discovered a talent for motivating others, turning her own struggles into lessons for the world. 
She remembered Nila Angelou’s words: “You may encounter many defeats, but you must not be defeated.” Every setback became a stepping stone. Every tear became fuel for her passion. Her sons watched her courage, learning resilience by example.
Years of relentless perseverance transformed Nila’s life. From losing everything, she built a world filled with purpose, recognition, and fulfillment. She became a motivational speaker, a life coach, and an acclaimed academic writer. She was invited as a guest of honour at seminars and conferences, inspiring countless people with her story. The little girl who once trembled at life’s storms now stood tall, a beacon of hope, courage, and resilience. J.K. Rowling’s words echoed in her journey: “Rock bottom became the solid foundation on which I rebuilt my life.”
Nila’s journey teaches us that the darkest moments can forge the strongest spirits. Loss, heartbreak, and struggle are not endings they are beginnings. She rose from zero, carrying her sons, her dreams, and her indomitable spirit. Today, Nila stands not just successful, but unstoppable a living testament that no matter the age, the pain, or the challenges, YOU CAN RISE. YOU CAN REBUILD. YOU CAN SHINE. LIFE’S STORMS DO NOT DEFINE YOU—YOUR COURAGE DOES.
And this is me, proudly declaring my journey: DR. J. SHIFA FATHIMA, a Proud Daughter, Mom of Two Sons, Assistant Professor, Academic Writer, Motivator, Public Speaker, Life Coach.

In the chilling cold of January 2021, I was counting time not in hours, but in oxygen levels—
in the rise and fall of borrowed breath.
The corridors were always too bright. White light on white walls,
as if we could bleach away what was happening inside them.
Monitors spoke in broken rhythms, ambulance rehearsed grief outside hospital gates.
I watched a son stand six feet away from the man who once taught him how to walk.
His father lay sealed in plastic—a quiet parcel of memory.
Fear stood between them thicker than blood. “I can’t,” the son said.
Not cruel. Just afraid. 
I watched a wife leave her husband, propped against a pillow of failing air.
Her bangles did not clink when she walked away.
He kept looking at the door as if love might return wearing gloves and a mask.
But the door stayed a door.
Those were days when death felt routine—Routine is the cruelest word for goodbye.
And then, one evening, after a shift that tasted of metal and antiseptic despair, 
I stepped outside for air that did not hiss through tubes.
In a city that had forgotten how to be loud.
Shops shuttered. Footpaths empty. Almost.
At the corner sat a child—
no mask, no fear, no protective gear.
He was playing with a crumpled teddy bear,
one eye missing, stuffing escaping like tired clouds.
He made engine sounds with his mouth,
sent the toy flying across cracked cement,
then caught it in a triumph of laughter.
He looked up at me—a stranger in stained scrubs—
and grinned as if I were simply another human being,
not a custodian of endings.
In his tiny hands, the torn teddy was still capable of flight.
In his unbroken smile was a rebellion against statistics.
I stood there, six feet away from everyone,
and felt something cross the distance. 
Not denial. Not forgetfulness. Hope.
Fragile as gauze. Stubborn as a pulse.
I have seen fear divide blood from blood.
I have seen love falter at the edge of infection.
But I have also seen a child teach a broken toy to soar.
And in the middle of a city gasping for air,
that small, defiant joy filled my lungs.

INTRODUCTION — Why I Am Telling This Story 

I never thought I would write about my life. I never saw myself as a writer, an author, or even someone with a story worth telling. I am just an IT graduate — someone who was supposed to be logical, practical, and good with words in code, not in feelings.
But there are so many things I cannot say out loud. Sometimes my thoughts feel too heavy, too messy, or too confusing to speak. My voice gets stuck, my words disappear, and I end up keeping everything inside. That is why I started writing — not for others, but for myself.
At first, my writing felt like a secret conversation with my own heart. I wrote about my observations, my overthinking, my quiet struggles, and the emotions I didn’t know how to express. Slowly, I realized that these thoughts — my private diary — were actually shaping a story.
This book is about that story. It is the story of my transformation — from who I was to who I am becoming. It is not perfect, not confident, and not always clear. But it is real. It carries my doubts, my fears, my growth, and my small moments of courage.
I am still learning how to speak, how to feel, and how to understand myself. I am still becoming. And through these words, I hope to understand myself better — and maybe help someone else who also feels silent, lost, or unheard.
This is my honest, emotional, and unfinished journey — written not just with my mind, but with my heart.




CHAPTER 1 — Where I Came From

I often wonder when I first started feeling different from others. Maybe it began much earlier than I remember.
I grew up in a simple world — not perfect, not terrible, just real. When I look back at my childhood, I realize that I was not the same person I am today. I was simpler, sillier, and more carefree in my own little world.
As a small girl of six or seven, I did not like going to school. The routine, the rules, the expectations — they all felt heavy for my young heart. But outside of that, I was full of energy, curiosity, and mischief. I was a bit of a tomboy — not in a loud or rebellious way, but in my own natural way.
I never liked dresses much. I preferred jeans and T-shirts, just like my brothers. I did not like long hair either; I wished I could have hair like them. To me, comfort felt more important than looking “like a girl.” I ran around, played freely, and was often called naughty — but in a playful, loving way.
As time passed, I slowly began to notice the differences between boys and girls. By the time I reached seventh or eighth grade, I started behaving more like a “proper girl,” more aware of how I was supposed to act, speak, and present myself. That was when I began to change — not suddenly, but gradually.
In school, I was actually very clever. I studied seriously, paid attention, and performed well. I had many friends, laughed a lot, and was quite talkative — almost bubbly and cheerful, the kind of girl people described as lively or “Happier.” Yet, beneath that brightness, I was always quietly observing.
I watched people closely — how they behaved, how they spoke, how they treated others. I understood more than I let on, but I rarely revealed my deeper thoughts. I spoke a lot, but I did not always show who I truly was inside.
Looking back now, I see that this was the beginning of my transformation. Even then, I was already becoming someone — shaped by my innocence, my curiosity, my observations, and my quiet sensitivity.















CHAPTER 2 The girl who began to change

As I moved beyond my childhood, something inside me slowly began to shift. I was still that lively, talkative girl on the outside, but inside, I was becoming more aware — of myself, of others, and of the world around me.
In my early school years, I had been carefree, playful, and unbothered by how people saw me. But as I grew older, especially around my teenage years, I started thinking more. I began noticing expectations — how a girl should look, how she should behave, how she should speak. Without realizing it, I started adjusting myself to fit those invisible rules.
I was still clever, still studious, still someone who paid attention in class. I worked hard in my studies and took pride in doing well. Teachers appreciated me, friends liked me, and from the outside, everything seemed fine. I laughed, joked, and spoke freely like before — that same bubbly, “chulbuli” girl people enjoyed being around.
But inside, something was different. I became more cautious with my words. I began thinking twice before speaking. I started observing even more — not just people, but my own reactions, my own feelings, my own silence. Sometimes, I wondered why I felt things so deeply when others seemed so unaffected.
There were moments when I felt misunderstood, even among my friends. I had many people around me, yet sometimes I felt alone in my thoughts. I wanted to express what I felt, but the words did not always come easily. So I kept many emotions inside, smiling on the outside while thinking endlessly within.
Slowly, the simple, carefree girl I once was began to carry more weight — more thoughts, more questions, more unspoken feelings. This was not a sudden change; it happened quietly, little by little, like a flower growing without making a sound.
Looking back now, I see that this was not the loss of my childhood self, but the beginning of my transformation — the stage where I started becoming more aware, more reflective, and more sensitive to both the world and my own heart.















CHAPTER 3 — Carefree Days

Even after childhood, I remained the same girl at heart — carefree, curious, and full of life. I didn’t think much about the future. Every moment felt like it deserved to be enjoyed. I laughed freely, I played, I observed people, and yet I carried nothing heavy from those observations. Life felt simple, happy, and limitless.
Even in school and later in college, I stayed that way. I was serious about my studies — I wanted to do well, and I expected the best from myself. But beyond that, I didn’t stress about life or the future. I studied hard, yes, because I wanted to achieve, but once class was over, I was all about living in the moment.
College life was another adventure. I stayed in the hostel, surrounded by friends, laughter, and endless conversations. I was cheerful, sometimes mischievous, always ready to make memories. I had many friends, and those days were filled with small joys — late-night talks, jokes, shared meals, and countless silly moments.
Time passed, as it always does. And slowly, I began to realize how precious those carefree moments were. Those friendships, laughter, and memories were the best times of my life. But life moved on, people changed, friends drifted, and not everyone stayed in touch. Some of those moments now exist only in my memory, but they remain vivid, warm, and unforgettable.
Looking back, I see those years as the bridge between who I was and who I was becoming — a mix of carefree joy, learning, laughter, and the small beginnings of understanding life’s impermanence.



CHAPTER 4 — Struggles and Lessons

Life isn’t always laughter and carefree days, and eventually, I began to feel that too. Even though I was cheerful, playful, and full of energy, there were moments when everything felt heavier than I wanted it to be. It wasn’t always dramatic — sometimes it was small things, small doubts, and quiet frustrations that weighed on me.
In college, I faced moments of pressure. Expectations, responsibilities, and the idea of the future began creeping into my thoughts. I wanted to do well in my studies, but I also wanted to enjoy life. Sometimes balancing the two felt impossible. I feared failure, yet I didn’t want fear to stop me from being myself.
I also realized that life wasn’t always fair. Friendships faded, people changed, and things I thought would stay forever slipped away. That was confusing, and at times, painful. I learned that people come and go, and you can’t control everything around you. But even in those quiet struggles, I discovered something important — resilience.
I learned that it’s okay to stumble, to feel unsure, and to have moments of weakness. It’s okay to laugh even when life feels heavy, and it’s okay to feel lost and still keep moving forward. Those struggles didn’t break me — they taught me who I am, and slowly, they started shaping the person I am becoming.
Looking back, I see that life’s challenges were never meant to stop me. They were meant to teach me. To help me grow, to make me wiser, and to remind me that even in hardship, I can still find joy, curiosity, and hope.

CHAPTER 5 — The Turning Point

After graduation, life felt like it was moving faster than I could catch up with. I had to take the next step — pursue my Master’s. On paper, it was the logical path. But in my heart, I wasn’t entirely ready. I wasn’t serious all the time; I was still that carefree girl who loved to laugh, make memories, and live in the moment. Yet, life demanded more than laughter.
Those Master’s years became a whirlwind of emotions. Friendships deepened, new bonds formed, some faded. Love appeared, hearts broke, and through it all, I learned that relationships — romantic or platonic — are fragile, unpredictable, and often teach you more about yourself than anyone else. Jealousy crept in too, sometimes from others, sometimes from me, blending with admiration, competitiveness, and the constant push to do better.
At the same time, there was the pressure of expectations. I had to study hard, perform well, and top the class. Parents, teachers, friends, and even my own dreams placed invisible weight on my shoulders. Some days, it felt like too much — like I was standing in a storm of responsibilities, emotions, and unanswered questions.
And yet, it was in that storm that I began to see change. I realized that I couldn’t control everything — people, circumstances, or even my own emotions. But I could choose how I responded. I started to notice my own thoughts shifting, my mindset evolving. I became more aware of what I wanted from life, from friendships, and from myself. I started thinking more seriously about my own growth, my values, and the person I wanted to become.
Those years were confusing, intense, and sometimes overwhelming. But they were also transformative. I laughed, I cried, I learned, I failed, and I grew. I discovered that personal growth isn’t a sudden moment — it is a slow, messy, beautiful process. And it was during this time, surrounded by challenges, love, jealousy, expectations, and lessons, that I began to truly step into the person I am becoming.
















CHAPTER 6 — A New Beginning

After completing my Master’s, life took a new and beautiful turn — I married the man I had always wished to be with. Even during my final semester, we were already engaged, and the thought of this next chapter filled me with excitement, joy, and a sense of destiny.
Marriage brought with it a whole new world of experiences. Suddenly, I was no longer just the carefree girl who laughed and lived in the moment. I became a wife, a partner, a person responsible for another’s happiness alongside my own. Yet, even with these responsibilities, I discovered that joy could coexist with duty. I didn’t lose myself; I evolved.
In those early years, I embraced life fully. I remembered how to laugh freely, how to enjoy little moments, and how to live as a girl who loved to explore and celebrate life. I traveled, savored food, and cherished every memory with my husband, who became not just a life partner but a friend and confidant. Together, we built a life full of laughter, adventure, and warmth.
Motherhood added another dimension to my life. With a child now, and later another ten-year-old, I discovered a depth of love I had never known. Responsibility became a new part of my identity, but it did not diminish my spirit. I learned that caring for others and caring for myself could exist in harmony.
Looking back, marriage and family became a profound turning point in my life. The carefree girl I once was did not vanish; she evolved into a woman who could balance happiness, responsibility, and growth. I became someone who could love deeply, live fully, and embrace life’s complexities — a wife, a mother, a partner, and most importantly, still myself.
These years taught me that transformation is not always about struggle or hardship. Sometimes, it comes through love, joy, and the conscious choice to step into new roles with an open heart. This was the chapter of my life when I realized that happiness, responsibility, and self-discovery could coexist — and in that realization, I truly began to understand the person I was becoming.















CHAPTER 7— Rediscovering Myself

Fourteen years had passed in what felt like a blink. Marriage, children, responsibilities — I had embraced them all with love and dedication. I was a wife, a mother, a daughter, and yet, somewhere deep inside, a quiet question began to echo: Who am I right now?
In my past, I was a studious, driven girl. I was an IT graduate, a Master’s student, a workaholic, someone who aimed high and fought for her goals. I had ambitions, dreams, and a vision of the person I wanted to become. And yet, here I was, living a happy, fulfilled life, but feeling a strange emptiness inside.
One day, something small triggered a flood of emotions. A missed opportunity, a frustrating bus ride, a moment when I felt powerless — and I found myself crying like the girl I once was, the girl who cared deeply about her own achievements. It was a flashback to my younger self, reminding me of the person I had been. And suddenly, I realized how much I had put aside for others. How much of “me” had been lost in caring for everyone else.
I questioned myself. What should I do? What have I achieved? What do I want now? I had studied hard, learned so much, and yet it felt like I had nothing of my own. I wasn’t working in the IT field. I wasn’t pursuing personal projects. I was dependent on my husband’s earnings, and for the first time, I felt small, invisible, and restless.
Social interactions only amplified these thoughts. Some people asked, casually or jokingly, “What do you do with your life?” And inside, a storm of emotions rose: confusion, guilt, frustration, and a deep longing to reclaim myself. I wanted to do something meaningful, something that belonged to me — a life that reflected my choices and my passions.
Fourteen years of my life had been dedicated to my family, my children, and my responsibilities. Every day, I cared, I nurtured, I gave — and I did it wholeheartedly. Yet, sometimes, people asked me casually, “What have you done with your life?” and I felt the sting of their words. Did I achieve nothing? Did I not matter?
For a moment, I felt small. But then I realized the truth: what I did for these 14 years mattered. Growing my children, loving my husband, supporting my family — these were achievements too. I had given myself to the ones I love, and that is no small thing.
Still, I learned something even more important: sometimes, you have to choose yourself. Self-love is not selfish; it is essential. You cannot give your best to others if you ignore yourself. You need to nurture your own dreams, your own passions, your own growth — before you can truly care for anyone else.
This was my turning point. I realized that I could love my family fully and reclaim myself. That I could be a mother, a wife, and still pursue my own ambitions. That life does not have to be only about giving; it can also be about growing. And that lesson — choosing yourself, valuing yourself, proving to yourself what you are capable of — became the next chapter of my life.
It was the beginning of rediscovering myself. Not the carefree, playful girl of childhood, and not just the loving, responsible wife and mother. But me — my ambitions, my voice, my thoughts, and my dreams — all integrated into the life I live today. This moment became the spark of a new journey: the journey of finding myself again, in my own way, with my own words, and on my own terms.





CHAPTER 8 — My Blogging Journey: Finding My Voice 

After 14 years of dedicating myself to my family, my children, and my responsibilities, I realized something essential: I had to choose myself sometimes. I had to remember who I was, what I wanted, and what I could still become. That’s when I turned to writing.
I started with a small diary — a safe place to pour my thoughts, frustrations, dreams, and reflections. I wrote honestly, without worrying about style or grammar. I wrote to myself first, to remember who I was. Slowly, those pages became a mirror, reflecting the person I had been, the person I had become, and the person I wanted to be.
And then came a turning point. I decided to share my writing with the world. It had been only 15 days, but in that short time, I had written 15 blogs about my life — my journey, my mistakes, my thoughts, and the questions I had about who I was and who I wanted to become. Writing was no longer a hobby. It had become my voice — my way of expressing the parts of me that I had ignored for so long.
Every blog reminded me of my worth, my intelligence, and my ability to reflect deeply. I wrote about my mistakes, my struggles, my joys, and my growth. Each post became a bridge between my past and my present, between the girl I once was and the woman I am becoming.
Blogging taught me patience, humility, and courage. Not everyone would read, comment, or understand — and that was okay. This was for me first. It was my therapy, my outlet, and my declaration: I exist, I have a voice, and my story matters.
Slowly, I discovered a rhythm: writing about my life, sharing my reflections, and connecting with my inner self. Blogging reminded me that reclaiming yourself is a journey, not a destination — and for me, it was the beginning of rediscovering who I truly am.
CHAPTER 9 — Looking Forward: My Journey Continues

Right now, I am a learner. A starter. I have only just begun to tell my story, to share my thoughts, my mistakes, my reflections, and my growth. I don’t know exactly what the future holds, and that’s okay. Life is unpredictable, and my journey is still unfolding, one step at a time.
This book is simple — just a small piece of my life, a glimpse into my thoughts and experiences. It is not perfect, it is not complete, but it is honest. It is my voice, my truth, and my way of saying: I exist, I have lived, I have grown, and I am still becoming.
I started writing to find myself, to reflect, and to reclaim my identity. I wrote about who I was, who I am, and who I want to become. I shared my journey not because I have all the answers, but because every small step of growth matters. Every mistake, every triumph, every reflection is part of this journey.
And so, I continue to write, to learn, and to grow. I am a beginner, and that is okay. I am a starter, and that is enough. Life is not about perfection — it is about showing up, speaking your truth, and living fully. This is my journey, my voice, and my story — a story that will continue, day by day, as I continue to become the woman I am meant to be.

I was a house that learned your weight,
The patience of a breathing gate;
My corridors held steady flame,
And every silence knew your name.

No lightning split what we had grown,
No violent wind, no overthrown;
Just subtle shifts in borrowed air,
A thinning warmth we did not share.

You did not leave in sharpened cry,
Nor wound the dark with one last why;
You lessened — gently, day by day,
Like color draining out of clay.

And in that quiet, walls withdrew,
The doors forgot what they once knew;
A hinge that opened without sound
Now rusted where your pulse was found.

Love is not always lost in fire,
Nor ended by a grand desire;
Sometimes it folds without a seam,
Unthreads itself from shared esteem.

When memory knocks on hollow air
And finds no pulse remaining there,
Love is the door we did not close—
But left to weather what it knows.

I was a house of muted air,
With careful walls and folded prayer;
A clock that marked but never moved,
A truth rehearsed, yet never proved.

No storms declared a life undone,
No choirs crowned a rising sun;
Just quiet days in narrow seam,
Half-stitched between the real and dream.

Then not with fire nor grand display
You changed the angle of the day.
You did not dazzle, burn, or blaze—
You simply stayed. And stayed. And stayed.

And in that stillness something grew,
A steadier pulse my silence knew;
A door once locked by doubt and pride
Unlatched itself from the inside.

Now love is not a fragile art,
Nor fevered plea of reckless heart;
It is the will to stand and see
What night requires of you and me.

When darkness comes to claim its due
And strips all borrowed light from view,
Love is the choice we make, and keep—
The quiet work we choose to reap.

The pursuit 

Life is a journey full of pursuits 
If you don't pursue you are considered a destitute 

A newborn baby born with a sense of vanity 
Tries to pursue a physical identity 

A toddler experiences a sense of immense joy 
When he pursues his most cherished toy

Growing up he relinquishes his desire for toys 
And pursues to find solace in the company of other boys

As an adolescent  to stand out from the rest 
He pursues academic and professional success and tries to be the best 

In his relentless drive  for success, when he realises it's too late 
He goes out in pursuit of an ideal mate

When finally he thinks everything in the universe is by his side 
Life takes him on an emotional roller coaster ride 

Tormented and Tortured by the turmoils of the external world 
He pursues to find his authentic self in the depths of his inner world

Discovering his authentic self he experiences a sense of immense freedom 
But after a few years of exploring his interior world , he experiences boredom 

So in order to fill this deep psychospiritual hole 
He transcends his seperate self sense and pursues to be one with the whole 

From womb to tomb . Life is a journey full of pursuits 
If you don't pursue you are considered a destitute

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there lived a brilliant doctor in the quiet, isolated town of Qiumena. The only orthopaedic doctor in the whole town was James, who had built a hospital in the heart of the town. In the early days, the hospital was mostly empty, as people generally travelled to the city for any major surgeries. However, the hospital gradually became crowded, and the number of patients reached its peak during the ‘Night Phantom Tragedy’. The newspapers were flooded with reports of random attacks on people. The people of the town were being attacked by a random stranger at night. The attacker was given the name of ‘The Night Phantom’. The mysterious attacker injured several people, leaving them with a broken bone or two. These people were then rushed to James’s hospital. The town had a low crime rate, which made these cases exceptionally rare. The town had a peaceful atmosphere, and never in its history had such a tragedy befallen it. The police were yet to catch the perpetrator due to a lack of evidence. The victim’s testimony mentioned that someone from behind hit them, and then they collapsed on the ground. This situation made the hospital crowded. James managed to treat all the patients who came to him. Earlier, the people incurred significant expenses for both travelling to the city and for the surgery. The townspeople were impressed by his work and considered him capable of performing major surgeries, and he was often referred to as ‘Shaman of Qiumena’.
Meanwhile, in the hospital's waiting area, people were discussing daily affairs, the night phantom, politics, and some were glued to magazines or newspapers. Suddenly, they noticed a patient being rushed into the hospital; he had a head injury, although he wasn’t looking critically injured and was conscious as well. The person who brought him there responded that he was hit by a speeding motorcycle. He was immediately taken to the operating room while his friend remained seated in the ward. People of Qiumena were quite talkative. A man named John broke the ice and asked Tim, the injured man’s friend, about the incident. Tim responded that they were together when the incident occurred. He mentioned that they were on their way to a local store when a motorcyclist, travelling at high speed, lost control and collided with his friend. The people kept discussing their lives with each other for a while. An hour later, a nurse came out and asked Tim to meet the doctor. When Tim entered the doctor’s chamber, he was met with the doctor’s silent gaze. James told Tim with regret in his eyes, “Alas! We tried our best, but we couldn’t save him. He was in critical condition when you brought him, and unfortunately, we drew the short end of the stick.” Tim stood there frozen. He couldn’t move a muscle; he felt betrayed, angry, sad and helpless - all these feelings hit him at once. As soon as James started to talk after a long pause, Tim lashed out at him, claiming that he was a fraud. He said angrily, “You are a fraud, aren’t you? As I can see with my own eyes, you can only treat the victims of the night phantom.”
James didn’t utter a single word. “I knew it! I knew it! You are a con artist!” Tim yelled in agony. Hearing all the commotion, people began to gather outside the operating room and the doctor’s cabin. Tim continued relentlessly, shouting accusations of fraud at James. People who were discussing the night phantom incidents a while ago started connecting the dots in the story. They realized that the motorcycle victim had died, even though he was in such good condition. The mob mentality quickly took over, and the crowd started screaming and hurling abuses at the doctor. The crowd felt betrayed. Tim shoved the doctor aside and emerged from the cabin, and said in a high-pitched voice to everyone, “Everything is clear now! Everything is crystal clear! We were all taken as fools! A man who was perfectly fine - in better condition than the others - has died! If a doctor can’t save someone like him, how can he possibly treat the victims of the night phantom?”
He continued by saying, “There’s always a pattern to everything. This doctor was rusting away in this isolated town because no one needed him. But as soon as the night phantom appeared, he got a chance to fill his pockets. How convenient, isn’t it?”
The crowd nodded in complete agreement.
Most of the people, being educationally backwards, agreed to whatever was said to them in the heat of the situation. Then, Tim, consumed by anger, declared in an instant, “Death to the scammer! Death to the collaborator of the night phantom! Death to the fraud doctor!
The crowd echoed his voice throughout the hospital halls. The hospital staff panicked and instinctively closed the doors of the doctor’s cabin to keep the mob from breaking in. James, surrounded by frightened hospital staff, started laughing in the midst of the chaos. The staff watched in disbelief as James was laughing nonstop like some complete lunatic. However, he suddenly stopped and extended a helping hand to a nurse who had tripped in shock due to his sudden laughter. In a calm voice, he said to her, “Deduction is the art of seeing what others ignore - in simple terms, the ability to uncover details that have been overlooked because of their incompleteness in a situation that has already occurred. The details are generally dismissed for their vague or irrelevant description, but when a link connects those details and completes the puzzle, our neurons transmit a feeling of accomplishment”. The hospital staff stared at the doctor, believing he had gone mad due to the situation at hand. The doctor continued by saying, “I am telling you this because I want you to understand the psychology behind the mob that is currently behind that door. They do not speak the language of evidence.
They feel that they’ve reached a higher level of perception and have agreed upon a common way of thinking. They will not stop until their own generic notion of justice has been achieved.” Meanwhile, a member of the hospital staff promptly contacted the authorities and alerted them regarding their situation. On the other hand, the doctor went on with what seemed like nonsense, saying, “When a collective conclusion is achieved among people, they become like mindless zombies, destroying everything in their path and infecting others with the same delusion. It’s like a distant prophecy born out of a diseased mind.”
The nurse, unable to contain herself, yelled at James, “Tell me, sir! Please tell me - are you associated with the night phantom or not?”
James replied with a peaceful smile on his face, “No matter which path you take - good or evil
- you are always met with uncertainty, which leads you to insanity or perhaps I should say, lack of belief.”
“That doesn’t answer my question, sir!” replied the nurse.
“Answering your question is irrelevant”, James said calmly, “feel free to do the deducing part on your own. Some things are better left unsaid.”
James continued in a sorrowful tone, “I’m no longer able to see the quiet, peaceful life I had always desired. Maybe it’s true indeed - The tranquillity I hold on to despises me. I am heading out now; they are after me, right? I am no longer interested in this life anyway, but I want you all to live longer lives and understand what I meant when I spouted that so-called nonsense a while ago.”
The hospital staff watched as a man with minimal attachment to life marched towards an angry crowd. After the doctor exited, the staff immediately closed the door. They could only hear the sounds of fighting and shouting, but they kept their heads down and prayed that the noises would stop quickly. After some time, when the noises stopped and the uproar died down, the police asked them to open the doors, as the crowd had been controlled and the hospital was now silent. The police then questioned the hospital staff regarding the doctor, how they perceived him and whether they knew what had caused all the ruckus. They explained to the police how a patient died during surgery, and how the crowd had collectively tied the doctor to the night phantom and deduced that he was the criminal who injured people to bring them to his hospital. During the interrogation, they informed the police about the doctor’s strange behavior - that he had left his cabin to confront the crowd instead of staying inside. It was as if innocence found its way into the will of a decaying parasite. 
Although the hospital staff couldn’t differentiate between the right interpretation and misinterpretation, their moral compass had been shaken. It was also possible that the patient who died had truly been in critical condition and had only appeared fine due to a surge of adrenaline. On the contrary, the doctor might indeed have been guilty, and the patient may have died due to the incompetence of the doctor, as he could only handle mild cases and was building his fortune through unethical means, possibly by collaborating with the night phantom. After everything was done, the authorities left, and the hospital was shut down.
